Runtime data (audit logs, number-issuing records, notifications, mail bodies, page version history, low-code business tables) keeps growing and drags down query performance, backup size and packaging size. The data-archive feature provides a policy-driven, observable, recoverable general archive engine: it moves expired data from source tables to an archive target (MySQL archive database/table in phase 1), and two-phase reconciliation guarantees that a crash at any moment leaves at most extra data in the source table — data is never lost.
This page explains how to extend the platform runtime authentication chain with a new authentication scheme (authenticator).

The unified authentication center is the authoritative data source for organizations, users, and roles (the identity directory). Data integration answers: how do integrated business systems sync this master data and its relationships (user↔org, user↔role, org↔role) to their own side, or how do they provision their user data into the auth center.
Note: this chapter introduces the feature menus that ship with the Auth Center admin console, following the actual structure of the admin sidebar and explaining what each feature is for.
This page explains how any third-party application can integrate with the lite-login lightweight login facade provided by the unified authentication center, focusing on two things:

The unified authentication center implements standard OAuth2/OIDC protocol endpoints. Whether it is the user-facing authorization code flow (browser login for business systems) or the user-less machine-to-machine flow (client_credentials), both are part of the standard OAuth2 protocol and are documented together in this chapter.

While the unified auth server centrally manages data for all connected systems (roles, menus, permissions, grants, users, organizations, and sessions), it also exposes a set of HTTP management APIs (/api/open/v1/) for each integrator: using its own machine token, an integrator can self-manage the data that belongs to it and build its own admin UI on top.
Note: Unified Authentication is not considered a built-in core framework capability. It is essentially an independent Unified Authentication Center (Auth Server) service.

This document is for platform subsystem and third-party system developers. This page covers 7 entities across API services, custom orchestration, export templates and application authorization relations. Api defines the service interfaces an application exposes; CustomSql is code-free API orchestration; the three App*Map relation tables authorize applications against models, views and orchestrations; ExportTemplate supports file export.

This page covers 8 entities across application definition, version management, page collaboration, multi-language, and menu navigation. The application (App) is the aggregate root of the low-code platform; the page (AppPage) is the core artifact produced by the designer; pages support multi-user collaboration through a check-in/check-out mechanism; the multi-language entities carry i18n text for applications and pages; TreeNode and MenuItem carry navigation.

This page has two sections: dictionary and system config (Dict, DictItem, SysConfig, Qrcode), and files and attachments (FileInfo, Attach, Compress, Resources). The three attachment entities inherit all their fields from the attachment base class Attachment (see Overview).

This page covers 7 entities across three mechanisms Notification (the subject, one notification per row) + NotificationUser (recipient status, one row per recipient) + NotificationOutbox (delivery outbox, one row per channel); their separated responsibilities support independent read states for multiple recipients and reliable per-channel delivery. Message/Notice are the earlier single-table message and notice; UserEmailAccount is the user's external mailbox configuration.

This page covers 6 entities across organizations, companies, users, administrative divisions and tenants. User is the platform account principal; Org forms the organization tree; Company carries legal-entity company information and links to organizations; Tenant/TenantSite carry multi-tenancy and site configuration. For the read-side view of organizations and users in the security contract, see Security Contract Overview.

geelato-meta is the module where the platform's business entities are centrally defined: the entities the platform itself needs to run — applications, organizations, users, roles and permissions, dictionaries, message notifications, file attachments, scheduling and integration — are all declared with the @Entity annotation in the module's cn.geelato.meta package, 54 in total. This chapter provides a field-level catalog, entity by entity, grouped by business domain; entities of other feature modules (business alerting, business exceptions, mail, etc.) are listed in the Platform Entity Index.
This page is the master index of all runtime entities in the platform they all live under the cn.geelato package and are auto-registered by the MetaManager startup scan (see Overview).
This page covers Role, Permission and 9 permission-related relation tables — 11 entities in total. All relation tables extend BaseEntity; common fields are listed in Overview.

This page covers 7 entities across scheduled tasks, ORM hooks and various logs. OrmHook + OrmHookLog form the "configuration + outbox" mechanism for pushing entity events outward; Schedule + ScheduleLog form the scheduled-tasking pair; EncodingLog records document number/serial generation; AppPageLog and PlatformExceptionLog are the page operation log and the platform error log.

The business exception center is a rule-based judging → one-instance-per-person → resolution-loop engine: business semantics like "booking acceptance stuck" or "billed beyond credit" become configurable exception rules; judging pipelines built on the framework's script engine (geelato-script) detect hits in batch or on change, and a unique exception instance is maintained per "rule × business object × participant" until resolved.
How to define exception rules, write judging pipelines, and which REST APIs are available. Overview: Business Exception.

This page summarizes the framework capabilities that ship with geelato-dyn and how to consume them. Business modules access all of them by referencing OSGi services with a zero-config `` — no addresses, accounts or secrets are copied anywhere.

geelato-dyn does not use Spring's application.yml. Its configuration is built on OSGi Config Adminproperty-placeholder defines defaults, a .cfg file under the Karaf etc/ directory overrides them by PID, and changes take effect hot.

New business modules are created by copying the scaffold geelato-dyn-template. The template mirrors the structure of real business modules: three Blueprint templates, a DDL script and a scheduled-job skeleton.
The integration unit of geelato-dyn is a Karaf featurerepo-add and installs with feature:install.
geelato-dyn-common ships a unified message dispatch capability registered as the OSGi service MessageDispatcher. Design principles:

geelato-dyn is a dynamic integration framework built on Apache Karaf 4.4.10 + OSGi. It runs independently of the geelato platform (the Spring Boot host); the two share no Maven dependency and are integrated only through embedded security contracts, direct platform-database access, and REST calls.

Welcome to the Geelato Framework! This document is designed for both human developers and AI coding assistants (e.g., Trae, Copilot). It provides a clear capability matrix, a quick lookup map, and best practices for collaborating with AI, helping you quickly locate requirements and start coding.
This page explains how to start a new Geelato-based project from scratch and keep the first integration focused on the framework foundation instead of platform-heavy extensions.

Geelato Framework provides two standard approaches to start a project. Whether you are building a new application from scratch or integrating Geelato into an existing Spring Boot project, you can choose the path that best fits your needs.

Slow multi-table queries can be served by materialized views maintained by an external engine: writes still go to the source database (MySQL), the engine incrementally syncs and materializes the query result, and once enabled, queries on the view land directly on the materialized view — with zero changes to caller queries (transparent switching).

RisingWave is the first engine adapter of the materialized view acceleration framework: PostgreSQL protocol (default port 4566), a native mysql-cdc connector that reads the MySQL binlog directly to build ingestion channels, and incrementally maintained materialized views.

PlatformWebRuntime is the runtime application shell of the Geelato web platform. It is the runnable entry that boots the shared geelato-web-platform base for business-execution scenarios.

Geelato provides a unified job scheduling center: scheduled jobs are registered as database configuration in the platform_schedule table. On application startup, enabled jobs are loaded automatically and triggered periodically by cron expressions; changes made while running take effect through hot refresh, with no restart required.

This page is for business developers and operations staff who need to configure scheduled jobs on the platform. It covers how to configure a scheduled job, how to start/stop it, and how to view execution logs and troubleshoot problems. For the positioning of the scheduling capability and deployment notes, see Scheduler Overview.
脚本执行时，引擎按场景档案注入一批预置变量。每个变量是什么、来自哪里、能做什么，本页逐一说明。
内置 kit（见内置 Kit）之外，集成方可以把自有能力开发为 kit 注入脚本：一个标注注解的 Java 类 + 一次注册。SDK 内置的 cn.geelato.script.kit.demo.DemoService 是参考模板。
实验性功能：在线调试处于实验阶段，界面与体验待完善，接口与行为可能调整，暂不建议在生产环境依赖。
脚本不能 import 任意 Java 类；要把第三方库能力提供给脚本，由宿主声明整库引入：SDK 按包扫描其中的工具类，把 interop 兼容的公共方法挂载为 $kit 顶层对象。库本身以普通 Maven 依赖进入宿主 classpath，脚本侧零声明。
kit 是脚本调用宿主能力的受控通道，built=true 的 kit 挂在 $gl 对象下。ScriptEngineBuilder.build() 默认注册六个内置 kit；消费方显式注册同名 kit 时优先消费方（见自定义 Kit）。脚本内 $gl.help() 可速查当前可见的 kit 与方法。
geelato-script is the general-purpose script execution engine SDK of Geelato Framework. Built on the GraalVM Polyglot sandbox, it provides safe script computation.
This page describes how to write platform scripts: structure, variables, the six built-in kits ($gl.*), the write channel and dry-run, error handling and best practices.

The search engine follows a port-adapter split: geelato-search-api defines the contract, geelato-search-lucene is the reference implementation. Business systems can replace it with another engine (e.g. Elasticsearch) or extend routing without changing engines.

The Geelato search engine accelerates fuzzymatch multi-number fuzzy search in MQL. A typical query — "one document's numbers are spread across multiple columns of the main table and multiple rows of child tables; hitting any number hits the document" — originally relied on the database stored function gfn_fuzzymatch, which degrades into a full table scan on large tables (measured 3s+ on 1.44M rows).

SecurityContext is the thread-level security context: it holds the current thread's user, tenant, password, and application through ThreadLocal variables, and is the single entry for reading "who is current" at runtime. This page documents the four dimensions, the judgment methods, the write boundary, and cross-thread propagation.

This page documents the three snapshot loader SPIs and the two loading helper contracts of geelato-security. Loaders are the assembly boundary from "external security data" to "immutable snapshots": the framework and platform never read the database directly — data is assembled into snapshots through these three interfaces and cached by providers (see Provider Contracts).

This page documents the security model defined by geelato-security, attribute by attribute: six core entities, four attachment relation classes, and the relation rules between them. All classes live in the cn.geelato.security package as pure data contracts (POJOs) with no source or storage details; the platform DB column mapping is covered in Platform Defaults.

geelato-security is the security contract module of the framework: it only defines the security model, read interfaces, loading mechanisms, and context contracts — it never binds to a concrete data source. Runtime consumers (authentication, org enrichment, participant resolution, data permission) program against these contracts only; where the data comes from is decided by the implementation layer and is invisible to consumers.

This page documents every default implementation of the security contracts by layer, together with the Spring assembly and the replacement paths for host projects. Contracts live in geelato-security; framework-layer defaults (snapshot providers, bridging, refresh coordination) live in geelato-core; platform-layer JDBC loaders and the unified assembly live in geelato-web-platform. All three share the package name cn.geelato.security (a split package, kept deliberately for import consistency).

This page documents the four Provider interfaces of geelato-security and the paging contract, method by method. Providers are the read boundary for security data: consumers depend on these interfaces only, never on concrete implementations; every method defines read capability only, with no storage or network details.

This page documents the three snapshot classes (OrgSnapshot/UserSnapshot/RoleSnapshot) — their index structures and immutability guarantees — plus the unified loading and refresh chain. Snapshots are produced by the loader SPI and cached behind providers; they are the foundation of the lock-free read side.
This page explains the main configuration entry of geelato-web-quickstart, the per-module property files, and the key settings of each module.

This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, the APIs for saving, querying, versioning, publishing and locking process definitions. The data model (nodes / flows / properties) is described in Workflow Orchestration; version and publish status semantics in Workflow Orchestration · Versions and Status.

This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, the APIs scoped to the current logged-in user: my pending tasks, done tasks, to-read, read, processes started by me, opinion phrases and circulation. The data scope is automatically the current user — no user parameter is needed (or accepted).

This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, all runtime APIs: process start, next-step and participant resolution, task submission and handling, instance/task queries, instance management and reminding. The behavioral semantics (when to call what, how resolution works) are described in Workflow Runtime.

This page describes the core model of geelato-workflow process design: process nodes, sequence flows, participants, process properties and node properties. The designer produces a JSON process definition; on save the workflow service converts it into standard BPMN 2.0 and deploys it to the engine. Integrators only need the business model and fields described here — no BPMN knowledge required.

geelato-workflow is an independently deployed workflow service built on the Activiti engine (7.1.0.M6), providing process definition, approval flow, circulation (to-read), attachments, notifications and process permissions. Business systems integrate via REST APIs; the service owns a dedicated workflow datasource plus a platform-database bridge.

This page describes the full lifecycle of a process instance withdraw, reject, transfer, circulate and remind. The REST APIs for each action are documented in Runtime Integration and My Process Integration.

The business alert center decouples "things people need to know" from business code: event/schedule triggering → rule matching → aggregation & suppression → template rendering → multi-channel delivery. It is a separate engine from Business Exception but interconnected — exception instance lifecycle events are the alert's only built-in event source. Module: cn.geelato:geelato-alert. The engine is off by default; enable with geelato.alert.engine.enabled=true (quickstart default ${GEELATO_ALERT_ENGINE_ENABLED:false}). The render wiring (alert-render profile) is always registered.

Rules live in platform_alert_rule (4-table set: rule / template / alert / silence): Column Description alert_code ALR-{seq} match_json Event-source match {source, events, ruleCodes} — generalized event-source design; currently only EXCEPTION is built-in (maps to platform_exception, events via framework ORM events); unknown sources hard-fail trigger_mode / cron_expression / dataset_json EVENT / SCHEDULE / BOTH; SCHEDULE defines a dataset caliber aggregate_mode INDEPENDENT (pass-through) / AGGREGATE (group), i.e. SINGLE/GROUP group_wait_seconds / group_interval_seconds / repeat_interval_minutes Group window / min re-notify interval / repeat reminder for active groups max_items / resolve_notify / daily_limit List render cap / resolve notification / daily delivery cap receiver_json / route_json Receiver selectors / channel routing {default:{channels, templateCode}}

AlertEngineScheduler (self-managed single thread) main tick serially: source scan → flush → deliver → REPEAT schedule tick independently polls SCHEDULE crons (default 30s) Event leg: AlertMatcher (event type + ruleCodes) → AlertGrouper SINGLE: straight to PENDING (flush_at=now) GROUP: append to active group (eventIds deduped) or create group (group_wait window + unique active_group_key) source_json (business data snapshot) is collected at record creation — rendering never re-queries source tables Flush: FlushScanner (PENDING→READY→render snapshot) → RepeatScanner → ResolveHandler (RESOLVE notify) Deliver: DeliverEngine (silence final check → render fallback → receiver solving → daily_limit → per-channel enqueue) Alert record state machine: PENDING → READY → SENT / PARTIAL / FAIL / SILENCED.

Template rendering is built on the framework's script engine (geelato-script): Template table platform_alert_template: templateCode + channel variants (titleScript/contentScript js); missing or disabled variants fall back to (code, default). Three context shapes: SINGLE=$source / GROUP=list+stats / SCHEDULE=dataset injection. Data access is structurally forbidden: rendering runs under the alert-render profile — frozen read-only bindings, no SQL kit or datasource wired; template scripts can only transform $ctx/$source. Per-script timeout 2s; title ≤120, content ≤32KB truncated. Render switch geelato.alert.engine.enabled (testRender is a placeholder when off); workbench-base-url (default /fms/exception-center) for deep links.

MessageTransport → POST {message-base-url}/message/enqueue (default port 8086), sender=fms-alert, buss=alert; auth headers X-System-Code + Authorization: Bearer. Split per channel from route_json (wework→weixin_work_group mapping); bizKey={recordId}:{batchNo}:{channel}, idempotency backed by message-side idempotency_key. All-channel failures retry with backoff (backoffBaseSeconds * 2^n); over maxRetry → FAIL dead letter, manual resend only (POST /api/alert/record/{id}/resend replays the snapshot without re-rendering).

AlertReceiverSolver supports the same six selector kinds as exceptions (USER/ROLE/DEPT/DEPT_ROLE/BIZ_FIELD/ORG_TREE_UP) + fallback-role-code (empty → FAIL logged); first delivery snapshots receiver_ids/names. Silence platform_alert_silence: dimension + time window; RESOLVE notifications can be exempted; match-preview rehearses matching.

Key Default Description enabled false Engine & render master switch message-base-url required when enabled geelato-message base URL message-timeout-ms 10000 enqueue timeout message-system-code / message-api-key — enqueue auth fallback-role-code — Receiver-solving fallback role tick-seconds 5 Main tick deliver-batch-size 20 Delivery batch max-retry / backoff-base-seconds 3 / 60 Retry count / backoff base schedule-tick-seconds 30 SCHEDULE poll cadence source-lookback-seconds 600 Restart lookback watermark (no missed scans) source-batch-size 200 Source scan batch

Backend fully implemented with unit tests: matching/aggregation/flush/rendering/delivery/silence/repeat/schedule/admin endpoints; rule YAML seeds (ALR-001~007) and template seed SQL ready. Event-source generalization: EXCEPTION is the only built-in source; others are design + skeleton (AlertSources.KNOWN). Front-end not yet shipped: rule builder / template studio / record pages exist as design prototypes (bea/page 12–14).
How to configure alert rules, templates and silence, and which REST APIs are available. Overview: Business Alert.

Deploy geelato-message (default port 8086) and verify the enqueue contract (see the message integration guide, appendix C); Add the geelato-alert dependency and configure: geelato.alert.engine.enabled=true geelato.alert.engine.message-base-url=http://127.0.0.1:8086 geelato.alert.engine.message-system-code=xxx geelato.alert.engine.message-api-key=xxx Enable the exception engine (geelato.exception.engine.enabled=true) to produce EXCEPTION events; Import or create alert rules and enable them.

Five elements: event-source match (match_json) → trigger (EVENT/SCHEDULE/BOTH) → aggregation (INDEPENDENT/AGGREGATE + windows) → receivers (receiver_json) → channel routing (route_json). YAML round-trip like exceptions: POST /api/alert/rule/import-yaml, GET /{id}/export-yaml; seed rules ALR-001~ALR-007. EXCEPTION-source match_json: { "source": "EXCEPTION", "events": ["OPEN", "ESCALATED"], "ruleCodes": ["EXC-BL-015"] } events matches platform_exception lifecycle event types; when ruleCodes is declared, only instances whose source rule code is in the list alert (otherwise all).

platform_alert_template: templateCode + channel variants with titleScript / contentScript (js) and sample contexts. Scripts read $ctx / $source only (no data access by construction) and produce title/content; disabled or missing variants fall back to (code, default). Debugging: POST /api/alert/template/test-render (real render; placeholder when the engine is off), GET /context-schema, GET /context-from-record/{recordId} (use a real record's snapshot as a sample).

platform_alert_silence suppresses delivery by dimension + time window (RESOLVE notifications can be exempted). POST /api/alert/silence/match-preview rehearses "which active alerts would be silenced" without persisting.

note Endpoints are declared via @ApiRestController; with the /api prefix the real path carries /api. Rules /api/alert/rule Endpoint Description POST /pageQuery, GET /{id}, POST /save Page / detail / save POST /{id}/enable, /disable, /delete Enable/disable/delete POST /import-yaml, GET /{id}/export-yaml YAML round-trip POST /{id}/trial-run Trial run GET /{id}/records Rule alert records Templates /api/alert/template: POST /pageQuery, GET /{code}, POST /save, POST /{code}/delete, POST /test-render, GET /context-schema, GET /context-from-record/{recordId} Records /api/alert/record: POST /pageQuery, GET /{id}, GET /{id}/messages (message-side messages), POST /{id}/resend (snapshot resend), POST /{id}/silence-from Silence /api/alert/silence: POST /pageQuery, POST /save, POST /{id}/revoke, POST /match-preview Admin /api/alert: POST /alert/admin/trigger, POST /alert/admin/flush, GET /alert/admin/stats, POST /alert/event (event ingestion)

No missed scans on restart: source scans look back source-lookback-seconds (default 600s). Delivery troubleshooting: record status PARTIAL/FAIL plus message-side messages (GET /{id}/messages); FAIL dead letters resend via resend (no re-render). Stuck groups: GROUP groups are bound by group_wait_seconds and group_interval_seconds; flush manually with POST /alert/admin/flush. Daily cap: deliveries over daily_limit are dropped with a log and recover in the next window.

Static reference for all REST endpoints under the platform package cn.geelato.web.platform.srv — 90 controllers and 500+ endpoints. This chapter is organized by business domain: one page per domain (srv sub-package), sections per controller, and one table per endpoint covering URL, parameters, and result. The information is extracted directly from source signatures and kept in sync with the code.

Controllers annotated with the custom @ApiRestController family (including @DesignTimeApiRestController and @ApiRuntimeRestController) automatically get an /api prefix at runtime: actual URL = /api + class-level path + method-level path. A few controllers using the plain @Controller / @RestController annotations do not get the /api prefix (e.g. the /package endpoints of app packaging); always follow the URL shown on each endpoint. The prefix is registered by ApiPrefixAutoConfiguration and only applies to the quickstart host.

appId: application identifier; accepts appId / AppId / App-Id. tenantCode: tenant code; accepts tenantCode / TenantCode / Tenant-Code, falling back to the current session when absent. These apply to every endpoint and are not repeated in per-endpoint parameter tables.

Shared by list/paged endpoints: pageNum: page number, aliases current and page. When absent in a GET request it defaults to -1, meaning no pagination (full result); when absent in a POST body it defaults to 1; values < 1 fail hard. pageSize: page size, alias limit. When absent in a GET request it defaults to -1 (full result); when absent in a POST body it defaults to 10; values are clamped to [1, 1000]. orderBy: sorting, alias order; default seq_no ASC,update_at DESC.

Query or body keys support the fieldName|operator syntax (e.g. name|like); only keys matching existing entity fields are kept. The default operator is eq; bt (between, two values), nil (is null) and others are supported.

Controllers marked with ⚙ are design-time endpoints (@DesignTimeApiRestController), mainly consumed by the designer / IDE; the rest are runtime endpoints (@ApiRestController). Controllers annotated with @ApiRuntimeRestController whose category is platform-design are also marked as design-time.

Field ApiResult ApiPagedResult ApiMetaResult Description code ✓ ✓ ✓ Result code, 200 for success msg ✓ ✓ ✓ Message status ✓ ✓ ✓ Status data ✓ ✓ ✓ Data cache ✓ ✓ ✓ Cache flag total / page / size / dataSize — ✓ — Total / page / size / row count of current page meta — ✓ ✓ Metadata ApiMultiPagedResult returns data as Map<String, PageData>, where PageData contains total / page / size / dataSize / data / meta, used when one request pages multiple entities.

This static reference is extracted directly from source and serves as the supplementary entry for browsing by controller. MQL is not an external standard contract but the platform-internal universal metadata access protocol; see MQL.
1 controller with 1 endpoint in total. Controllers marked with ⚙ are design-time APIs.
AI Q&A: sends the question to a large language model and streams the answer back over SSE.

Item Content URL POST /api/ai/ask Params body: Map<String,String>, key content, the question text. Returns Writes directly to the response stream (no JSON body): SSE streaming response (content-type text/event-stream), pushing the AI answer chunk by chunk; return type is SseEmitter (30-minute timeout).
1 controller with 2 endpoints in total. Controllers marked with ⚙ are design-time APIs.

Login-popup announcement mechanism: announcements are markdown files in a configured directory (geelato.announcement.dir, usually maintained by scheduled git pulls) and the endpoint returns the latest one by date; the read state is kept by the frontend in localStorage ({announcementId}_{userId}_read) and the server stores nothing.

Item Content URL GET /api/announcement/current Params None Returns ApiResult<AnnouncementInfo>: data is the latest announcement (id random-number primary key, i.e. the first segment of the file name; title title, the middle segment; date announcement date formatted as yyyy-MM-dd; fileName announcement file name; content markdown source rendered by the frontend); data is null when there is no announcement. Each call lightly rescans the directory, so announcements pulled by git take effect without a restart.

Item Content URL POST /api/announcement/refresh Params None Returns ApiResult<AnnouncementInfo>: data is the refreshed latest announcement (same structure as above, null when none); clears the cache and rescans the directory immediately. Intended for ops scripts after a git pull (Authorization: SystemToken <fixed key>, configured at geelato.security.system-token.token, overridable via the GEELATO_SYSTEM_TOKEN environment variable).
1 controller with 1 endpoint in total. All endpoints in this domain are design-time APIs.
Arco form component support: returns select option data for a registered enum code.

Item Content URL GET /api/arco/sod/{code} Params code: path, string, enum code (registered in ArcoEnum, case-insensitive). Returns ApiResult<List<SelectOptionData>>: data is the select option list (label/value, etc.); an empty list is returned when the code does not exist or the enum is invalid.
2 controllers with 18 endpoints in total. Controllers marked with ⚙ are design-time APIs.

Core of login and current-user self-service operations: account/anonymous login, identity and tenant switching, delegate-on-behalf sessions, current user info and menus, avatar and profile maintenance, password reset and recovery, account verification and binding.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/login Params username: body, string, required, login name (max 64). password: body, string, required, login password (max 128). tenant: body, string, optional, tenant code. suffix: body, string, optional, login-name suffix (e.g. @tenant; when non-empty it takes precedence over tenant for tenant resolution). org: body, string, optional, reserved field (not used by the current login logic). Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: on success returns a full identity isomorphic to Current user info (basic user info, org/company info, org list orgs, tenant list tenants, role strings roleCodes/roleIds) plus a token; the JWT payload fields are id, loginName, passWord, orgId, tenantCode. When the login name exists under multiple tenants, the call fails with a multi-tenant exception code and data.tenants carries the candidate tenant list for you to choose from.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/login/anonymous Params username: body, string, required, anonymous account login name. password: body, string, required, must equal the platform-configured anonymous fixed password. Other fields are the same as login. Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: same as login; the JWT payload additionally carries an anonymous field. The platform anonymous-login option must be enabled, otherwise the call fails. The anonymous channel is decided by the global context: the environment variable GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED (true/false) takes precedence when set; otherwise it follows the security level (on when level < 10, off when level ≥ 10). See Global Context.

Item Content URL GET /api/user/switchIdentity Params org: query, string, optional, target org ID. tenant: query, string, optional, target tenant code. Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: re-issues the JWT with the new orgId/tenantCode and returns the full login result (same structure as Current user info); if the given org or tenant is not among your options, it falls back to the user's default value. Delegate mode ends with the old credential when the token is re-issued.

Item Content URL GET /api/user/delegators Params None Returns ApiResult<List<UserDelegateMap>>: list of principals you (as the delegate) may act on behalf of (records with scope=mentor_assist, enabled and valid, deduplicated by principal ID), for the top-right delegate switcher. Fails when you are not logged in.

Item Content URL GET /api/user/delegateAs Params targetUserId: query, string, target principal user ID. Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: does not re-issue any token; it only writes a server-side "credential → delegation target" session mapping and returns the target principal's basic user info (whitelist DTO, credential fields excluded). Checks: a valid delegation relationship must exist; nested delegation and delegating to yourself are forbidden.

Item Content URL GET /api/user/exitDelegate Params None Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty; removes the delegation session for the current credential and clears the delegate-mode context cache, restoring your own identity.

Item Content URL GET|POST /api/user/info Params None Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: full current-user info, including token, org list orgs, tenant list tenants, role info roles/roleCodes/roleIds, and delegateUserId/delegateUserName when in delegate mode.
Item Content URL POST /api/user/logout Params None Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/user/avatar/{userId} Params userId: path, string, target user ID. file: form, multipart file, avatar file (parameter name file). Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/user/update/{userId} Params userId: path, string, target user ID. name: body, string, optional, name (max 64). enName: body, string, optional, English name (max 64). mobilePrefix: body, string, optional, mobile prefix (max 16). mobilePhone: body, string, optional, mobile number (max 16). telephone: body, string, optional, telephone (max 64). email: body, string, optional, email (max 128). nationCode, provinceCode, cityCode: body, string, optional, nation/province/city codes (max 32). address: body, string, optional, address (max 255). description: body, string, optional, description (max 255). Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/user/menu Params flag: body, string, optional, filter flag passed through to the menu query. appId: body, string, optional, application ID. tenantCode: body, string, optional, tenant code; when non-empty it must match your current tenant, otherwise validation fails. Returns ApiResult<List<Map<String,Object>>>: menu nodes authorized for the current user (queried by app/tenant). Returns an empty list when appId or the tenant code is missing.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/user/resetPassword Params passwordLength: query, int, optional, length of the new password; default 8, max 32. Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the newly generated random plaintext password.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/forgetValid Params validType: body, string, required, verification type (1 mobile, 2 email, 3 password). validBox: body, string, required, mobile number or email. prefix: body, string, required when validType is 1, mobile prefix. Returns ApiResult<User>: data contains only the id of the matched user (for the subsequent recovery steps); throws a business exception when no unique user matches.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/forget Params action: body, string, required, business action identifier (used for auth-code validation). validType: body, string, required, verification type (1 mobile, 2 email). validBox: body, string, required, mobile number or email. authCode: body, string, required, auth code. userId: body, string, required, user ID. password: body, string, required, new password. prefix: body, string, optional, mobile prefix. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty; resets the user's password after the auth code is validated.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/validate Params validType: body, string, required, verification type (1 mobile, 2 email, 3 password). userId: body, string, required, user ID. authCode: body, string, required, auth code; used as the login password when validType is 3. prefix: body, string, optional, mobile prefix. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty; validates the auth code or password according to the verification type, and throws a business exception on failure.

Item Content URL POST /api/user/bindAccount Params validType: body, string, required, binding type (1 mobile, 2 email, 3 password). userId: body, string, required, user ID. authCode: body, string, required, auth code. validBox: body, string, required, mobile number/email/new password. prefix: body, string, optional, mobile prefix. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty; when validType is 3 the validBox is encrypted and saved as the new login password; when it is 1/2 the mobile number or email is bound after the auth code is validated.
OAuth2 integration login: exchanges an authorization code for tokens at the OAuth server, fetches user info to complete the login on this platform, and refreshes access tokens.

Item Content URL POST /api/oauth2/login Params code: query, string, OAuth2 authorization code. Returns ApiResult<LoginResult>: exchanges the code for tokens using the platform-configured OAuth server URL and client credentials, fetches user info, stores the access/refresh token mapping, and assembles the full login result from the platform's stored user record matched by user ID (token is the OAuth access token). Fails when token exchange or user-info fetching fails, when the SSO data lacks a user ID, or when the matching platform account does not exist.

Item Content URL POST /api/oauth2/refreshToken Params oldToken: query, string, old access token. Returns ApiResult<HashMap<String,String>>: data contains access_token and refresh_token; looks up the refresh token by the old token, exchanges it at the OAuth server for new tokens, and updates the token mapping on success. Fails when no refresh token is found or the exchange fails.

Health status query and manual refresh for auxiliary suites, admin-only.

Item Content URL GET /api/system/monitor/auxiliary-suites/health Params None Returns ApiResult<AuxiliarySuiteHealthSummary>: auxiliary suite health summary (checked time, poll interval in seconds, suite count with healthy/abnormal/unknown counts, hasFailure flag, last error, per-suite snapshot list suites); fails for non-admin users.

Platform system configuration query (grouped by platform/tenant/app) and refresh of a given config key.

State workflow definition update notification.

Platform initialization self-inspection: configuration properties, datasources, and SQL scripts.

File and configuration upload: attachment upload, config object/JSON persistence, and entity record export as config files.

Item Content URL POST /api/upload/file Params file: form-data file field, required, uploaded file. serviceType: query/form-data, string, file server type. tableType: query/form-data, string, table type (determines the default save path and the attachment source). root: query/form-data, string, optional, custom file root directory; the save path is built from it when provided. isRename: query/form-data, boolean, optional, rename the file, defaults to true. objectId: query/form-data, string, optional, business object ID. formIds: query/form-data, string, optional, related form IDs. genre: query/form-data, string, optional, file genre. batchNo: query/form-data, string, optional, batch number. invalidTime: query/form-data, string, optional, invalidation time (datetime format). validDuration: query/form-data, integer, optional, validity duration in seconds; overrides invalidTime when set. isThumbnail: query/form-data, boolean, optional, generate a thumbnail. onlyThumb: query/form-data, boolean, optional, generate the thumbnail only. dimension: query/form-data, string, optional, thumbnail dimension. thumbScale: query/form-data, string, optional, thumbnail scale. appId: query/form-data, string, optional, app ID, defaults to the current app. tenantCode: query/form-data, string, optional, tenant code, defaults to the current tenant. Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: the uploaded attachment info (source set to tableType, storageType set to serviceType).

Item Content URL POST /api/upload/object Params params: body, Map<String,Object>, required, config content written to the file (Java-serialized object). fileName: query/form-data, string, required, file name; the .config suffix is appended automatically when missing. catalog: query/form-data, string, optional, subdirectory under the config root. Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the stored file name; an existing file is first backed up by renaming, and overwritten when the backup rename fails.

Item Content URL POST /api/upload/json Params JsonData: body, string, required, JSON text (raw request body). fileName: query/form-data, string, required, file name; the .config suffix is appended automatically when missing. catalog: query/form-data, string, optional, subdirectory under the config root. Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the stored file name; existing files are handled the same way as uploadObject.

Item Content URL POST /api/upload/model/{entityName}/{id} Params entityName: path, string, entity (table) name. id: path, string, record ID. fileName: query/form-data, string, required, export config file name; multiple names can be comma-separated. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: queries the record's field values (excluding entity default columns and fields listed in unSaveConfig) and writes each as a .config file; data is empty.
3 controllers with 17 endpoints in total. Controllers marked with ⚙ are design-time APIs.
Export file list query, plus file generation (Excel/Word etc.) either by template or by column metadata, with download and PDF conversion support.

Item Content URL POST /api/export/file/list Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult: data is the paged attachment list (Attach entity, records of the platform_attach table).

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/export/file/{dataType}/{templateId} Params dataType: path, string, data parsing type, mql or data; with data the payload is parsed from the gql JSON body, other values fail. templateId: path, string, export template ID. index: query, string, optional, template index (1-19), defaults to 1. fileName: query, string, optional, export file name (defaults to templateName_timestamp, template extension appended automatically). markText: query, string, optional, watermark text. markKey: query, string, optional, watermark style config key (style resolved from system config). readonly: query, boolean, whether the exported file is read-only. isDownload: query, boolean, when true the file is written to the response as a download. isPdf: query, boolean, when true the file is converted to PDF and the original export file is deleted. body (with dataType=data): gql JSON containing valueMapList (List<Map>, multiple rows) and valueMap (Map, a single record). Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the attachment record of the exported file; with isDownload=true the response is written directly to the stream (no JSON body, content-type and file name taken from the attachment); with isPdf=true data is the PDF attachment record.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/export/file/column/meta/list Params appId: query, string, optional, app ID, defaults to the appId header. fileName: query, string, optional, export file name (defaults to exportExcelByColumnMeta_timestamp.xlsx). markText: query, string, optional, watermark text. markKey: query, string, optional, watermark style config key. readonly: query, boolean, whether the exported file is read-only. isDownload: query, boolean, when true the file is written to the response as a download. isPdf: query, boolean, when true the file is converted to PDF and the original export file is deleted. body: gql JSON containing valueMapList (List<Map>, multiple rows), valueMap (Map, a single record), column (List<ExportColumn>, table header column definition, required) and meta (List<PlaceholderMeta>, placeholder data definition, required). Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the attachment record of the exported file; with isDownload=true the response is written directly to the stream (no JSON body, content-type and file name taken from the attachment); with isPdf=true data is the PDF attachment record.

Item Content URL GET /api/export/file/toPdf/{id} Params id: path, string, attachment ID of the Excel export file. Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the attachment ID of the converted PDF; fails when the file or its attachment record is missing or conversion fails.
documents.s: toPdf Convert export file to PDF

documents.t: Export/import template (ExportTemplate) management: paged and list queries, copy, save, delete, template file generation and template content lookup.
Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/pageQuery Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult: data is the paged template list (ExportTemplate).

Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/query Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiResult<List<ExportTemplate>>: data is the template list (ordered by the sort parameter).
Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/get/{id} Params id: path, string, template ID. Returns ApiResult<ExportTemplate>: data is the template detail.

Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/copy/{id} Params id: path, string, ID of the template to copy. Returns ApiResult<ExportTemplate>: data is the new template record (title suffixed with - 副本 (copy), new ID generated).

Item Content URL DELETE /api/export/template/isDelete/{id} Params id: path, string, template ID; fails when the template does not exist. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: sets enableStatus to disabled and deletes the record; data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/export/template/generateFile/{id} Params id: path, string, template ID. fileType: body, string, file type to generate, template (import template file) or meta (metadata/rule file), multiple values comma-separated. Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the generated attachment record; fails when params are missing or the template does not exist.

Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/index/{id} Params id: path, string, template ID. Returns ApiResult<Map<Integer,Object>>: data maps template index (1-9) to template file name, non-empty templates only; returns an empty map when the template does not exist.

Item Content URL GET /api/export/template/base64/{id}/{index} Params id: path, string, template ID. index: path, string, template index (1-19). Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the template content string for that index (Base64Helper JSON with the file name and base64 file content); fails when the template does not exist, throws when the index is out of range.
Excel data import: import template lookup, import from attachment/uploaded file, and complex template parsing.
Item Content URL GET /api/import/template/{templateId} Params templateId: path, string, import template ID. Returns ApiResult<ExportTemplate>: data is the import template record.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/import/attach/{importType}/{templateId}/{attachId} Params importType: path, string, import type: part partial import / all full import (interrupt and roll back on error). templateId: path, string, import template ID. attachId: path, string, attachment ID of the business data Excel file. index: query, string, optional, template index. Returns ApiResult: on success data is the import transaction UUID (string) and msg the import count summary; on data validation failure data is the error report file attachment (Attachment), see the error file for details.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/import/file/{importType}/{templateId} Params importType: path, string, import type: part partial import / all full import (interrupt and roll back on error). templateId: path, string, import template ID. index: query, string, optional, template index. body: form-data file field file, the uploaded business data Excel (.xls/.xlsx). Returns ApiResult: on success data is the import transaction UUID (string) and msg the import count summary; on data validation failure data is the error report file attachment (Attachment), see the error file for details.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/import/complex/{importType}/{templateId}/{attachId} Params importType: path, string, import type (reserved parameter, kept for signature compatibility). templateId: path, string, import template ID. attachId: path, string, attachment ID of the business data Excel file. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data is the flattened parsed JSON (not persisted): fixed cell fields and list regions are flattened on the same level, list keys are the list fieldName with row arrays as values.

Attachment record management: copy, quote, query, update, replace, existence validation, storage migration, deletion and Excel-to-PDF conversion.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/copy/{id} Params id: path, string, ID of the attachment to copy. genre: body, string, optional, business genre tag (written to the new attachment's genre). name: body, string, optional, new file name (original extension appended automatically). invalidTime: body, string, optional, invalidation time (DATETIME format). Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the new attachment record created by the copy; fails when the attachment or its file is missing.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/quote/{id} Params id: path, string, ID of the attachment to quote. genre: body, string, optional, business genre tag. name: body, string, optional, new file name (original extension appended automatically). invalidTime: body, string, optional, invalidation time (DATETIME format). Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the new quote attachment record (file path shared with the source attachment, pid pointing to it); fails when the source attachment is missing.
Item Content URL GET /api/attach/get/{id} Params id: path, string, attachment ID. Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the attachment record.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/image/{id} Params id: path, string, parent attachment ID (pid). Returns ApiResult<List<Attachment>>: data is the list of attachments under that pid (e.g. thumbnails of an image).

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/update/{id} Params id: path, string, attachment ID. body: Map<String,Object>, attachment field name to value mapping (populated onto Attachment fields). Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the updated attachment record.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/replace/{sourceId}/{targetId} Params sourceId: path, string, source attachment ID. targetId: path, string, target attachment ID. body: Map<String,Object>, field updates for the target attachment. Returns ApiResult<Attachment>: data is the target attachment record (fields updated, source pid inherited and tagged Replace, its ID replaced with the source attachment ID; the source record is kept under a new ID); fails when the source or target attachment is missing.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/valid Params attachmentIds: body, string, comma-separated attachment IDs. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Boolean>>: data maps attachment ID to whether its file exists (boolean); fails when the IDs are empty or the attachments do not exist.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/storage/{type} Params type: path, string, target storage type: local local storage / aliyun Alibaba Cloud OSS. attachmentIds: body, string, comma-separated attachment IDs. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,String>>: data maps attachment ID to a processing message, containing only problem items (file missing, migration failed, storage type unchanged); fails when the IDs are empty or the attachments do not exist.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/list Params body: Map<String,Object>, query conditions and paging params (e.g. ids, pids, batchNo, storageType; paging keys current/pageSize/order, see FileHandler.getAttachments). Returns ApiResult<List<Attachment>>: data is the matching attachment list.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/pageQuery Params current: body, long, page number, defaults to 1. pageSize: body, int, page size, defaults to 10. order: body, string, sort (field|direction, | replaced by a space, defaults to create_at desc). remaining keys: body, used as query conditions. Returns ApiPagedResult: data is DataItems<Attachment> (items attachment array + total count), with paging info on the outer envelope.

Item Content URL GET /api/attach/column/{type} Params type: path, string, column type: source, storageType (enum values returned directly), type, resolution (distinct values queried from the table). Returns ApiResult<List<String>>: data is the list of available values for that column.

Item Content URL DELETE /api/attach/remove/{id} Params id: path, string, attachment ID. isRemoved: query, boolean, whether to physically delete from the database (true deletes, false marks as deleted). deleteOss: query, boolean, optional, defaults to false, whether to also delete the OSS object. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/attach/remove/{type} Params type: path, string, deletion scope; with batchNo the batch numbers are resolved from the attachment IDs and every attachment of the same batches is deleted. isRemoved: query, boolean, whether to physically delete from the database. attachmentIds: body, string, comma-separated attachment IDs. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: deletes the attachments one by one; data is empty; fails when the IDs are empty.

Item Content URL GET /api/attach/toPdf/{id} Params id: path, string, attachment ID; only .xlsx/.xls files are supported. Returns ApiResult<String>: data is the attachment ID of the converted PDF; fails when the attachment or file is missing, the format is unsupported, or conversion fails.
Attachment packaging (zip, split into packages) and compressed-package attachment ID resolution, supporting compression by attachment ID, batch number and thumbnail.

Item Content URL POST /api/pack/by/fileIds Params body: CompressRequestBody structure: attachmentIds (string, comma-separated attachment IDs), batchNos (string, comma-separated batch numbers), fileName (string, archive file name), serviceType (string, storage service type), genre (string, business genre tag), validDuration (int, validity duration in seconds, invalidation time derived automatically), invalidTime (date, invalidation time), amount (int, max files per archive, system default when omitted), gql (string, gql statement). Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data contains attachmentIds (list of archive attachment IDs) and batchNo (batch number); fails when compression fails.

Item Content URL POST /api/pack/by/batch Params body: same CompressRequestBody structure as by/fileIds. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data contains attachmentIds (list of archive attachment IDs) and batchNo (batch number); fails when compression fails.

Item Content URL POST /api/pack/by/{type}/{column} Params type: path, string, pack to compress / simple to resolve attachment IDs only. column: path, string, id by attachment ID / batchNo resolves batch numbers from the IDs and expands to all attachments of the same batches. attachmentIds: body, string, comma-separated attachment IDs. Returns ApiResult<List<String>>: data is the attachment ID list (for pack, the archive attachment IDs, file name taken from the current timestamp); throws when attachments are missing or compression fails.

Item Content URL POST /api/pack/by/thumb Params body: same CompressRequestBody structure as by/fileIds; attachmentIds is resolved by pid into their child attachment (thumbnail) IDs before compressing. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data contains attachmentIds (list of archive attachment IDs) and batchNo (batch number); fails when compression fails.
OSS (Alibaba Cloud object storage) management: bucket statistics and dual-side (database vs cloud) file verification as an async task. Registered only when the OSS component is enabled.

Item Content URL GET /api/oss/stats Params None Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data is the OSS bucket statistics (storage usage, file count, etc.); fails when the statistics cannot be fetched.

Item Content URL POST /api/oss/start-verify Params None Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data contains taskId; verification runs asynchronously, task results are kept for 30 minutes, poll verify-status for progress.

Item Content URL GET /api/oss/verify-status/{taskId} Params taskId: path, string, verify task ID. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data contains status (running/completed/failed), total, checked, existCount, missingCount, results (each item with attachId, name, objectName, type, exists, plus error when the check throws), and errorMessage on failure; fails when the task does not exist or has expired.

1 controller, 2 endpoints in total. This domain is not a design-time API; it only provides view and refresh of the in-memory rules. The rule JSON is written to Redis directly by operations (the key is determined by geelato.traffic.gray.redis-key, default geelato:gray:rules). After changing it, call /reload to take effect immediately.
Gray rule management API: loads rules from Redis into memory and lets you inspect them.
Item Content URL POST /api/gray-rules/reload Params None Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: data.count is the number of in-memory rules after reloading.
Item Content URL GET /api/gray-rules/get Params None Returns ApiResult<List<GrayRule>>: data is the list of current in-memory gray rules (GrayRule: targetType, targetValue, priority, grayTag, etc.).

2 controllers with 26 endpoints in total. Endpoints marked with ⚙ are design-time APIs. MetaController merges the former runtime and design-time controllers under the same prefix /api/meta; its runtime endpoints read the GQL query body directly from the raw request (the body is not a plain JSON map). See MQL for GQL/MQL semantics.

Metadata service under a single prefix: runtime APIs (GQL query/save/delete) and design-time APIs (entity metadata definitions, conflict diagnosis/sync between Java class sources and the online DB source, reverse code generation).

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/list, POST|GET /api/meta/list/* Params withMeta: query, boolean, optional, default true, whether to include field metadata with the data. GQL query body (read from the raw request): a single entity object or an array of entities; pagination (@p), fields (@fs), view template params (@pf) and more are expressed in GQL, see MQL. Returns ApiPagedResult: data is a list of record maps; page/size/dataSize/total are filled from the query result, and meta/cache are returned when present (declared return type is the raw ApiPagedResult<?>).

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/multiList Params withMeta: query, boolean, optional, default true, whether to include field metadata with the data. GQL query body (read from the raw request): an array of entities, each with its own pagination and filters. Returns ApiMultiPagedResult: data is a Map<entityName, PageData>; each PageData holds that entity's data/total/page/size/dataSize/meta; the top-level cache flag is returned when present.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/save/{biz} Params biz: path, string, required, business entity name. GQL save body (read from the raw request). Returns ApiMetaResult: data is the primary key of the saved record (string); on failure a marker such as saveFail/transactionRollback is returned.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/batchSave Params GQL batch save body (read from the raw request): multiple save commands executed one by one within a single transaction. Returns ApiMetaResult: data is the list of saved primary keys (string array); any failure rolls back the whole batch.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/multiSave Params GQL save body (read from the raw request): multi-entity save commands executed within a single transaction. Returns ApiMetaResult: data is the list of saved primary keys (string array).

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/delete/{biz}/{id} Params biz: path, string, required, business entity name. id: path, string, required, record primary key. Returns ApiResult<Integer>: number of deleted records.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/delete2/{biz} Params biz: path, string, required, business entity name. GQL delete body (read from the raw request): delete conditions are expressed in GQL. Returns ApiResult<Integer>: number of deleted records.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/tree/{biz} Params entity: query, string, required, business entity name associated with platform_tree_node (the entity must have a tree_node_id field). treeId: query, long, required, tree ID. biz: path, string, path placeholder (unused in the method body). Returns ApiResult: tree node list (children nested under children); fails with the reason when the entity is not valid.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/uniqueness Params GQL query body (read from the raw request): the check condition is expressed in GQL; @fs=id is added automatically when @fs is absent, and @p=1,10 when @p is absent. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: true when the check query total is 0 (no duplicates; declared return type is ApiResult<?>).

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/defined/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. Returns ApiMetaResult: data is all simple field metadata of the entity; fails with not found meta defined when the entity does not exist.
Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/fullDefined/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. Returns ApiMetaResult: data is the complete metadata of the entity (EntityMeta).
Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/entityNames Params None Returns ApiResult: list of all loaded entity names.
Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/entityLiteMetas Params None Returns ApiResult: list of lite entity metadata.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/conflicts Params None Returns ApiResult: data is a Map<entityName, diff details> listing entities that exist in both the Java class source and the online DB source with field-level diffs (for diagnosing duplicated entities that break CRUD SQL generation).

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/conflicts/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. Returns ApiResult: field-level diff details of the entity; an empty diff is returned when there is no conflict.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/sync/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. direction: query, string, optional, default db-to-class; currently the only supported value (any other value fails immediately). Returns ApiResult: reloads the entity's online DB definition, refreshes the main cache (db-to-class direction) and returns the latest diff verification result.

Item Content URL POST|GET /api/meta/codegen/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. packageName: query, string, optional, package of the generated class, default cn.geelato.meta. Returns ApiResult<Map<String,Object>>: className, fileName, packageName, source (.java source text annotated with @Entity/@Col/@Title/@Id; preview only — nothing is persisted to the DB or written to disk).

Item Content URL GET /api/meta/codegen/{entity}/download Params entity: path, string, required, entity name. packageName: query, string, optional, default cn.geelato.meta. Returns Writes directly to the response stream (no JSON body): streams the generated {ClassName}.java source file as text/plain; returns 404 when the entity metadata does not exist.
Design-time DDL operations: recreate database tables and views per entity/app, validate view SQL, refresh the online metadata cache.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/table/{entity} Params entity: path, string, required, entity name (determines the database table to operate on). Returns ApiMetaResult: recreates or creates the database table by entity name (requires switching the database); data is empty on success, error message on failure.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/tables/{appId} Params appId: path, string, required, app ID (determines the scope; tenant code comes from the current session). Returns ApiMetaResult: data is a Map<entityName, result> (true created/updated, false failed, "ignore" skipped for non-manual source types); data is empty when the app has no enabled tables; on error data holds the partial results plus an error message.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/views/{appId} Params appId: path, string, required, app ID (tenant code comes from the current session). Returns ApiMetaResult: data is a Map<viewName, result> (true created/updated; explanatory text for virtual/materialized views or missing related connection/table); data is empty when the app has no views.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/viewOne/{id} Params id: path, string, required, view ID. Returns ApiMetaResult: creates or updates a single view (virtual and materialized views are rejected); data is empty on success.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/view/{view} Params view: path, string, required, view name. connectId: body, string, required, database connection ID. sql: body, string, required, view SQL (body is a JSON object with connectId and sql). Returns ApiMetaResult: validates the SQL first, then creates/updates the view (requires switching the database); data is empty on success.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/view/valid/{connectId} Params connectId: path, string, required, database connection ID. sql: body, string, required, view SQL to validate (body is a JSON object, sql field is read). Returns ApiMetaResult<Boolean>: whether the view SQL is valid (on validation exceptions the success structure is still returned with data of false plus the error message).

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/view/valid/{connectId}/{entityName} Params connectId: path, string, required, database connection ID. entityName: path, string, required, entity name. Returns ApiMetaResult<Map<String,String>>: data is a Map<viewName, result> ("true" valid, "false" invalid or the exception message); an empty map when no views match.

Item Content URL POST /api/meta/ddl/redis/refresh Params tableId: body, string, table ID. entityName: body, string, entity name. connectId: body, string, connection ID. appId: body, string, app ID. tenantCode: body, string, optional, tenant code (falls back to the current session tenant when absent). (body is a JSON object) Returns ApiMetaResult: re-parses the online DB metadata by the given conditions and refreshes the cache (operates only on the metadata database); data is empty on success.
7 controllers, 48 endpoints in total. All endpoints in this domain are design-time APIs (@DesignTimeApiRestController), intended primarily for the visual designers.
Design-time management of database connections (ConnectMeta): CRUD, connection testing and dynamic data source refresh.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/pageQuery Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult<ConnectMeta>: paged list of database connection configurations (connect name, db type, host, port, db name, schema, user name, etc.).

Item Content URL GET /api/model/connect/query Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiResult<List<ConnectMeta>>: list of connection configurations (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL GET /api/model/connect/get/{id} Params id: path, string, required, connection ID. Returns ApiResult<ConnectMeta>: connection configuration detail (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/createOrUpdate Params form: body, ConnectMeta object, required. Common fields: connect name dbConnectName, db type dbType, host dbHostnameIp, port dbPort, database dbName, schema dbSchema, user name dbUserName, password dbPassword. Returns ApiResult<ConnectMeta>: first checks duplicates by type+host+port+db name+app+tenant (fails on duplicate); with a non-blank id it updates (schema changes upgrade metadata accordingly), otherwise it creates and immediately refreshes the dynamic data source. Returns the saved connection.

Item Content URL DELETE /api/model/connect/isDelete/{id} Params id: path, string, required, connection ID. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: fails when the connection is referenced by tables/views/checks; otherwise marks it disabled and soft-deletes. data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/jdbcConnect Params form: body, ConnectMeta object, required; the driver and URL format are resolved from dbType. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: whether a valid JDBC connection can be established.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/batchCreate Params appId: body, string, required, target app ID. connectIds: body, string array, required, source connection IDs. userName: body, string, required, database user name. password: body, string, required, database password. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: copies the source connections to new ones (overriding user name, password and app); fails when an identical connection already exists. data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/refresh/{id} Params id: path, string, required, connection ID. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: whether the refresh succeeded; fails when the connection does not exist or the dynamic data source capability is disabled.
Item Content URL POST /api/model/connect/refreshAll Params None Returns ApiResult<Integer>: number of refreshed data sources; fails when the dynamic data source capability is disabled.
Design-time CRUD and uniqueness validation of table check constraints (TableCheck).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/check/pageQuery Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult<DataItems>: data is a DataItems (total plus items, the list of check constraint records).

Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/check/query Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiResult<List<TableCheck>>: list of check constraints (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/check/get/{id} Params id: path, string, required, check constraint ID. Returns ApiResult<TableCheck>: check constraint detail (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/check/createOrUpdate Params form: body, TableCheck object, required. Common fields: title title, code code, type type, check clause checkClause, owning table tableId, related column columnId (connectId, tableName, etc. are filled from the owning table). Returns ApiResult<TableCheck>: saved with synced set to not-synced, and the entity metadata cache of the owning table is refreshed (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL DELETE /api/model/table/check/isDelete/{id} Params id: path, string, required, check constraint ID. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: soft-deletes and refreshes the entity metadata cache of the owning table. data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/check/validate Params form: body, TableCheck object, required; tableId and type must not be blank, code is the uniqueness key. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: first checks platform_dev_table_check for an existing record with the same code and type, then switches to the target connection to check the database for a check constraint with the same name; returns true only when neither exists (false when the connection is missing or something exists).
Design-time CRUD of table columns (ColumnMeta), plus default column templates, select types and name-uniqueness validation.
Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/column/pageQuery Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult<ColumnMeta>: paged list of columns.

Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/column/query Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiResult<List<ColumnMeta>>: list of columns (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).
Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/column/get/{id} Params id: path, string, required, column ID. Returns ApiResult<ColumnMeta>: column detail (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/column/createOrUpdate Params form: body, ColumnMeta object, required. Common fields: column name name, title title, column type type/dataType, owning table tableId, select type selectType, auto add autoAdd/autoName, etc. Returns ApiResult<ColumnMeta>: on update, a renamed column is first copied in the database (keeping the old one) and column permissions are adjusted; on create, it is marked not-synced and table default column permissions are reset; when the select type is organization/user with auto-add enabled, related columns are generated automatically. Finally the default view and entity metadata cache are refreshed (method signature declares a raw ApiResult).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/column/insertCommon Params tableId: body, string, required, target table ID. columnIds: body, string, required, IDs of the columns to copy, comma-separated. tableName: body, string, read by the code but not used. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: copies existing columns into the target table (skipping same names, marked not-synced) and refreshes the default view and entity metadata cache. data is empty.

Item Content URL DELETE /api/model/table/column/isDelete/{id} Params id: path, string, required, column ID. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: soft-deletes and refreshes the default view and entity metadata cache. data is empty.
Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/column/queryDefaultMeta Params None Returns ApiResult<List<ColumnMeta>>: list of built-in default column templates.

Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/column/selectType Params None Returns ApiResult<List<ColumnSelectType>>: selectable data types for columns (group group, label label, value value, database type mysql, disabled flag, default length, value range, etc.).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/column/validate Params form: body, ColumnMeta object, required; uses name, tableId, appId, tenantCode. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: checks whether the column name is duplicated within the same table (queries platform_dev_column); true when available.
Design-time CRUD of tables (TableMeta) with copy, upgrade, default view and database-driven reset.
Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/pageQuery Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiPagedResult<TableMeta>: paged list of tables.
Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/query Params Pagination and filter params: see Conventions Returns ApiResult<List<TableMeta>>: list of tables.
Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/get/{id} Params id: path, string, required, table ID. Returns ApiResult<TableMeta>: table detail.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/createOrUpdate Params form: body, TableMeta object, required. Common fields: entity name entityName, title title, connection connectId, table type tableType, source sourceType, etc. (tableSchema and dbType are filled from the connection). Returns ApiResult<TableMeta>: on create, marks not-synced, initializes table default permissions and creates default columns for non-third-party sources; on update, an entity-name change backs up the old table and renames it in the database (adjusting permissions and refreshing the default view). Finally the entity metadata cache is refreshed; returns the saved table (signature declares ApiResult<?>).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/copy Params id: body, string, required, source table ID. entityName: body, string, required, entity name of the new table. title: body, string, optional, title of the new table. connectId: body, string, optional, connection of the new table. tableComment: body, string, optional, comment of the new table. appId: body, string, optional, app ID. tenantCode: body, string, optional, tenant code. Returns ApiResult<TableMeta>: copies the source table and its columns into a new table (source type reset to manual creation), initializes default permissions and refreshes the entity cache.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/upgradesTable Params tableId: body, string, required, target table ID. columnNames: body, string, required, comma-separated upgrade-template column names. upgradeType: body, string, optional, contains app to enable cross-app and workflow to enable cross-workflow. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: adds the upgrade-template columns missing from the table, updates the cross-app/cross-workflow flags per upgradeType and refreshes the entity cache; data is empty on success (signature declares ApiResult<?>).

Item Content URL DELETE /api/model/table/isDelete/{id} Params id: path, string, required, table ID. Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: soft-deletes (the database table is renamed with a _d timestamp suffix and the title/comment get a "deleted" prefix) and removes the entity metadata cache; data is empty.

Item Content URL GET /api/model/table/queryDefaultView/{entityName} Params entityName: path, string, required, entity name. Returns ApiResult<String>: the default view SQL (viewConstruct) generated from the entity columns.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/resetDefaultView Params form: body, TableMeta object, required; entityName must not be blank (matched together with id and connectId). Returns ApiResult<NullResult>: rebuilds or updates the default view for the matched tables. data is empty.

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/reset/{tableId} Params tableId: path, string, required, table ID; disabled tables cannot be reset. Returns ApiMetaResult<NullResult>: syncs the table definition from the actual database structure (updates the table info and resets columns and foreign keys; when the table no longer exists in the database it is soft-deleted). data is empty (with the extra meta).

Item Content URL POST /api/model/table/validate Params form: body, TableMeta object, required; uses entityName, connectId, appId, tenantCode. Returns ApiResult<Boolean>: checks whether the entity name is duplicated within the same connection; when conflict detection is enabled and the name clashes with a loaded Java built-in entity, a failure message is returned directly.
