This page summarizes the framework capabilities that ship with geelato-dyn and how to consume them. Business modules access all of them by referencing OSGi services with a zero-config <reference> — no addresses, accounts or secrets are copied anywhere.

geelato-dyn-datasource centrally defines every MySQL connection pool (HikariCP) and publishes them as OSGi services by logical name. Connection credentials exist in exactly one place in the repo; business modules reference by logical name and never configure IP/username/password themselves. Logical name Database platform geelato platform database portal Portal database integration Integration database buss Business database Two-step integration: <!-- Blueprint: reference by logical name; this module carries no credentials --> <reference id="portalDataSource" interface="javax.sql.DataSource" filter="(datasource.name=portal)"/> <bean id="portalJdbcTemplate" class="org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate"> <property name="dataSource" ref="portalDataSource"/> </bean> <!-- features.xml: declare the dependency on the central datasource feature --> <repository>mvn:cn.geelato/geelato-dyn-datasource/${project.version}/xml/features</repository> <feature name="geelato-dyn-xxx" version="${project.version}"> <feature version="${project.version}">geelato-dyn-datasource</feature> </feature> Behavior notes: <reference> is a strong dependency: while the central datasource module is not ready, business bundles wait (GracePeriod) instead of starting broken; Hikari pools connect lazily: an unused database in some environment is never physically connected and does not affect other pools; Each datasource contributes a health item running SELECT 1, exposed through health aggregation; Java constant: cn.geelato.dyn.datasource.GeelatoDataSources; Adding a new logical datasource only touches the central module (a property group + bean + service publication in datasource.xml); business modules can use it immediately — see the repo's geelato-dyn-datasource/README.md for the steps.

SPI: cn.geelato.dyn.common.health.ModuleHealthReporter (module() / snapshot() / ttlMs()), with ModuleHealthSnapshot / HealthCheckItem / HealthLevel. Module side: implement a reporter and register it as an OSGi service; scheduled-job modules pair it with a HealthState (recordStart / recordSuccess / recordFailure instrumentation, failure messages must be sanitized); optionally cn.geelato.dyn.common.logging.ModuleLogLevelProvider fills the logLevel field in aggregated output; Aggregation side: geelato-dyn-manage collects all reporters automatically via <reference-list> — no aggregation-side code changes, a newly installed module shows up on its own; REST: GET /cxf/health, GET /cxf/health/modules, GET /cxf/health/modules/{module} (no auth); Snapshots carry runtime / business status levels plus items detail; after ttlMs() expires the aggregator marks the entry ttl expired (for scheduled jobs use maxSilenceMs or 2–3× the schedule interval). Framework modules (datasource / unified-api / consumer-main, etc.) ship built-in reporters; business modules implement the SPI as needed to join the aggregation.

geelato-dyn-common embeds the community geelato-security jar and exports the contract package cn.geelato.security (SecurityContext / User / Org / Tenant / UserProvider / OrgProvider). Every bundle in Karaf only needs to Import-Package it — nothing else to install. The built-in DBUserProvider / DBOrgProvider connect directly to the geelato platform database, querying platform_user / platform_org / platform_org_r_user / platform_role_r_user in real time with no snapshot cache: <reference id="userProvider" interface="cn.geelato.security.UserProvider"/> <reference id="orgProvider" interface="cn.geelato.security.OrgProvider"/> User user = userProvider.getUser(userId); // includes roles and affiliated orgs User user2 = userProvider.getUserByExtendKey("zhangsan", "loginName"); Org org = orgProvider.getOrg(orgId); String deptId = orgProvider.getDeptId(orgId); // walks up the pid chain to dept/company String companyId = orgProvider.getCompanyId(orgId); Additionally cn.geelato.dyn.common.user.UserDirectoryService (JDBC implementation) fetches contacts in batch by userId — used for message recipient resolution and similar scenarios.

Two styles, pick per need: Style 1: service properties (consumed by the Karaf scheduler feature; shows up in the console's "scheduled services" tab): <bean id="myJob" class="cn.geelato.dyn.xxx.MyJob"/> <service ref="myJob" ref-type="service" interface="java.lang.Runnable"> <service-properties> <entry key="scheduler.name" value="my-job"/> <entry key="scheduler.expression" value="0 * * * * ?"/> <entry key="scheduler.concurrent" value="false"/> </service-properties> </service> Style 2: declarative (Blueprint extender): <scheduler:scheduledRunnable ref="myJob" cron-expression="0 0/10 * * * ?"/>
cn.geelato.dyn.common.id.SnowflakeIds: process-wide ID generation, shared by persistence primary keys (e.g. callback capture tables) and business entity IDs.

geelato-dyn-manage ships a visual console. Everything is read-only and never changes runtime state. Page: http://<host>:8181/cxf/dyn/manage/; APIs require the X-Manage-Token header (configuration in Configuration & Logging). geelato-dyn does not use Spring's application.yml. Its configuration is built on OSGi Config Admin: a Blueprint cm:property-placeholder defines defaults, a .cfg file under the Karaf etc/ directory overrides them by PID, and changes take effect hot.

Blueprint cm:default-properties (in-code defaults, works out of the box) ▲ overrides Karaf etc/<PID>.cfg (environment-specific values; Config Admin rebuilds beans on change, no restart) Key points: cfg values take precedence over defaults, and you only need to override the keys that differ per environment; update-strategy="reload": saving a cfg change applies it immediately (e.g. datasource pools are rebuilt automatically); cfg files natively support ${env:XXX} environment-variable references — preferred for credentials so no plaintext lands on disk; If Blueprint defaults are blanked and the cfg is missing, the bundle fails fast at startup naming the missing property, preventing silent misrouting to the wrong database.

PID (cfg file name) Module Key settings cn.geelato.dyn.datasource geelato-dyn-datasource Connection and pool settings for the 4 logical databases cn.geelato.dyn.manage geelato-dyn-manage Console access token Business modules custom business modules See each module's Blueprint cm:property-placeholder

Key pattern: <logicalName>.jdbcUrl / username / password / pool.maxSize / pool.minIdle. The cfg template lives in the repo at geelato-dyn-datasource/config/: platform.jdbcUrl = jdbc:mysql://<host>:3306/geelato?useSSL=true&serverTimezone=Asia/Shanghai&characterEncoding=UTF-8 platform.username = geelato_user platform.password = ${env:GEELATO_PLATFORM_DB_PASSWORD} platform.pool.maxSize = 10 platform.pool.minIdle = 2 # portal / integration / buss follow the same pattern For what the logical names mean and how to reference them, see Built-in Capabilities / Central Datasources.

manage.console.token=<access-token> The console exposes sensitive data such as database credentials, so a non-empty token is mandatory; when it is unset, /cxf/dyn/manage/api/* always responds 503 (the page loads but shows no data). Changes apply hot on save.

Some settings are not cfg keys but bean properties inside Blueprint XML; changing them requires rebuilding and republishing the bundle: Location Contents geelato-dyn-common/.../geelato-common-message.xml Message outbox MessageCenterOutbox (baseUrl / systemCode / apiKey / timeoutMs); in-app direct channel InAppDirectChannelAdapter (enabled / baseUrl / communityToken / timeoutMs) geelato-dyn-unified-api/.../spring-jdbc.xml Callback persistence datasource; processor switches (unifiedConsumer=true, db / rabbitMq default false); RabbitMQ connection settings Business module *.xml Business config beans (API URLs, secrets, cron expressions, etc.) :::note Choosing where a setting belongs One codebase, two usages: with no cfg deployed the XML defaults apply (zero ops); dropping the cfg template into etc/ hands control to operations. Values that change per environment (databases, tokens) should go through cfg first. :::

The Karaf (pax-logging-log4j2) baseline config gives each of the 13 modules its own logger by root package plus its own log file, with no Java code changes: Log files live in Karaf's data/log/, named dyn-<module>.log (e.g. dyn-common.log, dyn-unified-api.log); All module loggers set additivity=false: module logs go only to their own file, and karaf.log keeps container plus Camel / CXF / Spring / Blueprint framework logs; Rolling policy matches karaf.log: 16MB per file, up to 20 rolled files per module; Attribution follows the package the code lives in: classes in cn.geelato.dyn.common invoked from other modules still log into dyn-common.log; Nested packages never cross files (Log4J2 matches the most specific logger). The baseline file and push script are in the repo under karaf/: karaf/etc/org.ops4j.pax.logging.cfg + karaf/scripts/apply-logging-config.sh (backs up the target's current config before overwriting). If the target instance has customized its logging cfg, do not overwrite the whole file — append the baseline's geelato-dyn modules block to the existing file instead.

karaf@root()> log:set DEBUG cn.geelato.dyn.{module} karaf@root()> log:get cn.geelato.dyn.{module} karaf@root()> log:set INFO cn.geelato.dyn.{module} # revert log:set writes the change back into the instance's org.ops4j.pax.logging.cfg, so the instance file diverging from the repo baseline afterwards is expected; the instance file is authoritative.
Append one module block (appender + logger, three paired renames) to the end of org.ops4j.pax.logging.cfg and re-push the baseline; the template is in the repo's karaf/README-logging.md.

New business modules are created by copying the scaffold geelato-dyn-template. The template mirrors the structure of real business modules: three Blueprint templates, a DDL script and a scheduled-job skeleton.

Copy the geelato-dyn-template directory and rename it to geelato-dyn-{your-module}; Global-replace three identifiers: Replace Example Template → {YourModule} (leading capital) TemplateJob → InventoryJob template → {your-module} (all lowercase) package cn.geelato.dyn.template → cn.geelato.dyn.inventory tt_ → {your_prefix}_ table prefix, e.g. tt_entity → inv_task Change the pom.xml artifactId to geelato-dyn-{your-module}; Edit and run the DDL script src/main/resources/sql/init.sql; Add the new module to the root pom.xml <modules>.

Component Pattern Example Package cn.geelato.dyn.{module} cn.geelato.dyn.inventory Job entry {Module}Job implements Runnable InventoryJob Business service {Module}Service InventoryService Database service {Module}DatabaseService InventoryDatabaseService Entity {Module}Entity InventoryEntity Business Blueprint {module}.xml inventory.xml Table prefix custom prefix + _ inv_

File Responsibility {module}.xml Business bean wiring (Service / Job / DatabaseService dependency injection) spring-jdbc.xml Datasource reference: <reference> by logical name to the central datasource + own JdbcTemplate; no credentials in this module cron.xml Declarative scheduled job scheduler:scheduledRunnable

<!-- Central datasource --> <reference id="dataSource" interface="javax.sql.DataSource" filter="(datasource.name=buss)"/> <!-- Unified message dispatch --> <reference id="messageDispatcher" interface="cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.MessageDispatcher"/> <!-- Security contracts: users / orgs --> <reference id="userProvider" interface="cn.geelato.security.UserProvider"/> <reference id="orgProvider" interface="cn.geelato.security.OrgProvider"/> To appear in health aggregation, add a ModuleHealthReporter (see Built-in Capabilities / Health Check). For config keys, declare a PID with <cm:property-placeholder> and ship an etc/<PID>.cfg template (see Configuration & Logging).

SPI Owner Purpose cn.geelato.dyn.common.health.ModuleHealthReporter common Module health snapshot reporting (runtime / business / items / ttlMs) cn.geelato.dyn.common.logging.ModuleLogLevelProvider common Fills this module's logLevel in aggregated output cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.channel.MessageChannelAdapter common Add a message channel (outbox or direct style) cn.geelato.dyn.unified.api.service.UnifiedConsumerBinding unified-api Register callback token → bizCode routing and self-check endpoints ...processor.AbstractCallbackProcessor unified-api Add a callback processing style beyond persistence / MQ / bus

Three options, choose as needed: Security contracts (recommended, zero cost): geelato-dyn-common already exports the cn.geelato.security contract package plus DBUserProvider / DBOrgProvider implementations — <reference> them to query users and orgs. Message REST (recommended): <reference> the MessageDispatcher; delivery is handled by the message center (see Unified Message Dispatch). community ORM (advanced): a business module can host the community OrmAutoConfiguration inside an embedded Spring Context in a bundle, making the Fluent DSL (MetaFactory.query/insert/...) usable (decision record: the ADR docs under the repo's examples/). Key points: Embedded dependencies: geelato-orm / geelato-core / geelato-lang / geelato-utils + spring-boot(autoconfigure); Blueprint injects the central datasource OSGi service, registered as a singleton in the embedded Context before context.refresh(); TCCL switch: the Blueprint extender thread's contextClassLoader is Karaf's root classloader — temporarily switch it to the bundle classloader around refresh, otherwise @ConditionalOnBean handler classes cannot be loaded; Disable entity auto-scan: scanning is unreliable under OSGi's multiple classloaders; set geelato.orm.entity-auto-scan-enabled=false and register entities explicitly with MetaManager.parseOne(clazz); Do not manually register OrmProperties again (OrmAutoConfiguration already provides it; a duplicate causes NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException).

# Build (bundle jar + features classifier) mvn -pl geelato-dyn-{your-module} -am clean install # Install / update / uninstall feature:repo-add mvn:cn.geelato/geelato-dyn-{your-module}/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features feature:install geelato-dyn-{your-module} The feature declares its dependencies on geelato-dyn-common (and geelato-dyn-datasource as needed), which Karaf installs transitively.

Blueprint references datasources by logical name only; no IP/username/password anywhere in the module Scheduled jobs carry health instrumentation (recordStart / recordSuccess / recordFailure, sanitized failures) and a registered ModuleHealthReporter A logger block for this module was added to karaf/etc/org.ops4j.pax.logging.cfg (otherwise logs go to karaf.log) A config/<PID>.cfg template exists for any cfg-managed settings features.xml declares all prerequisite features mvn -pl <module> -am clean install passes and features.xml is published with classifier=features After installation, GET /cxf/health/modules lists this module
Integration & Deployment — feature install and update commands Unified Callback & Consumer Bus — wiring consumer-style modules

The integration unit of geelato-dyn is a Karaf feature: each module is published as a bundle jar plus features.xml (classifier=features). The target Karaf adds the repository definition with feature:repo-add and installs with feature:install.

Item Requirement Java JDK 17 Karaf 4.4.10 Maven repository Reachable from the target Karaf (private repo or the build machine's local ~/.m2) Database Run each module's DDL script (under each module's src/main/resources/sql/) Platform side Message outbox requires a reachable geelato-message center; in-app direct delivery requires a reachable community platform

Build and install (or deploy to your private repo) from the geelato-dyn project root: mvn -pl <module> -am clean install Make sure features.xml is published with classifier=features — feature installation depends on it; installing the bare jar with bundle:install alone leaves out the runtime dependencies.

# Foundation: messaging / security / users / health / IDs feature:repo-add mvn:cn.geelato/geelato-dyn-common/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features feature:install geelato-dyn-common # Central datasources: prerequisite for any module that needs a database feature:repo-add mvn:cn.geelato/geelato-dyn-datasource/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features feature:install geelato-dyn-datasource :::warning Why installing the bundle alone is not enough The Blueprint of geelato-dyn-common declares HikariDataSource, JdbcTemplate, Jackson and other dependency bundles. Running only bundle:install -s mvn:cn.geelato/geelato-dyn-common/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT without those bundles makes Blueprint bean instantiation fail with ComponentDefinitionException / ClassNotFoundException. Always use feature:* commands — dependencies are provided transitively by features.xml. :::

Scenario Install command (repo-add first, coordinates as above) Prerequisites Health aggregation + management console feature:install geelato-dyn-manage common Unified callback + consumer bus feature:install geelato-dyn-unified-consumer-main common; this feature installs unified-api transitively Adding a callback consumer feature:install geelato-dyn-unified-consumer-{your-module} consumer-main When installing a module, Karaf resolves and installs the feature dependencies declared in its features.xml. <reference> service dependencies are strong (GracePeriod): a business bundle waits instead of starting in a broken state when its prerequisite module is not ready.

# Feature / bundle status feature:list | grep geelato-dyn bundle:list | grep geelato-dyn # Central datasources: expect 4 DataSource services, each with a datasource.name property service:list javax.sql.DataSource # Security contract services registered services | grep -E "UserProvider|OrgProvider" # Health aggregation (requires manage, no auth) curl "http://localhost:8181/cxf/health"

Standard update flow (after re-publishing artifacts): feature:uninstall <feature-name> feature:repo-remove mvn:cn.geelato/<module>/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features feature:repo-add mvn:cn.geelato/<module>/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features feature:install <feature-name> For jar-only changes with unchanged dependencies, a lightweight refresh works: feature:repo-refresh bundle:update <bundleId> Uninstalling: feature:uninstall <feature-name> feature:repo-remove mvn:cn.geelato/<module>/0.0.1-SNAPSHOT/xml/features

The root POM ships a karaf-deploy profile (karaf-maven-plugin) that pushes features directly to a remote Karaf instance at build time, which suits CI pipelines; day-to-day operations should still use the feature:* commands.
Configuration & Logging — cfg overrides, hot reload and log separation after deployment Built-in Capabilities — how to consume each capability

geelato-dyn-common ships a unified message dispatch capability registered as the OSGi service MessageDispatcher. Design principles: Zero channel configuration for business modules: they assemble a MessageRequest and call dispatch, unaware of any channel address or token; No direct platform-database access: the email / sms / bot / WeCom channels are "outbox style" — they submit over REST to the geelato-message center (POST /message/enqueue), which handles idempotency, routing, platform_msg persistence and actual delivery; Channel configuration lives in one place: everything is wired in geelato-dyn-common's geelato-common-message.xml; one change affects all business modules. For the message center's own payload format and routing, see the Message Center docs.

<!-- Blueprint: zero-config reference --> <reference id="messageDispatcher" interface="cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.MessageDispatcher"/> MessageRequest request = new MessageRequest(); request.setTitle("Stock warning"); request.setTextContent("SKU A1001 below safety stock"); request.setChannels(List.of(MessageChannel.EMAIL, MessageChannel.INAPP)); request.setRecipients(...); // MessageRecipients request.setBizKeyBase("stock-warning"); // idempotency key prefix request.setTenantCode("geelato"); List<String> msgIds = messageDispatcher.dispatch(request); // returns platform_msg ids Types live in the cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.model package: MessageRequest (setter-style POJO), MessageRecipients, MessageAttachment, MessageChannel (channel code constants).

Field Notes title / textContent / htmlContent Title and body: plain-text reminders only need textContent; rich emails fill htmlContent (in-app falls back to text when htmlContent is absent) attachments Attachment list (email attachments; WeCom may build a link card from the first attachment) linkUrl / linkTitle / linkDesc WeCom link card (when linkUrl is empty the adapter may fall back to the first attachment url) recipients MessageRecipients recipient set channels Channel code list, constants in MessageChannel bizKeyBase Business idempotency key prefix; final platform_msg.biz_key = bizKeyBase + ":" + channelCode tenantCode / sender Tenant (defaults to geelato) and sender identity Others Channel extension attributes etc., see the source Javadoc

SPI: cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.channel.MessageChannelAdapter (channelCode() + resolve(MessageRequest)), base class AbstractMessageChannelAdapter. The registry MessageChannelRegistry manages two groups: Channel Path Notes email Outbox (message center) HTML and attachments supported sms Outbox (message center) SMS bot Outbox (message center) WeCom group robot (session-based) weixin_work_group Outbox (message center) WeCom app / group messages weixin_work_robot Outbox (message center) Not yet usable: the message center has no route mapping for this type yet and would reject the enqueue; enable once the route exists inapp Direct (bypasses the message center) InAppDirectChannelAdapter synchronously POSTs to the community platform's in-app messaging (fixed Authorization: SystemToken key); with enabled=false the channel is skipped, no outbox fallback

Outbox and direct-channel settings are centralized in geelato-dyn-common/src/main/resources/OSGI-INF/blueprint/geelato-common-message.xml (adjust per environment at deployment): <!-- Message center outbox: systemCode goes into the X-System-Code header, apiKey into the Authorization: Bearer header (only needed when the message center enables integration auth) --> <bean id="messageCenterOutbox" class="...channel.MessageCenterOutbox"> <property name="baseUrl" value="<message-center-url>"/> <property name="systemCode" value="geelato-dyn"/> <property name="apiKey" value="<apiKey>"/> <property name="timeoutMs" value="10000"/> </bean> <!-- In-app direct: communityToken is the community platform's SystemToken fixed key, matching the community's geelato.security.system-token.token (Bearer will not work) --> <bean id="inAppDirectChannelAdapter" class="...channel.InAppDirectChannelAdapter"> <property name="enabled" value="true"/> <property name="baseUrl" value="<community-platform-url>"/> <property name="communityToken" value="<SystemToken>"/> <property name="timeoutMs" value="10000"/> </bean> :::note How to change these settings Outbox URL, direct URL and tokens are bean properties in this XML — i.e. Blueprint bean configuration: after editing, rebuild and republish the common bundle and reinstall the feature; all business modules pick it up at once. :::

Implement MessageChannelAdapter (or extend AbstractMessageChannelAdapter), add the new adapter to the MessageChannelRegistry adapters / directChannels list and republish common; business modules can then select it via a MessageChannel constant.
Built-in Capabilities — user directory (batch recipient resolution) and other supporting capabilities Unified Callback & Consumer Bus — the reverse path: receiving third-party callbacks

geelato-dyn is a dynamic integration framework built on Apache Karaf 4.4.10 + OSGi. It runs independently of the geelato platform (the Spring Boot host); the two share no Maven dependency and are integrated only through embedded security contracts, direct platform-database access, and REST calls. The problem it solves: business integration units (scheduled jobs, third-party callbacks, outbound integrations) are added and removed frequently and released independently — they should not force repeated restarts of the platform process. Each functional unit is an OSGi bundle that is installed, updated and uninstalled independently through Karaf features, without affecting other bundles at runtime. :::note Unrelated to the "dynamic datasource" This framework (geelato-dyn) has nothing to do with the dynamic datasource capability in geelato-orm (see the Datasource chapter) despite the similar name. The dynamic datasource handles multi-database routing inside the Spring host; geelato-dyn is a separate runtime inside Karaf. :::

Component Version Role Apache Karaf 4.4.10 Container and feature-based deployment OSGi Blueprint Aries Bean wiring and <reference> service injection OSGi Config Admin Aries etc/*.cfg configuration with hot reload Apache CXF JAX-RS 2.1 REST services (mounted under Karaf's default /cxf) Apache Camel 3.22.4 In-process routing (vm: endpoints) Karaf Scheduler Quartz cron Scheduled jobs HikariCP 5.1.0 Connection pools (held centrally by the datasource module) pax-logging (log4j2) — Per-module log file separation Java 17 Build and runtime baseline

Capability Provided by Facade / Entry point Central datasources (referenced by logical name) geelato-dyn-datasource javax.sql.DataSource OSGi service (datasource.name=…) Unified message dispatch (6 channels) geelato-dyn-common cn.geelato.dyn.common.message.MessageDispatcher Security contracts + user/org lookup geelato-dyn-common cn.geelato.security.UserProvider / OrgProvider Health check & aggregation geelato-dyn-common + geelato-dyn-manage ModuleHealthReporter SPI → GET /cxf/health Unified callback north-bound entry geelato-dyn-unified-api POST /cxf/unified/callback/{token} Unified consumer bus geelato-dyn-unified-consumer-main Camel vm: dispatch by bizCode Visual management console geelato-dyn-manage /cxf/dyn/manage/ (token auth) Scheduled jobs Karaf scheduler / Blueprint Runnable service properties or scheduler:scheduledRunnable Snowflake IDs geelato-dyn-common cn.geelato.dyn.common.id.SnowflakeIds Per-module log separation Karaf baseline config One dyn-*.log per module See Built-in Capabilities for how to consume each capability. Message dispatch and the callback bus get their own pages: Unified Message Dispatch and Unified Callback & Consumer Bus.

Module (artifactId) Role Deployment geelato-dyn-common Foundation bundle: contracts and wiring for messaging / security / users / health / IDs Required (prerequisite of all modules) geelato-dyn-datasource Central datasources: 4 HikariCP logical pools published as services Prerequisite for modules that need a database geelato-dyn-manage Health aggregation REST + visual management console Optional (operations) geelato-dyn-unified-api Unified callback north-bound entry + capture/processed persistence Optional (callback scenarios) geelato-dyn-unified-consumer-main Unified consumer bus (Camel vm: dispatch) Optional (pairs with unified-api; its feature installs unified-api transitively) geelato-dyn-template Scaffold for new modules (not deployed) Not deployed This chapter covers only the generic and abstract framework modules above. Concrete business implementations (business consumers, bus-* scheduled modules, *-integrate modules, etc.) are out of scope; refer to each module's own documentation in the repository.

geelato-dyn-common (foundation: messaging / security / users / health / IDs) ├── geelato-dyn-datasource (central datasources; required by DB-backed modules) ├── geelato-dyn-manage (operations aggregation, installed independently) └── geelato-dyn-unified-api (callback entry) └── geelato-dyn-unified-consumer-main (consumer bus; its feature installs unified-api) └── business consumer modules (publish a UnifiedConsumerBinding to join) Business modules (scheduled jobs, callback consumers, external-system integrations) all sit at the leaves of this topology: implement the corresponding SPI and declare the feature dependency to join, without touching any framework module. There is no single-starter integration entry point: the minimal runtime set is geelato-dyn-common (plus geelato-dyn-datasource when a database is needed). Everything else is installed on demand and fully pluggable.

Integration point Mechanism Notes Security contracts Embedded jar geelato-dyn-common embeds the community geelato-security jar via Embed-Dependency and exports cn.geelato.security; every bundle in Karaf can import it directly User / org data Direct platform DB access DBUserProvider / DBOrgProvider query platform_user / platform_org and related tables in real time, no cache Message sending REST Outbox submits to the geelato-message center via POST /message/enqueue; the center persists and delivers In-app message Direct REST The inapp channel calls the community platform directly (fixed Authorization: SystemToken key), bypassing the message center ORM (optional) Spring Context embedded in a bundle A business module can host the community OrmAutoConfiguration inside a bundle, enabling the Fluent DSL (see Developing a New Module)

Integration & Deployment — prerequisites, feature installation, updates and verification Configuration & Logging — Config Admin hot reload, PID inventory, log separation Built-in Capabilities — datasources / health / security / scheduling / console / REST endpoint table
This guide explains how to create a production-ready backend project based on geelato-app-scaffold-starter, and how to use the built-in baseline capabilities.

By introducing this Starter, your project will automatically have the following 7 core capabilities: 🔐 Login and Authentication: Built-in JWT local login and OAuth2 authorization code login, automatically intercepting and parsing Tokens. 📁 File Processing and OSS: Provides unified local/OSS file upload, download, and preview interfaces. 🔍 MQL Dynamic Query: Through the /api/meta/* interface, the frontend can directly send JSON to query the database dynamically. ⚙️ ORM Fluent DSL: Backend business code can directly use MetaFactory for chained CRUD operations that prevent SQL injection. 📖 Data Dictionary: Built-in creation, maintenance, and fast querying by Code for dictionary items. 👥 Organization and RBAC: Built-in standard user, organization, role, permission models, and assignment interfaces. 📚 OpenAPI (Swagger): Automatically generates and exposes interface documentation in the dev/test environments by default.

Before calling any of the above capabilities, please note the basic conventions: Unified Prefix: All scaffold interfaces start with /api. Tenant Isolation: It is recommended to carry Tenant-Code in all request headers (defaults to geelato if not provided). Authentication Credentials: After a successful login, Authorization must be carried in the request header. JWT Login: Authorization: JWTBearer {token} OAuth2 Login: Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}

Item Requirement JDK 17 (java -version) Maven 3.8+ (mvn -v) MySQL 8.x installed and running, localhost:3306 reachable; the DB bootstrap needs an account with CREATE USER privileges Port 8088 is free Upload directories /upload, /upload/convert, /upload/config must be created manually and be writable (use local absolute paths such as D:/upload on Windows) Maven repository A repository with credentials that can resolve cn.geelato artifacts — see the next section Note: some environments inject variables such as SERVER__PORT; Spring Boot relaxed binding lets them override server.port. Check with env | grep -i SERVER or pass --server.port=8088 explicitly.

The framework is currently distributed as 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT through a private Maven repository; no Geelato artifacts are available on Maven Central yet. Without credentials the build fails at BOM import with Non-resolvable import POM: cn.geelato:geelato-framework-bom:pom:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT. Request a packages.aliyun.com artifact-repository account from the framework team. Configure ~/.m2/settings.xml: <settings> <servers> <server> <id>geelato-snapshots</id> <username><!-- requested account --></username> <password><!-- requested credential --></password> </server> </servers> <profiles> <profile> <id>geelato</id> <repositories> <repository> <id>geelato-snapshots</id> <url>https://packages.aliyun.com/maven/repository/2367868-snapshot-hDbqny</url> <releases><enabled>false</enabled></releases> <snapshots><enabled>true</enabled></snapshots> </repository> </repositories> </profile> </profiles> <activeProfiles> <activeProfile>geelato</activeProfile> </activeProfiles> </settings> Precheck: mvn -B dependency:get -Dartifact=cn.geelato:geelato-framework-bom:pom:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT Notes: a global <mirrorOf>*</mirrorOf> mirror must exclude this repository (<mirrorOf>*,!geelato-snapshots</mirrorOf>); the commercial dependency com.aspose:aspose-words also lives only in the private repository. geelato-app-scaffold-starter has no public source-build path (it depends on geelato-package and plugin-all outside the public repository), so credentials are required.

You can either: copy the runnable sample geelato-hello-example/geelato-app-scaffold, then change Maven coordinates / package name / configs or create an empty Spring Boot project and add the starter dependency

If you want to standardize and automate “create the business project + fill in required configs + verify the minimal working loop”, you can reuse the Skill from the sample repository and let AI guide/modify your project automatically. Skill source: https://github.com/geelato-projects/geelato-hello-example/tree/main/skills/geelato-app-scaffold-starter-guide Recommended usage: import the above folder as a custom Skill in your AI tool (TRAE Skills) in chat, invoke: Use Skill: geelato-app-scaffold-starter-guide provide: project directory, groupId/artifactId, base package, database connection, and enabled capabilities (login/mql/dictionary/organization/user/upload) This Skill is distilled from the starter project guide and will walk you through: minimal runnable project setup (pom / bootstrap class / application.properties) artifact repository and credential configuration verifiable baseline loops (dictionary, org/user, upload) Minimal pom.xml snippet: <dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>cn.geelato</groupId> <artifactId>geelato-framework-bom</artifactId> <version>${geelato.version}</version> <type>pom</type> <scope>import</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> </dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>cn.geelato</groupId> <artifactId>geelato-app-scaffold-starter</artifactId> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>com.mysql</groupId> <artifactId>mysql-connector-j</artifactId> <scope>runtime</scope> </dependency> </dependencies>

Use cn.geelato.web.platform.boot.BootApplication as the base class and make sure your business package is included in scanning: @SpringBootApplication(scanBasePackages = {"cn.geelato", "com.acme.order"}) public class AcmeOrderApplication extends BootApplication {}

spring.application.name=acme-order-center server.port=8088 spring.datasource.primary.name=primary spring.datasource.primary.jdbc-url=${GEELATO_PRIMARY_JDBCURL:jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/acme_order_center?useUnicode=true&characterEncoding=utf-8&useSSL=false&allowMultiQueries=true&serverTimezone=GMT%2B8&allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true} spring.datasource.primary.username=${GEELATO_PRIMARY_JDBCUSER:acme_user} spring.datasource.primary.password=${GEELATO_PRIMARY_JDBCPASSWORD:acme@psd} spring.datasource.primary.driver-class-name=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver geelato.orm.dao-bean-name=dynamicDao geelato.datasource.dynamic.enable-jta-transaction=false geelato.datasource.dynamic.enable-seata-proxy=false geelato.app.scaffold.auto-init-tables=true springdoc.api-docs.enabled=true springdoc.api-docs.path=/v3/api-docs geelato.app.scaffold.openapi-enabled=true geelato.app.scaffold.openapi-expose-in-prod=false # OSS (optional) # enable /api/oss/* only when the config is complete # geelato.oss.accessKeyId=*** # geelato.oss.accessKeySecret=*** # geelato.oss.endPoint=oss-cn-xxx.aliyuncs.com # geelato.oss.bucketName=your-bucket # geelato.oss.region=cn-xxx geelato.meta.scan-package-names=cn.geelato,com.acme.order geelato.graal.scan-package-names=cn.geelato,com.acme.order

The scaffold opens standard login entry points by default. Usage: JWT Password Login The seeded user gl_user ships without a usable plaintext password. Reset it first (after this the password is Geelato@2026): UPDATE platform_user SET password = 'e7c3f13e711f5a0a95675761b8d9a8e2b97e8e43', salt = 'def8ff5614e0892f' WHERE login_name = 'gl_user' AND tenant_code = 'geelato'; Password storage: password = hex(sha1(salt + plaintext)) chained-iterated with sha1 up to 1024 rounds. Then log in (note the request fields are username / tenant, matching LoginParams — not loginName / tenantCode; no token required): curl -X POST "http://localhost:8088/api/user/login" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ --data "{\"username\":\"gl_user\",\"password\":\"Geelato@2026\",\"tenant\":\"geelato\"}" A response with code: 20000 carries data.token, which is used for all subsequent business requests via Authorization: JWTBearer {token}.

Allows the frontend to define query structures via JSON to fetch required data directly, without the backend writing extra Controllers/Mappers. Usage: Frontend requests MQL interface List query: POST /api/meta/list Save single record: POST /api/meta/save/{biz} Delete single record: POST /api/meta/delete/{biz}/{id} Query example (fetch user list, returning only specified fields and sorting): { "platform_user": { "@fs": "id,loginName,name", "@p": "1,10", "@order": "createAt|-" } }

Backend developers no longer need to write tedious SQL or MyBatis XML for custom business logic. Usage: Call MetaFactory directly in Service // Query example: fetch 10 users on page 1, returning only id and name fields List<Map<String, Object>> users = MetaFactory.query("User") .select(new String[]{"id", "name"}) .page(1, 10) .list();

Provides a standard data dictionary maintenance system, supporting tree or list structures. Usage: Maintain and Query Dictionaries Create dictionary: POST /api/dict/createOrUpdate Create dictionary item: POST /api/dict/item/createOrUpdate Business query: The frontend can quickly fetch dictionary items for dropdown rendering via GET /api/system/dictionary/{code} (e.g., GET /api/system/dictionary/order_status; requires Authorization).

A complete set of permission management APIs is built-in. Usage: User and Role Assignment Create organization: POST /api/security/org/createOrUpdate Create user: POST /api/security/user/createOrUpdate Assign role: POST /api/security/role/user/insert

Unified handling of frontend file uploads and downloads. If object storage like Aliyun is configured, it automatically switches to OSS mode. Usage: File Upload Interface: POST /api/upload/file (multipart) curl -X POST "http://localhost:8088/api/upload/file" \ -H "Authorization: JWTBearer {token}" \ -F "file=@D:/tmp/demo.png"

Your custom interfaces and scaffold interfaces are automatically aggregated into a standard OpenAPI specification document. Usage: Access Documentation Swagger UI: http://localhost:8088/swagger-ui/index.html JSON Contract: http://localhost:8088/v3/api-docs

# Whether to expose Swagger in prod (default false for security) geelato.app.scaffold.openapi-expose-in-prod=false # Auto-enable /api/oss/* if OSS parameters are provided geelato.oss.accessKeyId=*** geelato.oss.accessKeySecret=*** geelato.oss.endPoint=oss-cn-xxx.aliyuncs.com geelato.oss.bucketName=your-bucket Capability pruning note: the current starter (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT) prunes platform controllers against a built-in capability set (15 items, returned as capabilities by /api/scaffold/ready). geelato.app.scaffold.strict and geelato.app.scaffold.capabilities are planned keys that have no effect in this version; geelato.app.scaffold.enabled is not a valid key. Use geelato.app.scaffold.extra-controllers (list of controller FQCNs) to extend the whitelist with your own controllers.

Welcome to the Geelato Framework! This document is designed for both human developers and AI coding assistants (e.g., Trae, Copilot). It provides a clear capability matrix, a quick lookup map, and best practices for collaborating with AI, helping you quickly locate requirements and start coding.

Different scenarios have different entry points. Choose based on your needs: My Goal Is... Recommended Path / Anchor I want to start from scratch and quickly generate a complete CRUD backend project Recommended to use the App Scaffold. See: Scaffold Project Guide I have an existing Spring Boot project and want to integrate Geelato core capabilities Recommended Minimal Integration. See: Minimal Integration I want to learn the platform's Runtime and Designer app shells Read the app shell docs. See: PlatformWebRuntime I want to quickly integrate Single Sign-On (SSO) and authentication See the authentication overview. See: Authentication Overview
When you need a specific function during development, use the table below to quickly jump to the corresponding guide.

Intent Core Components / Tech Stack Documentation Write backend CRUD code MetaFactory, Fluent DSL ORM: Fluent DSL Configure table names and field mappings on Entity classes @Title, @Col, @Model ORM: Annotations Perform complex queries via JSON from frontend or gateway MQL (Meta Query Language) MQL: Syntax & Usage Configure or connect multiple databases Dynamic Datasource Dynamic Datasource

Intent Core Components / Tech Stack Documentation Get current login user, tenant, or request context Global Context, SecurityContext Capabilities: Global Context, Security Contract: Security Context Intercept logic before/after data save or update Entity Events, Event Bus ORM: Event Features Extend platform default rules (e.g., query filters, field filling) SPI, Spring Bean Query Filter and Field Fill SPI Develop, load, and unload business plugins Plugin Mechanism Plugin: Development

Intent Core Components / Tech Stack Documentation Handle attachment upload and download FileController, OSS Module File Upload Query RESTful API contracts provided by the backend SrvExplain, OpenAPI API Reference
If you are using an AI assistant (like Trae, Cursor), providing the correct "Geelato terminology" will yield higher-quality code generation.

🟢 When building queries: "Please use Geelato's MetaFactory and Fluent DSL (MetaQuery) to write Java code that queries the top 10 records from the dev_project table where status is 1." 🟢 When writing Entity classes: "Please use Geelato's ORM annotations (@Title, @Col, @Model) to define an entity class named SysUser with id, name, and loginName fields." 🟢 When integrating frontend APIs: "Based on Geelato's MQL syntax, construct a JSON request body for paginated queries on the user table (gl_user) with a join on the department table (gl_org)." 🟢 When retrieving the current user: "In a Spring Boot Controller, how do I get the current request's tenantCode and userId using Geelato's SecurityContext or Global Context?"

If you need the AI to better understand a Geelato project, you can paste the following context: "This project is built on the Geelato Framework, a metadata-driven foundation that supports adaptive seamless switching between multiple databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle. Direct SQL or MyBatis XML is NOT recommended for database operations. Instead, use the built-in ORM (via MetaFactory for FluentDSL) or the JSON-based MQL syntax. The project's security context is usually handled by the unified authentication module. For API design, refer to the SrvExplain API specification." Next Step: If you are new here, we suggest jumping straight to 👉 Quick Start.
This page explains how to start a new Geelato-based project from scratch and keep the first integration focused on the framework foundation instead of platform-heavy extensions.

Item Requirement JDK 17 (java -version) Maven 3.8+ (mvn -v) Maven repository A repository with credentials that can resolve cn.geelato artifacts, or build from source (see below) Port 8081 is free Note: some environments inject variables such as SERVER__PORT; Spring Boot relaxed binding lets them override server.port in the config file. Check with env | grep -i SERVER or pass --server.port=8081 explicitly.

The framework is currently distributed as 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT through a private Maven repository; no Geelato artifacts are available on Maven Central yet. Without repository credentials the build fails at BOM import with Non-resolvable import POM: cn.geelato:geelato-framework-bom:pom:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT. The repository URL, settings.xml snippet, and credential request process are shared with the scaffold guide — see Artifact Repository and Credentials. Precheck command: mvn -B dependency:get -Dartifact=cn.geelato:geelato-framework-bom:pom:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT

Without private-repository access, the minimal chain (BOM + starter and its core dependencies, 10 self-contained core libraries) can be built from the public source: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/geelato-projects/geelato-community-backend.git cd geelato-community-backend mvn -B install -DskipTests -pl geelato-framework-bom,geelato-lang,geelato-utils,geelato-security,geelato-meta,geelato-core,geelato-orm,geelato-web-common,geelato-framework-starter -am After the build succeeds, the 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT artifacts are in your local repository and no private repository is needed.

Import geelato-framework-bom Add geelato-framework-starter Start from geelato-sample-quickstart Verify the primary datasource, JdbcTemplate, Dao, ORM, and one sample endpoint Move to geelato-app-scaffold once the project needs ready-to-use backend services Add runtime, designer, or business extensions only after the minimal path is stable

The fastest verification is running the official minimal sample (in-memory H2, no external dependencies): # 0. Prerequisites: JDK 17, Maven 3.8+; a repository that resolves Geelato artifacts (or a local source build) git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/geelato-projects/geelato-hello-example.git cd geelato-hello-example/geelato-sample-quickstart # 1. Build mvn -B clean package # 2. Start (port 8081) java -jar target/geelato-sample-quickstart-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --server.port=8081 # 3. Verify curl -sS http://localhost:8081/api/sample/ping Expected output: {"msg":"sample quickstart is ready","code":20000,"status":"ok","data":{"app":"geelato-sample-quickstart","frameworkStarter":true,"database":"h2"},"cache":null} The sample consists of 4 files: a standalone POM (no parent), a bootstrap class, one /api/sample/ping controller, and application.properties. Copy them into your own project to complete the minimal integration.
documents.s: Run the Minimal Sample in 5 Minutes

documents.t: Without cloning the sample repository, create a project with 4 elements: POM snippet (the version must be resolvable through the repository setup above): <dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>cn.geelato</groupId> <artifactId>geelato-framework-bom</artifactId> <version>${geelato.version}</version> <type>pom</type> <scope>import</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> </dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>cn.geelato</groupId> <artifactId>geelato-framework-starter</artifactId> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>com.h2database</groupId> <artifactId>h2</artifactId> <scope>runtime</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> application.properties (spring.datasource.primary.jdbc-url is a hard prerequisite for the starter auto-configuration; without it startup fails with NoSuchBeanDefinitionException(primaryJdbcTemplate)): server.port=8081 spring.application.name=geelato-sample-quickstart spring.datasource.primary.name=primary spring.datasource.primary.jdbc-url=jdbc:h2:mem:geelato_sample;MODE=MySQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;DATABASE_TO_UPPER=false spring.datasource.primary.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver spring.datasource.primary.username=sa spring.datasource.primary.password= Bootstrap class (any package covered by @SpringBootApplication default scanning; no extra configuration needed): package com.example.demo; import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication; import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication; @SpringBootApplication public class DemoApplication { public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args); } } Sample endpoint (@ApiRuntimeRestController adds the /api prefix and the unified JSON convention automatically): package com.example.demo; import cn.geelato.lang.api.ApiResult; import cn.geelato.web.common.annotation.ApiRuntimeRestController; import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier; import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping; import java.util.LinkedHashMap; import java.util.Map; @ApiRuntimeRestController("/api/sample") public class SampleHelloController { private final JdbcTemplate primaryJdbcTemplate; public SampleHelloController(@Qualifier("primaryJdbcTemplate") JdbcTemplate primaryJdbcTemplate) { this.primaryJdbcTemplate = primaryJdbcTemplate; } @GetMapping("/ping") public ApiResult<Map<String, Object>> ping() { Map<String, Object> payload = new LinkedHashMap<>(); payload.put("database", primaryJdbcTemplate.queryForObject("select 'h2'", String.class)); return ApiResult.success(payload); } } Use the same build/start/verify commands as above.
documents.s: Build a Minimal Project from Scratch

documents.t: At the beginning, keep only: geelato-framework-bom geelato-framework-starter one primary datasource driver a Spring Boot web application Do not start with: platform-specific upload runtime designer-side metadata governance message, market, schedule, or similar extensions heavy platform capabilities that require extra middleware Dependency size note: geelato-framework-starter transitively brings GraalVM JS (~58 MB) and the Redis client; the minimal fat jar measures about 120 MB (starter runtime deps ~117 MB / 126 jars, plus the H2 driver declared by the host). Seata, Atomikos, and JDBC drivers are now optional — an H2-only project no longer carries the MySQL driver, and JTA dependencies stay out of the package; add geelato-web-platform-extras (one dependency) to restore them all. The "do not start with" list means don't add platform modules on top of the starter, not that the current dependency tree is already tiny.

The current starter wiring is triggered by spring.datasource.primary.jdbc-url, and it creates these default beans: primaryDataSource primaryJdbcTemplate primaryDao (of type cn.geelato.core.orm.Dao; inject by bean name) dbGenerateDao (also a proxied Dao; note it is not a separate DbGenerateDao type) If spring.datasource.secondary.jdbc-url is also provided, the secondary beans (secondaryDataSource / secondaryJdbcTemplate / secondaryDao) are created as well, without bean ambiguity against the primary ones.

The official minimal sample is geelato-sample-quickstart, which uses: geelato-framework-starter an in-memory H2 datasource JTA and Seata proxy disabled by default (ORM binds dynamicDao automatically, no extra configuration) Its purpose is to prove that the framework foundation can be consumed independently. Transaction note: JTA and the Seata proxy are disabled at the Geelato layer (the corresponding configuration keys are not loaded unless set to true), and the Atomikos / Seata dependencies themselves are optional — a minimal project no longer has Atomikos on the classpath, so no Atomikos output appears in startup logs and no ./atomikos-logs/ directory is created. Add com.atomikos:transactions-spring-boot3-starter to restore JTA.

If the project already needs these baseline backend capabilities: login MQL organization and user management dictionary upload do not keep growing the minimal sample. Move to: geelato-app-scaffold Its role is to be the official ready-to-start scaffold, not the minimal verification sample.
documents.s: When to Switch to the Scaffold

documents.t: The shortest successful path should verify the following 5 criteria, each directly testable: Criterion Verification the application starts console shows Started ... in X.XXX seconds and Tomcat started on port(s): 8081 the primary datasource is available /api/sample/ping returns data.database = "h2" JdbcTemplate can be injected the ping controller injects it via @Qualifier("primaryJdbcTemplate") (the app starting at all proves this) Dao can be injected inject @Qualifier("primaryDao") Dao dao and run dao.nativeQueryForObject("select 1", new Object[0], String.class) which returns 1 one runtime endpoint can be called curl -sS http://localhost:8081/api/sample/ping returns code: 20000 To verify bean wiring and ORM step by step, temporarily add a probe controller to the project: package com.example.demo; import cn.geelato.core.orm.Dao; import cn.geelato.lang.api.ApiResult; import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Qualifier; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping; import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController; @RestController public class BeanProbeController { private final Dao primaryDao; public BeanProbeController(@Qualifier("primaryDao") Dao primaryDao) { this.primaryDao = primaryDao; } @GetMapping("/api/probe/orm") public ApiResult<String> probe() { return ApiResult.success(primaryDao.nativeQueryForObject("select 'orm-ok'", new Object[0], String.class)); } } curl http://localhost:8081/api/probe/orm returning orm-ok proves ORM auto-configuration is active. The minimal starter ships neither actuator nor OpenAPI — 404s on /actuator/* and /v3/api-docs are expected.
If you want to build a real business project with ready-to-use backend services, read App Scaffold Quickstart MetaStore Extension

Geelato Framework provides two standard approaches to start a project. Whether you are building a new application from scratch or integrating Geelato into an existing Spring Boot project, you can choose the path that best fits your needs.
documents.s: Quick Start: Two Ways to Bootstrap

documents.t: Dimension Method 1: App Scaffold (Recommended) Method 2: Minimal Integration Positioning An out-of-the-box "fat scaffold" that provides a production-ready backend skeleton. A "thin starter" that only introduces foundational dependencies with minimal intrusion. Use Case New projects starting from scratch, needing a complete backend management capability instantly. Existing Spring Boot projects, or when you only need ORM/MQL capabilities. Capabilities Included Base foundation + Login, Org, User, Role, Dictionary, File Upload, MQL, and auto table initialization. Only base Web configuration, primary DB setup, dynamic datasource entry, JdbcTemplate, and ORM base setup. Dependency geelato-app-scaffold-starter geelato-framework-starter Database Tables Automatically detects and initializes about 17 platform tables (e.g., dict, user, role) on startup. Zero table requirements. You decide what tables to create. Dev Rhythm Minimal configuration. You can start writing business entities and CRUD right away. You need to build your own login interceptors, permission checks, attachment logic, etc.

If you are building a brand new backend system: 👉 Strongly recommended: App Scaffold Quickstart. It saves you the time of building foundational modules so you can focus on business logic on day one. If you are refactoring an old project, or only want to use a specific Geelato feature (like FluentDSL): 👉 Choose Minimal Integration. This method won't force any platform tables into your database, nor will it hijack your login system.
Please choose the corresponding guide based on your decision: 🚀 Method 1: App Scaffold Quickstart 🌱 Method 2: Minimal Integration
本页汇总 Geelato 使用中的高频问题。每条答案均可在对应章节找到更详细的说明。

两种标准方式（见 快速开始）： 脚手架启动（geelato-app-scaffold-starter）：开箱即用的"胖脚手架"，自动初始化约 17 张平台基础表，提供登录、组织、用户、角色、字典、上传、MQL。适合从零开始的新项目。 最小化接入（geelato-framework-starter）：仅引入底层依赖的"瘦启动"，零建表要求、对现有项目侵入最小。适合已有 Spring Boot 项目，或仅需使用 ORM/MQL 能力。
documents.s: Q1. 框架有哪两种启动方式？如何选择？
documents.h: #q1-框架有哪两种启动方式如何选择

documents.t: 可以。复制后需调整 groupId/artifactId/version、启动类包名与 scanBasePackages、spring.application.name、数据库连接，并保留对 geelato-app-scaffold-starter 与 geelato-framework-bom 的依赖。需区分："项目起步形态"可复制示例工程，但"后续公共能力升级入口"仍应依赖 Starter 与 BOM，而非与官方示例目录长期手工同步。 详见 脚手架快速启动指南。
documents.s: Q2. 可以直接复制 geelato-app-scaffold 示例工程作为业务项目起点吗？
documents.h: #q2-可以直接复制-geelato-app-scaffold-示例工程作为业务项目起点吗

documents.t: 当项目明确需要登录、MQL、组织与用户、字典、上传等基础后台能力时，不建议继续在最小样例上扩展，应直接采用 geelato-app-scaffold。其定位是可直接开工的官方脚手架，而非最小样例。 详见 新项目最小接入。

documents.t: 两者解决不同层级的问题：MQL 面向前端与平台协议侧，用 JSON 描述查询与写入；Fluent DSL 面向后端 Java 服务，用 MetaFactory 链式调用访问数据。推荐边界：页面、平台通用控制器、低代码场景用 MQL；后端标准 CRUD、轻量 join、过程调用用 Fluent DSL；超复杂 SQL 或复杂结果映射用原生 SQL / MyBatis。 详见 MQL。

documents.t: 本页汇总 Geelato 文档中的专有术语，按领域分组。每条给出定义并链接到详解页面，便于在阅读其他章节时快速对照。
平台侧基于 JSON 的元数据查询与操作协议，面向前端页面、低代码界面与平台通用数据接口，提供统一的数据访问表达方式。与后端 Java 侧的 Fluent DSL 解决不同层级的问题。 详见 MQL、MQL 使用指引。
Object-Relational Mapping（对象关系映射）。在 Geelato 中并非单一 API，而是围绕"元数据 + 查询协议 + Java DSL + 扩展机制"组织的体系，分为注解层、协议层（MQL）、Java API 层（Fluent DSL）与扩展层。 详见 ORM。
后端 Java 服务的元数据 CRUD 入口，通过 MetaFactory 的链式 API 完成查询、保存、更新、删除、关联、过程调用与原生 SQL。它是面向 Java 服务代码的独立入口，而非 MQL 的字符串包装。 详见 Fluent DSL 指引。
后端 Fluent DSL 的统一入口类，暴露 query/insert/update/delete/procedure/sql(...) 链。需要容器中存在 Dao Bean 以自动装配执行器。
MQL 的核心处理类，暴露平台通用数据接口（/api/meta/list、/api/meta/save/{biz}、/api/meta/delete/{biz}/{id} 等）。

Dao 封装 JdbcTemplate 承载 ORM 执行。primaryDao 绑定主数据源，dynamicDao 基于路由数据源。ORM 自动解析优先绑定 dynamicDao（它是唯一能支撑 useDataSource 切库的 Dao），不存在时回退 primaryDao，再回退唯一的 Dao Bean；无需显式配置，geelato.orm.dao-bean-name 仅用于绑定其他自定义 Dao。
@Entity(connectId=...) 属性，显式声明实体所属的动态数据源 key，是实体到数据源的核心绑定点。解析优先级：@Entity(connectId) > @Entity(catalog) 映射 > 数据库元数据 connect_id > 默认主库。 详见 动态数据源、ORM 注解说明。
定义"元数据从哪里来"的 SPI（cn.geelato.core.meta.spi）。默认实现 DefaultMetaStore 从平台设计时表读取表/列/视图/校验/外键定义。属 Spring 风格 SPI，非 JDK ServiceLoader。 详见 MetaStore 扩展。
geelato-web-platform 中的装配类，在 setApplicationContext(...) 阶段完成元数据扫描与数据库元数据装载，早于 BootApplication.run(...)。
统一元数据消费者。扫描 @Entity 类（由 geelato.meta.scan-package-names 控制扫描包），解析为 EntityMeta/FieldMeta/ColumnMeta，并维护来自类与来自数据库两份元数据，通过统一缓存对外提供访问。
元数据装载完成后的二次增强入口（metaBootstrap.bootstrap(metaManager, dao)），适用于元数据补丁、启动时注册或宿主工程自定义收尾。可选。
业务实体的推荐基类，承载通用字段 id/tenantCode/creator/creatorName/updater/updaterName/createAt/updateAt，与 Fluent DSL 保存链路的默认字段填充天然配合。
将类标注为框架可识别的元数据实体。关键属性：name（实体名，默认取类名）、table（表名）、catalog（逻辑库分组/数据源路由，platform 表示受保护系统实体）、connectId（显式数据源 key）。
声明列映射或列约束（name、charMaxlength、precision、scale），在默认推导与实际不一致时使用。
为实体或字段补充 title 与 description，服务于元数据管理、界面展示与文档理解。
标记不参与持久化的运行时属性，仍可参与 Java 业务逻辑，但不映射到数据库列。 详见 ORM 注解说明。
Geelato Web 平台的运行时应用壳，基于共享底座 geelato-web-platform 启动，面向业务执行场景。Spring Boot 启动类，继承 BootApplication。 详见 PlatformWebRuntime。
cn.geelato.web.platform.boot.BootApplication，Geelato Runtime 的启动编排器（非 Spring Boot 最外层入口）。其 run(...) 完成数据源定义缓存、SQL/DB 脚本、Graal 上下文、环境配置缓存的收尾初始化。业务启动类继承它。 详见 启动过程。
请求级（线程级）安全上下文。硬约束：安全主体只能在鉴权成功后由安全链路内部写入。 详见 安全上下文。

cn.geelato.core.GlobalContext，平台底层全局运行参数入口，承载环境标识、系统密级（环境变量 GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL，五档：0 开发级/1 基础级/2 标准级（默认）/3 增强级/10 严格级，4-9 预留视同 3）、匿名登录开关（环境变量 GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED）、列加密/API 加密开关、加密算法与密钥读取等。 详见 全局上下文。
为每次请求生成并透出的统一流量标记 trafficTag，用于灰度标识、链路透传、日志关联与在线用户观察。默认两档语义：default、gray。当前仅做标记，不内置网关分流。 详见 流量染色。
租户隔离字段。约定通过 Tenant-Code 请求头传递（未提供时默认 geelato），新增时自动填充。

将平台默认规则从底层模块抽离、改为在上层工程通过 SPI 显式接入： 查询过滤 SPI（MqlQueryFilterInjector、FluentQueryFilterInjector）：向查询链路自动注入租户、权限、组织等条件。 字段填充 SPI（MqlSaveFieldValueFiller、FluentSaveFieldValueFiller、EntitySaveFieldValueFiller）：向保存链路自动补齐审计字段。 运行时统一规则：0 个实现跳过、1 个实现按 isEnabled() 生效、多个实现直接报错。 详见 查询过滤与字段填充 SPI 扩展。

documents.t: 插件机制基于 PF4J 实现，宿主工程仅依赖扩展点接口（PluginExtensionPoint 继承自 org.pf4j.ExtensionPoint），插件实现可独立打包、按需启停，由 SpringPluginManager 管理并通过 PluginBeanProvider 调用。 详见 插件机制概览。
基于 geelato-app-scaffold-starter 的"胖脚手架"，开箱即用提供登录、组织、用户、角色、字典、文件上传、MQL 与自动建表，适合从零开始的新项目。与"瘦启动"最小化接入（geelato-framework-starter，零建表）相对。 详见 脚手架快速启动指南、快速开始。
从源码静态扫描控制器、生成逐 Controller Markdown 的接口补充说明，用于补充尚未完全 OpenAPI 化的端点。与 OpenAPI、MQL 构成"标准契约 / 静态补充 / 平台协议"的双轨/三轨关系。 详见 API Reference。
平台业务异常的统一基类体系。每个错误码对应一个 CoreException 子类，异常响应会携带错误码、文案以及 docUrl 文档链接与 logTag 关联键，便于排障定位。 详见 错误码参考。
异常响应中指向排障文档的字段。规则：错误码未声明 docSlug 时指向错误码参考页对应锚点（.../error-codes#{code}）；声明 docSlug 时指向独立详情页（.../error-codes/{slug}）。可通过 GlobalContext.__DocUrlEnabled__ = false 关闭。
异常发生时生成的一次性关联键，写入异常响应与日志。通过日志搜索接口按 logTag 反查，可定位到该次异常的完整上下文日志。详见 报障排查。
贯穿单次请求全链路的追踪标识。以 traceId 在请求日志、业务日志、数据层日志之间串联，可还原一次请求的完整调用链。详见 报障排查。
本页说明 Geelato 的日志体系、报障定位主工作流，以及常用调试工具，帮助快速定位线上问题与开发期故障。
定位一次故障所需的最小信息： 账号：loginName（优先）或 userId。 故障时间段：精确到秒，建议取 5–30 分钟窗口。
层 内容 访问日志 请求入口、响应结果、耗时、状态码。 业务日志 关键业务动作（新增/更新/删除/审批/消息发送）。 异常日志 统一异常模型、错误码、关联键。 安全日志 认证授权、失败原因、来源 IP（敏感信息脱敏）。 数据层日志 DAO 执行、动态数据源切换、慢操作告警。
请求与异常日志统一携带以下关联字段，用于串联链路： traceId、requestId、userId、loginName、tenantCode、uri、method、status、durationMs、errorCode、logTag。 其中 traceId 贯穿单次请求全链路，logTag 是异常发生时生成的一次性关联键，二者是排障的核心抓手（见 术语表）。
INFO：关键业务成功路径、请求摘要、数据源切换成功。 WARN：可恢复异常、参数不合法、外部依赖抖动、降级行为。 ERROR：业务失败或系统异常，必须带 traceId/logTag/errorCode。 DEBUG：排障临时信息，默认关闭，避免生产噪音。
password、token、authorization、apiKey、secret、accessToken、refreshToken 等字段必须脱敏；禁止打印完整凭证、私钥、会话密钥、明文密码。推荐打印掩码摘要（前 4 后 4）与上下文（IP、账号、路径、时间）。

按账号与时间段查询请求日志： GET /api/run/log/searchByUserTime?userId={userId}&from={from}&to={to} 时间格式：yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS。 from/to 缺省时默认最近 24 小时。 返回结果包含 file、lineNumber、lines。 在返回结果中找到 traceId、logTag、uri、status、errorCode。 若有 logTag，按其反查异常上下文： GET /api/run/log/search?tag={logTag} 以 traceId 在请求日志、业务日志、数据层日志之间串联，还原完整调用链。
先看请求日志的 uri / status / durationMs，判断是否慢请求或错误返回。 再看异常日志中的 errorCode / logTag，区分业务异常与系统异常。 最后看 DAO / 动态数据源日志，确认 SQL 与数据源切换是否异常。
平台通过 p6spy 记录实际执行的 SQL，关键配置（见 系统配置）： decorator.datasource.p6spy.enable-logging=true decorator.datasource.p6spy.log-file=/log/p6spy-sql.log 排查 SQL 问题时优先查看该日志文件，确认实际下发的 SQL 与参数。
后端 Fluent DSL 可在不执行的情况下预览生成的 SQL（见 Fluent DSL 指引）： toSql()：预览查询 SQL。 toCountSql()：预览计数 SQL。 用于排查关联、分页、条件拼接是否符合预期。

MQL Playground 是交互式的 MQL 调试与校验工具，通过配置开启： geelato.mql.playground.enabled=true 提供以下能力（挂在 /api/mql 下）： POST /api/mql/explain：MQL → SQL 预览（无需数据源）。 POST /api/mql/validate：校验 MQL 语法。 POST /api/mql/execute：针对主库真实执行（需 primaryJdbcTemplate）。 GET /api/mql/entities、GET /api/mql/schema/{entity}：查看实体与字段元数据。 GET /api/mql/scenarios 等：场景化回归套件（带 schema 初始化与清理）。 执行类操作支持 runAs 模拟身份，使租户隔离与数据权限注入器按生产等效方式生效，便于复现带权限上下文的查询问题。
业务异常通过 CoreException 体系统一管理，异常响应会携带： errorCode、默认文案。 docUrl：指向排障文档。未声明 docSlug 时指向 错误码参考 对应锚点；声明 docSlug 时指向独立详情页（如 SQL 执行异常）。 logTag：用于按上文工作流反查日志。 通过 docUrl 可从前端错误提示直接跳转到对应排障文档。

本地开发需直连生产主库时，若 platform_dev_db_connect 中的 host/port 为内网地址，可在不修改表数据的前提下通过 Host/Port 映射文件重写： 默认路径：应用运行目录下 conf/db-host-map.txt。 或通过环境变量指定：GEELATO_DS_HOST_MAP_FILE=/path/to/db-host-map.txt。 适用于通过公网、VPN 或 SSH Tunnel 连接生产库的场景。 详见 动态数据源：内网 Host/Port 映射。

症状 定位方法 按账号查不到数据 扩大时间窗；确认账号口径（优先 loginName，再试 userId）。 只有请求日志、无异常日志 检查 status 与 durationMs，可能是慢请求或前端中断。 ES 短时不可用 系统会降级、不阻塞业务；优先查本地文件日志。 MQL 报实体不存在 / 查不到业务实体 确认业务包已加入 geelato.meta.scan-package-names 与 scanBasePackages（见 FAQ）。 动态数据源切换不生效 确认热刷新已同时执行 Registry 与 RoutingDataSource 两步刷新（见 FAQ）。 保存后审计字段未自动填充 确认字段填充 SPI 实现唯一且 isEnabled() 返回 true（见 FAQ）。 启动报 NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException（MetaStore） 自定义实现加 @Primary（见 FAQ）。 SPI 注册后报 IllegalStateException 同一类 SPI 存在多个实现，收敛为单个（见 FAQ）。 重启后表结构未自动更新 auto-init-tables 仅首次建表，不做 ALTER（见 FAQ）。
错误码参考 术语表 常见问题 MQL 使用指引 Fluent DSL 指引 动态数据源：内网 Host/Port 映射

The maintenance module targets teams building on top of Geelato and provides two sets of development-time self-check tools: Entity three-way sync check and repair (cn.geelato.metasync): checks consistency between "Java entity class ↔ entity definition (platform_dev_table) ↔ physical table structure" and repairs toward a chosen baseline. MQL Playground (cn.geelato.mqltest): online MQL debugging and test suite with explain preview, real execution, identity simulation and scenario-based regression. Module coordinates: cn.geelato:geelato-maintenance, already included by the quickstart; not a scaffold standard part — add the dependency explicitly in business projects.

The module registers two Spring Boot auto-configurations, each controlled by its own switch, both off by default: Switch Controls Default geelato.meta.sync.enabled Three-way sync tool (page + REST) false geelato.mql.playground.enabled MQL Playground (page + REST) false The quickstart application.properties sets both to true with a note that they should be false in production. Tool page paths are pre-allowed by the security interceptor defaults.

The "three sides" are three forms of the same entity. Manual changes on any side (table DDL, class annotations, designer edits) can drift from the others.
