This page describes the complete flow of packing an application into a .zgdp: pre-pack gates, the three packing modes, the artifact pipeline, and download & upload. The UI entry is the app version management page in the IDE; the endpoints below can also be called directly. PackageController is a plain @Controller (no /api prefix) branching between v1/v2 by geelato.package.engine; the version management API AppVersionController lives under /api/app/version.

Before writing the package, two checks run after data query; either failing aborts hard and no package is produced: App exists: appId must resolve to a platform_app row, otherwise error 60001. Column consistency: the physical columns of each table (the column set of select *) must match the entity definition (EntityMeta fields). Physical columns missing from the entity definition raise 60002 "pack validation failed: physical table and entity definition are inconsistent, packing is blocked". :::note Why the gate exists Rows packed with select * that carry columns absent from the target platform's entity definition would always fail deployment validation. Intercepting at pack time surfaces the problem in the source environment — sync the table structure in the model designer (or drop the redundant physical columns) and pack again. ::: A version name may be passed or omitted; when omitted it is generated as <appCode>_versionyyyyMMddHHmmss. Version uniqueness per app+tenant+version applies (POST /api/app/version/validate, called automatically by the pack dialog).

GET/POST /package/packet/{appId}, optional version, description: Carries all rows of this app from the 19 whitelisted platform tables plus all rows of business tables with pack_bus_data > 0. Calling without extra parameters is whole-app packing — the regular way to migrate an environment.

Same endpoint; pass appointMetas in the body ({table: "rowId1,rowId2"}) to pick metadata rows: :::warning v1 and v2 differ v1 (default engine): appointMetas is a whitelist — listed tables are packed by the selected rows, unlisted tables are excluded entirely (only the package header remains). v2: appointMetas selects rows — listed tables are packed by the selected rows, and unlisted tables are still packed in full. Check the engine value before a partial delivery to avoid a package that differs from expectations. ::: platform_app is unaffected by appointMetas and always travels as the package header.

GET/POST /package/packet/merge, body {version: {table: "rowId1,rowId2"}}: Reads and parses the registered package files version by version. Merges only entities listed in appointMetas; an empty string selects zero rows for that entity. Deduplicates rows by id within the same entity across versions. Produces a new package and registers it (default description "package produced by comparison merge"). Typical scenario: run a version comparison in the version management page first, then merge several incremental deliveries into one package. The merge only deduplicates by row id and performs no cross-entity reference consistency check.

Internal execution order of a pack request: Build the query map: 19 platform tables + business tables (business table names validated against ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$ against injection). Query this app's data table by table; the platform_app row feeds the package header. Column-consistency check (above). Serialize the whole package with fastjson2 (with the LargeObject feature to support large packages). Write <geelato.package.path>/<appCode>/<appCode>.gdp. Compress into <version>.zgdp, archive per tenant and app, and register as an attachment. Write the app version record platform_app_version: packagePath (attachment id), source packet, status draft, pack time, tenant. Date values inside the package JSON are normalized to yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss to avoid parse failures caused by serialization differences between environments.

Action How Description Download The download button in the version management page (generic file download by attachment id); or GET /package/downloadPackage/{versionId} Yields the .zgdp file Upload Upload in the version management page (accept .zgdp) then register via POST /api/app/version/createOrUpdate; or POST /package/uploadPackage/{appId} The file lands in geelato.package.path/uploadFolder and an app version record is written After upload and registration the version can be deployed from the target environment's version list.

Endpoint Description POST /api/app/version/pageQuery Paged version query GET /api/app/version/get/{id} Version detail GET /api/app/version/package/{id} Read the version's package data (AppPackData) POST /api/app/version/createOrUpdate Register/update a version (called after upload) POST /api/app/version/validate Version uniqueness check DELETE /api/app/version/isDelete/{id} Delete a version record

Sensitive data travels as-is: rows are packed with select * and no masking is applied to platform_app.app_key/token or datasource connection strings; treat package files as sensitive data in delivery and storage. Dependencies are not pulled in: depend_app_code is a declaration only; depended-on apps must be ready in the target environment (see Packaged Contents & Runtime Roles). File binaries are not packed: platform_resources carries metadata rows only. Versions start as draft: status flips to deployed after a successful deployment; backup versions are generated automatically by v2 deployments (version suffix _backup). Dedicated log routing: pack/merge/deploy logs are routed by logger name cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.pack into ${LOG_DIR}/pack/, including per-table row counts and timings.

Deploying Application Packages: validation, persistence and activation on the target environment Packaged Contents & Runtime Roles: what each table in the package does at runtime System Configuration: Package Module: the geelato.package.* keys

This page explains the event-bus capability in: cn.geelato.web.common.event inside geelato-web-common. The current model has four core classes: BusinessEvent EventPublisher GlobalEventBus EventBusListener Its goal is to decouple "what business action happened" from "what follow-up work should run afterwards".

The event bus is suitable for: async follow-up work after a business action completes decoupling core business logic from notification, audit, or side synchronization attaching extension behavior without polluting controllers or main services serving as a trigger point for SSE, notifications, and audit logging Compared with ORM events, this model is more focused on: web or application-layer events domain action completion async extension after business operations instead of only DAO save/delete hooks.

This is the abstract base class of all business events. It provides: getEventCode() handle() sourceClass sourceMethod So one event object is both: a business event carrier a holder of its default handling action
This is the unified publishing entry: EventPublisher.publish(event) It checks initialization, logs event metadata, and delegates actual publishing to GlobalEventBus.
This is the wrapper around Spring event broadcasting. It depends on: ApplicationEventMulticaster and publishes through: eventMulticaster.multicastEvent(event)

This is the built-in global listener. It uses: @EventListener @Async("eventExecutor") to receive BusinessEvent and invoke: event.handle() So the current default semantics are: business code publishes the event Spring broadcasts it the event is handled asynchronously in the event executor

The recommended way is: create a class that extends BusinessEvent add the business fields you need implement getEventCode() implement the actual consumption logic in handle() Example: public class OrderCreatedEvent extends BusinessEvent { private final String orderId; private final String userId; public OrderCreatedEvent(Object source, String orderId, String userId) { super(source); this.orderId = orderId; this.userId = userId; } @Override public String getEventCode() { return "order.created"; } @Override public void handle() { // audit, notification, push, side synchronization, etc. } }
documents.s: How To Define Your Own Event

documents.t: Once the event is defined, publish it from business code: EventPublisher.publish(new OrderCreatedEvent(this, orderId, userId)); Typical publish points include: after a controller completes a key action after a service completes a domain action after business success when follow-up work can be asynchronous

In the current abstraction, the most direct subscription model is not multiple custom listeners first. The default model is: publish the event let the bus broadcast it let the built-in listener call event.handle() let the event define its own default handling logic This is simple and practical, but if one event later needs many fully independent subscribers, you may need to split responsibilities further or extend the listener model.

The event bus and SSE fit together very naturally. A recommended chain is: a business action happens publish a BusinessEvent in handle(), convert the event into an SSE message send it through SseHelper or SseEmitterManager let the frontend receive it through EventSource('/subscribe/{topic}') or /subscribe/topic/all Example structure: public class OrderCreatedEvent extends BusinessEvent { private final String orderId; public OrderCreatedEvent(Object source, String orderId) { super(source); this.orderId = orderId; } @Override public String getEventCode() { return "order.created"; } @Override public void handle() { // convert the business event into an SSE push // SseHelper.sendToTopic("order", new SseMessage(...)); } } This keeps: controller or service code free from direct SSE details business events separated from frontend transport decisions future replacement of SSE with another transport easier
documents.s: How To Combine It With SSE

documents.t: Use this distinction: event bus: describes what happened inside the backend SSE: describes what should be pushed to connected clients So the recommended flow is: publish a business event first decide in the event handling stage whether it should become an SSE push

keep getEventCode() stable and readable, such as order.created avoid putting overly heavy long-running logic into handle() add proper logging and fallback when the event logic calls external systems let SSE stay downstream of business events, not the other way around

The current event bus is a business-event abstraction built on Spring ApplicationEventMulticaster: BusinessEvent defines the event contract EventPublisher is the unified publish entry GlobalEventBus broadcasts the event EventBusListener consumes it asynchronously and invokes handle() Developers can use it to: define their own business events publish them asynchronously after business completion implement audit, notification, synchronization, and SSE push logic in handle() That makes it a good fit for: application-layer event extension backend internal propagation backend trigger entry for server-push via SSE
SSE Subscription Push Traffic Tagging Authentication and Authorization

This page explains: cn.geelato.core.GlobalContext in geelato-core. It currently acts as a low-level global runtime entry for: environment flag security level column-encryption and API-encryption switches default encryption algorithm AES / SM4 / SM2 / RSA key loading

GlobalContext centralizes runtime values that many low-level components need to read consistently, such as: which environment the system is in whether column encryption is enabled whether API encryption semantics are enabled which encryption algorithm is currently selected where the current algorithm keys come from
The code currently defines: __Environment__ = "development" and exposes it through: GlobalContext.getEnvironment()

The security level is a deployment-level protection grading, configured through an environment variable: GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL an integer from 0 to 10, default 2 illegal values (non-numeric or out of range) fail at startup read once at class-loading time and fixed afterwards Level definitions: Code Name Column Encryption API Encryption Anonymous Login 0 Development off off on 1 Basic on off on 2 (default) Standard on on on 3 Enhanced on on on 4-9 Reserved (same as 3) on on on 10 Strict on on off Derived rules: column encryption: enabled when level ≥ 1 (getColumnEncryptOption()) API encryption: enabled when level ≥ 2 (getApiEncryptOption())

The anonymous login channel is decided by: the environment variable GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED when set explicitly, accepting true / false (case-insensitive); illegal values fail at startup otherwise by the security level: on when level < 10, off when level ≥ 10 (getAnonymousOption()) The cache switch __CACHE__ depends on whether the environment is product.

The following items are explicitly supported through environment variables: GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED GEELATO_ENCRYPT_TYPE GEELATO_AES_KEY GEELATO_SM4_KEY GEELATO_SM2_PUBLIC_KEY GEELATO_SM2_PRIVATE_KEY GEELATO_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY GEELATO_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY The rule is: use the environment variable first when it exists and is non-empty otherwise fall back to the built-in default value

The following items are still static constants in the current code: __Environment__ __ColumnEncrypt__ (derived from the security level) __ApiEncrypt__ (derived from the security level) So the accurate statement for the current repository state is: encryption algorithm and keys already support environment variables security level and the anonymous switch support environment variables (GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL / GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED) the environment flag is still a static constant column-encryption and API-encryption switches are derived from the security level and cannot be set independently
documents.s: What Is Not Yet Environment-Variable Driven

documents.t: The default algorithm is read through: GlobalContext.getEncryptType() which prefers: GEELATO_ENCRYPT_TYPE EncryptUtils currently supports: aes rsa sm2 sm4 Encryption uses the current global algorithm, while decryption reads the algorithm prefix from the stored value itself. Stored encrypted values look like: aes:xxxx rsa:xxxx sm2:xxxx sm4:xxxx
documents.s: How To Choose the Encryption Algorithm

documents.t: GEELATO_AES_KEY
GEELATO_SM4_KEY
GEELATO_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY GEELATO_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY RSA encryption uses the public key and decryption uses the private key.
GEELATO_SM2_PUBLIC_KEY GEELATO_SM2_PRIVATE_KEY The current implementation requires both keys for SM2 operations.

Security level and anonymous channel example (production with heightened confidentiality): $env:GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL="3" $env:GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED="false" Classified deployment closing the anonymous channel: $env:GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL="10" PowerShell example for RSA: $env:GEELATO_ENCRYPT_TYPE="rsa" $env:GEELATO_RSA_PUBLIC_KEY="your-public-key" $env:GEELATO_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY="your-private-key" AES example: $env:GEELATO_ENCRYPT_TYPE="aes" $env:GEELATO_AES_KEY="your-16-char-key"
Column encryption is first guarded by: GlobalContext.getColumnEncryptOption() which is derived from the security level (on when level ≥ 1). Under the default level 2, it is enabled.

A field is not encrypted only because the global switch is on. The real per-field condition is: ColumnMeta.encrypted = true Only fields marked as encrypted in metadata enter the encryption path on save.
In JsonTextSaveParser, the save flow: checks GlobalContext.getColumnEncryptOption() iterates fields calls EncryptUtils.encrypt(...) only for fields whose ColumnMeta.isEncrypted() is true

At read time, CommonRowMapper calls: EncryptUtils.decrypt(...) for string values. If the value matches the algorithm:ciphertext pattern, it is decrypted by the prefixed algorithm. Otherwise it is returned as-is. So: encrypted values can be automatically decrypted plain string values are not broken

set GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL according to the deployment scenario (the default 2 suits general commercial production) explicitly close the anonymous channel in production (GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED="false") inject real keys through environment variables in production define GEELATO_ENCRYPT_TYPE explicitly mark only truly sensitive columns as encrypted=true do not confuse "global column encryption enabled" with "all columns are encrypted"

Although GlobalContext exposes concepts such as environment, security level, and API encryption, their externalization levels differ: algorithm and keys are externalized through environment variables security level and the anonymous switch are externalized (GEELATO_SECURITY_LEVEL / GEELATO_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED) the environment flag is still a static constant column-encryption and API-encryption switches are derived from the security level and cannot be set independently

Slow multi-table queries can be served by materialized views maintained by an external engine: writes still go to the source database (MySQL), the engine incrementally syncs and materializes the query result, and once enabled, queries on the view land directly on the materialized view — with zero changes to caller queries (transparent switching). The framework is engine-neutral: orchestration, metadata, routing and the read-only gate are unaware of the concrete engine. Engines (the first being RisingWave) plug in as adapters; replacing or adding engines later does not affect callers or existing views.

MySQL source tables (write path unchanged) | ingestion channel (engine-specific; RisingWave reads binlog via mysql-cdc) v External engine: ingestion channel -> materialized view (incrementally maintained, seconds-fresh) ^ | same-name materialized copy row in platform_dev_view (connect_id=engine connection) existing queries (/api/meta/list, MQL, dao) — the view name stays the same; when multiple same-name rows are loaded, MetaManager registers the materialized one first, so the entity's connectId points to the engine and routing flows through the existing dynamic datasource chain Placement and semantics: Data Where it lives Engine connection one platform_dev_db_connect row (e.g. db_type=risingwave) Original view the original platform_dev_view row is left untouched (default/custom/virtual as before) Materialized copy a new same-name materialized row in platform_dev_view: copies the original view data, changing only connect_id to the engine connection, view_type=materialized, view_construct=**the original definition SQL** (written with source table names; query building does not consume it for materialized — still queried by the physical view name), view_column=introspected column JSON Metadata registration with multiple same-name rows, MetaManager registers the materialized one first (regardless of load order); after disabling (soft-deleting the copy row) the original view takes over registration again Ingestion channel / backfill progress not persisted platform-side — the engine is the source of truth, introspected live :::info Why same-name dual records A materialized view is an acceleration copy of an existing view, not a new view: the original view row keeps the full definition and rollback capability; the same-name dual rows make entity registration a natural "materialized-first" routing takeover with zero caller changes. The view type options in the view management UI remain default/custom/virtual only — materialized views are managed via a switch in the "Materialized View" tab of the original view's editor. ::: Freshness semantics: ingestion is incremental CDC (seconds to minutes); queries read eventually consistent data, and results are incomplete while the initial backfill is running (status=BACKFILLING). Queries that cannot tolerate this should disable the materialized view (queries immediately fall back to the original view). Read-only hard failure: while enabled, write operations (save/insert/update/delete, etc.) on the view entity throw an explicit exception at the Dao layer; write to the source tables instead. Dialect resolution: when the view entity has no connectId of its own, its dbType inherits the dialect of the subject entity; the actual execution connection is resolved from the entity's connectId (the materialized copy row points to the engine connection). Engine dialect aliases registered at runtime (e.g. risingwave) are normalized to a dialect family via Dialects; SQL dialects are generated per the execution connection, decoupled from the metadata annotation.
documents.s: How It Works (dual records + materialized-first loading)

documents.t: Design-time API prefix /api/model/mv (DesignTime). Register the engine connection first via /api/model/connect. On the frontend, the whole flow is driven by a switch in the "Materialized View" tab of the view editor.

POST /api/model/mv/precheck { "engineConnectId": "engine connection id", "originConnectId": "MySQL source connection id", "tables": ["orders", "customers"], "viewName": "v_order_summary", "database": "optional, defaults to the source connection db_name" } Returns every check as an item (does not abort midway): engine adapter, source connectivity, binlog_format=ROW, binlog_row_image=FULL, REPLICATION SLAVE/CLIENT grants, source tables exist, view-name status on the engine.

POST /api/model/mv/view/create { "engineConnectId": "engine connection id", "viewName": "v_order_summary", "originConnectId": "MySQL source connection id", "tables": ["orders", "customers"], "originSql": "select o.id, o.amount, c.name from orders o join customers c on o.customer_id = c.id", "database": "optional", "recreate": false } Write originSql with source table names (the frontend pre-fills the original view's construct); the framework first expands view references in the statement into their underlying physical tables (mysql-cdc can only ingest physical tables), then lexically rewrites table references to the engine-side ingestion table names, creates the materialized view, introspects columns, and inserts/updates the same-name materialized copy row (the definition SQL is persisted into view_construct). Ingestion channels are named deterministically from (source connection + database + view), one channel per view — each physical table gets its own CDC ingestion table (RW 2.x/3.x API); repeated calls are idempotent and appending tables is naturally supported (a table-list change only creates the missing tables). With recreate=false, an existing same-name materialized view in the engine is reused directly (re-enabling after a disable skips backfill); recreate=true drops and recreates (rebuild after a definition change; backfill restarts). The response contains both originSql/engineSql definitions, the column list and the backfill status.
documents.s: 2. view/create — enable (engine creates the materialized view + the copy row)

documents.t: POST /api/model/mv/view/status { "engineConnectId": "engine connection id", "viewName": "v_order_summary" } Queries the engine catalog live: READY, BACKFILLING (results incomplete), NOT_EXISTS, or UNKNOWN (engine-version differences; progress unparseable), plus the current definition in the engine (definition) and the platform-side enablement (enabled).

POST /api/model/mv/view/disable { "viewName": "v_order_summary" } Soft-deletes the materialized copy row — queries immediately fall back to the original view; the engine-side materialized view and ingestion channel are kept, and re-enabling (view/create with recreate=false) reuses them without backfill. The cost of a misoperation is near zero.

POST /api/model/mv/view/drop { "viewName": "v_order_summary", "dropSource": "optional", "originConnectId": "required when dropSource", "database": "optional" } Engine dropView + soft-delete of the copy row; with dropSource=true the ingestion channel is dropped as well (fails with a hint if other materialized views still reference it).

Two steps to add an engine; the framework (orm/core knows no concrete engine type) and callers stay untouched: implement the adapter cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.mv.engine.MaterializedViewEngine (a Spring Bean claiming connections via supports(dbType)): ingestion channel, view DDL, status and column introspection, drops; every failure must fail hard with locatable context; at startup the adapter declares its JDBC shape via Dialects.registerAlias(dbType, built-in dialect family) (e.g. RisingWave registers as the postgresql family) — driver, URL template, pooling and connection testing all follow the family automatically, with zero framework branch changes. For the prerequisites and specifics of the first engine, see RisingWave Engine.

RisingWave is the first engine adapter of the materialized view acceleration framework: PostgreSQL protocol (default port 4566), a native mysql-cdc connector that reads the MySQL binlog directly to build ingestion channels, and incrementally maintained materialized views.

Source database (MySQL): binlog_format=ROW and binlog_row_image=FULL (checked item by item by /api/model/mv/precheck) the ingestion account needs REPLICATION SLAVE and REPLICATION CLIENT grants (GRANT REPLICATION SLAVE, REPLICATION CLIENT ON *.* TO ...) source tables must have primary keys (required by CDC) RisingWave must be able to reach the source database over the network Engine connection: register it via /api/model/connect with db_type=risingwave, db_schema set to public (or the schema where materialized views are created), default port 4566. At startup the adapter automatically registers risingwave as a postgresql dialect family alias (Dialects.registerAlias), so the driver, URL template, pooling and connection testing all follow the PG family — the framework layers contain no RisingWave concept.

Two-stage (RW 3.0 API): ① CREATE SOURCE {channel} WITH (connector='mysql-cdc', hostname, port, username, password, database.name) — connection definition only, no table list (the 1.x table.name.list is deprecated, and the single-table CDC CREATE TABLE is disabled); ② per physical table CREATE TABLE {channel}_{table} FROM {channel} TABLE '{db}.{table}' (FROM is followed directly by the source name, no SOURCE keyword) — the schema is derived automatically by the engine, no column definitions or type mapping needed Channel names gl_{connection_id}_{database}_{view_name} (one channel per view); each table attaches to the shared source independently, so appending tables is naturally supported (a table-list change only creates the missing tables) Source tables must have a primary key (the CDC upsert key); the engine reports on creation otherwise (with context in the error) Disable/drop: dropSource first drops the prefixed CDC tables, then the shared source the mysql-cdc server.name takes the channel name, which is naturally unique channels do not support appending tables: if an existing channel does not cover a requested table, the call fails hard with remediation hints (DROP SOURCE first, or use a different database/table combination)

Engine system catalogs (rw_sources / rw_relations / rw_materialized_views) and backfill-progress columns vary across versions; the adapter parses whatever columns are actually returned and reports UNKNOWN when progress is unparseable (never guesses). Channel/view DDL is centralized inside the adapter, so engine upgrades only affect that file. After pointing to a new engine version, run a precheck plus a view/create smoke test first.

Once enabled, the platform side uses "same-name dual records": the original view row stays untouched, plus a same-name view_type=materialized copy row pointing to the engine connection (see Materialized View Acceleration); when multiple same-name rows are loaded, MetaManager registers the materialized one first, so the entity's connect_id points to the engine and queries reach RisingWave through the existing dynamic datasource routing chain. limit N offset M pagination, double-quoted identifiers and the count wrapper are all compatible with RisingWave, and the query builder has no engine branches. Materialized view names are uniformly lowercase (matching the view-row afterSet folding). Writes are intercepted by the platform read-only gate and never reach the engine.

This page describes how the platform supports both: topic-based SSE subscription all-topic SSE subscription The goal is to let clients subscribe to one business topic precisely, or observe all pushed topics from one aggregated stream.

The platform already exposes a topic subscription endpoint: GET /subscribe/{topic} It also reserves an all-topic endpoint: GET /subscribe/topic/all The latter needs to be fully implemented so that it can return a working SseEmitter instead of staying as a placeholder.
Keep and complete: GET /subscribe/{topic} Requirements: returns text/event-stream validates non-empty topic cleans up the subscription automatically on lifecycle end
Implement: GET /subscribe/topic/all Clients can consume it directly: const source = new EventSource('/subscribe/topic/all'); This allows one connection to receive events from all topics.
The controller should explicitly declare: produces = "text/event-stream" and expose: topic subscription: /subscribe/{topic} all-topic subscription: /subscribe/topic/all
SseEmitterManager should add a global subscriber collection such as: allSubscribers and support: subscribeAll() lifecycle cleanup callbacks removal of failed subscribers on send errors

When sendToTopic(topic, message) is called, the message should be delivered to: subscribers of the given topic all-topic subscribers This preserves current topic-based behavior while adding aggregated subscription naturally.
Responsible for: managing topic -> emitters mapping managing the all-topic subscriber set registering onCompletion, onTimeout, and onError reclaiming invalid subscribers on send failure
Provides lightweight wrapping methods such as: subscribe(String topic) subscribeAll() to keep the calling style consistent.
Exposes HTTP endpoints: GET /subscribe/{topic} GET /subscribe/topic/all and returns SseEmitter.

path: GET /subscribe/{topic} return type: text/event-stream fit for listening to one business topic such as orders, notifications, or job status Example: const source = new EventSource('/subscribe/news');
path: GET /subscribe/topic/all return type: text/event-stream fit for aggregated notifications, monitoring, or debugging Example: const source = new EventSource('/subscribe/topic/all');
Even without running the full site, these checks are still recommended.
Validate SseEmitterManager by: creating one topic subscriber creating one all-topic subscriber calling sendToTopic(topic, message) confirming that both subscription paths receive the delivery
lifecycle callbacks clean up connections correctly send failure removes only the invalid subscriber empty collections are cleaned up to avoid memory growth

This capability does not change the existing topic subscription path. It only adds: all-topic subscription more complete cleanup and broadcast logic So it is a compatible enhancement rather than a breaking change.

This page describes how the platform generates, resolves, and exposes a request-level trafficTag so it can later support gray release, filtering, forwarding, interception, and online-user observation. The current plan starts with two common values: default gray But the implementation should still allow extension to any valid tag string.

Traffic tagging aims to: generate or recover a trafficTag for every request persist the tag in a cookie expose the tag through a response header keep the tag in server-side request context show the latest active trafficTag on the online-user card support filtering online users by trafficTag

Current rules are: use both Cookie and Header as carriers allow manual override only in non-product environments sign the cookie value fall back and overwrite on signature validation failure provide tagging capability first, without implementing business-side traffic routing yet

A dedicated configuration class should centralize: enabled tagCookieName tagHeaderName overrideHeaderName overrideQueryName defaultTag cookie path, domain, maxAge, httpOnly, secure signingEnabled signingSecret mdcKey requestAttributeKey This keeps protocol details and runtime settings out of scattered business code.
Provide a request-scoped context holder for the current trafficTag, so it can be read consistently from: interceptors services async submission points

Responsible for: generating signatures validating signatures validating tag format A recommended choice is: HmacSHA256 with a strict tag pattern to prevent unsafe values from entering cookies, headers, or logs.

Responsible for resolving, falling back, and issuing tags when a request arrives. Recommended priority: manual override in non-product environments existing cookie with valid signature default tag, then issue a new cookie The final tag should be written to: TrafficTagContext request attribute MDC response header Set-Cookie when refresh or issue is needed
The most suitable integration point is DefaultSecurityInterceptor.

Traffic tagging should run at the beginning of preHandle, before: the @IgnoreVerify early return path This ensures even unauthenticated endpoints still receive a consistent trafficTag. It should also guarantee: tagging failures only degrade gracefully and never block the normal security flow
At request completion, it should clear: TrafficTagContext the trafficTag entry in MDC to prevent thread reuse from leaking context values across requests.
Traffic tagging should also feed the online-user observation capability.

Online user details should add: trafficTag and Redis online-state records should store the tag from the most recent active request. The target outcome is: each item returned by /api/online/list includes trafficTag

The online-user card should: display trafficTag use tag styles to distinguish default and gray provide filters for All / default / gray Filtering only affects display and should not change polling or refresh behavior.

After a request passes through traffic tagging, the response should ideally include: Set-Cookie: gl_traffic_tag=... X-Gl-Traffic-Tag: default|gray In a non-product environment, if the caller specifies: X-Gl-Traffic-Override: gray or: ?glTrafficTag=gray the response should return: X-Gl-Traffic-Tag: gray and write the matching cookie back.
Focus on: tagging logic running before security early return cleanup in afterCompletion fallback to the default tag and cookie rewrite when signature validation fails
Focus on: whether online-state updates include trafficTag whether /api/online/list returns trafficTag whether the frontend card can display and filter by trafficTag

At this stage, the goal is to provide a unified tagging capability and an observation capability, not to immediately implement gray-routing strategies inside every business service. In other words, the current phase focuses on: how the tag is generated how the tag is exposed how the tag is stored how the tag is observed from the management side Gateway routing, service forwarding, or business interception based on the tag can be extended in later phases.
This page describes how to define extension points, implement plugins, package them, and call them from the host application. The current recommended split is: contract layer implementation layer
Shared extension contracts should live in: geelato-plugin-all This layer normally contains: PluginExtensionPoint business extension interfaces shared DTOs and metadata classes

Concrete plugin modules live in projects such as: geelato-example-plugin geelato-ocr-plugin They typically contain: plugin main class plugin Spring configuration extension implementation classes plugin.properties
Example: public interface Greeting extends PluginExtensionPoint { String getGreeting(); }
The current example uses SpringPlugin and creates its own Spring ApplicationContext.
Example plugin configuration provides plugin-local beans such as GreetingService.
Add @Extension to the concrete class so PF4J can discover it.
The current example contains: plugin.class plugin.dependencies plugin.id plugin.provider plugin.version

The plugin module should: depend on plugin-all enable org.pf4j.processor.ExtensionAnnotationProcessor write plugin metadata into the jar manifest After packaging, the jar should contain: META-INF/extensions.idx META-INF/MANIFEST.MF plugin.properties

The host application should use: PluginBeanProvider Example: Greeting greeting = pluginBeanProvider.getBean(Greeting.class, "example-plugin"); String result = greeting.getGreeting(); If no matching extension is found, the runtime throws: UnFoundPluginException
Overview Loading, Start/Stop and Uninstall Plugin Repository
This page explains how the current runtime uses the plugin directory, what is supported by the management API, and how to understand uninstall in the current implementation.

The runtime builds SpringPluginManager from: geelato.plugin.pluginDirectory The default value is: plugins So the basic loading model is still directory-based: plugin jars or directory-style plugins must be placed into the configured plugin directory.
The current controller exposes: GET /api/pm/list GET /api/pm/switchStatus GET /api/pm/log GET /api/pm/clearLog
/api/pm/list returns fields such as: id version description provider dependencies state enabled

/api/pm/switchStatus currently supports: status=enable status=disable Internally it uses: pluginManager.startPlugin(pluginId) pluginManager.stopPlugin(pluginId) So current public runtime management is focused on start/stop, not full install/delete workflows.

The current runtime does not publicly expose: unloadPlugin deletePlugin upload-and-install APIs So uninstall should be understood in two layers: runtime disable: stop the plugin physical removal: stop it, remove the jar or plugin directory, then restart the application
Plugin logs are written under: plugins/logs The runtime can: read plugin logs clear plugin logs through /api/pm/log and /api/pm/clearLog.
Overview Definition and Development Plugin Repository

This page describes the current Geelato plugin mechanism, its main runtime roles, and the difference between source modules and deployed plugin directories. The mechanism currently consists of: runtime plugin management extension point contracts plugin implementation projects In the current repository these are represented by: runtime plugin integration in geelato-web-runtime/.../plugin shared plugin contracts in geelato-plugins/geelato-plugin-all concrete plugins such as geelato-example-plugin, geelato-logging-plugin, and geelato-ocr-plugin
Creates: SpringPluginManager UpdateManager and initializes plugin paths from: geelato.plugin.pluginDirectory geelato.plugin.pluginRepository with defaults: plugins plugins/repository
Business code uses PluginBeanProvider to resolve an extension by: extension interface type pluginId
The current management APIs are exposed under: /api/pm/* including: GET /api/pm/list GET /api/pm/switchStatus GET /api/pm/log GET /api/pm/clearLog
Plugin source modules live in: geelato-plugins This is the build workspace, not the runtime deployment directory.
Actual deployed plugins live in: plugins This directory may contain: plugin jars directory-style plugins repository metadata files plugin logs

Shared extension contracts are defined through: PluginExtensionPoint which extends: org.pf4j.ExtensionPoint Concrete plugin APIs then extend PluginExtensionPoint, such as: Greeting This keeps the host application coupled to contracts instead of plugin implementation classes.
Definition and Development Loading, Start/Stop and Uninstall Plugin Repository
This page explains the current repository-related configuration and the meaning of: geelato.plugin.pluginDirectory geelato.plugin.pluginRepository
The defaults are: pluginDirectory = plugins pluginRepository = plugins/repository They serve different purposes.
This is the actual runtime plugin root directory used for loading and managing deployed plugins.
This is the repository metadata directory used by the update manager.
The current workspace already contains: plugins/repositories.json plugins/plugins.json These files describe: repository entries plugin release lists
The current sample defines a folder repository with: id url pluginsJsonFileName
The current sample defines plugin releases with: id description releases and each release includes: version date url

The runtime already creates: UpdateManager so repository support is reserved in the current implementation. However, the code does not yet expose a full public management workflow for: browsing repositories installing from repository updating plugin versions online So the safest current interpretation is: repository metadata and update-manager infrastructure exist practical deployment still mainly relies on packaging and copying plugins into the plugin directory

平台 Web 层（Controller）的统一规范：分页参数解析、异常处理。规范的目标是同一套参数约定、同一套异常链路；端点由各控制器自行声明，BaseController 只提供参数捕获与工具能力（不带任何内置端点）。
Controller 不写 try-catch。业务异常直接抛出，由全局异常处理器 PlatformExceptionHandler 统一处理（见下文"异常处理约定"）。 分页/过滤参数解析统一走 ParameterOperator（BaseController 已继承），不自造参数名。
参数 规范名 兼容别名（按优先级） 说明 页码 pageNum current（旧 POST body）、page 同时出现时规范名优先 页大小 pageSize limit 单页上限 1000 排序 orderBy order（旧 POST body） | 分隔符替换为空格，如 create_at|desc 新接口一律使用规范名；旧接口传历史别名同样可解析。

入口 未传页码/页大小时的默认值 语义 POST body（pageQuery 链路） pageNum=1、pageSize=10 分页查询 GET query（query 链路） pageNum=-1、pageSize=-1 不分页、全量查询（QueryCommand.hasPagination() 以 > 0 判定） GET 链路的全量语义是既有行为：未传分页参数即要求全量。显式传 -1 或 0 会被拒绝（见下）。
参数**非整数、非正数、页大小超上限（1000）**时不做静默纠正，直接抛 InvalidPageParamException（错误码 10005，HTTP 400），文案包含参数名与实际传入值，便于调用方自助修正： 分页参数 pageSize=abc 不是有效整数 分页参数 current=0 必须为正整数 分页参数 pageSize=5000 超出上限 1000
沿用 字段名|操作符 键值约定，由 getFilterGroup(entityClass, requestBody, true) 统一解析为 FilterGroup（按实体字段名过滤，未知操作符报错）： { "userName|contains": "张", "createAt|bt": "2026-01-01,2026-12-31", "enableStatus": 1 }
Controller 方法内不捕获异常、不拼装失败响应。历史写法（catch (Exception e) { log.error(...); return ApiResult.fail(e.getMessage()); }）已废弃——它会吞掉异常，使全局处理器的排障机制全部失效。

异常统一由 PlatformExceptionHandler（@RestControllerAdvice）处理： 异常类型 HTTP 状态 响应 CoreException（业务异常基类） 按 getHttpStatus()（鉴权类 401/403/400，默认 500） ApiResult.fail(PlatformErrorResult, 友好文案) ConstraintViolationException（JSR-303） 400 字段错误明细 其他 Exception（兜底） 400 透出 ex.getMessage()（无消息时"系统异常：类名"） 所有分支均携带 logTag 反馈凭据：文案末尾追加 （错误码 xxx，反馈凭据 xxx），异常完整堆栈异步落库到 platform_exception_log（id=logTag），用户报障凭截图即可在服务端检索根因。
HTTP 状态码：语义化（401/403/400/500），错误分支（axios catch）同样解析响应体。 业务码：ApiResult.code，20000 为成功、-2 为失败（历史成功码即 20000）。 响应体结构（msg/code/status/data）在成功与失败路径保持一致。
需要向前端反馈可恢复的业务错误（如"登录名不能为空"）时，抛 CoreException 子类（httpStatus=400），不要返回 ApiResult.fail(...)（后者 HTTP 200，不符合语义化状态码约定）。

端点由控制器自行声明（@ApiRestController + @RequestMapping），BaseController 不提供内置端点。 调用 getFilterGroup 的方法签名需声明 throws ParseException。 两个控制器不能使用相同的类级路径前缀（父子前缀如 /dict 与 /dict/item 不冲突）。历史上 /api/meta 曾由运行态/设计态两个控制器"方法分家"共存，属遗留隐患，已合并为单一 MetaController（运行态 + 设计态接口分区，category 用中性的 platform）。

业务 Service 若声明比父类更窄参数边界的方法（如 DictItemService.updateModel(DictItem) 携带"禁用联动子项"逻辑），会与 BaseService 的泛型 <T extends BaseEntity> updateModel(T) 构成重载而非覆盖——调用点经 BaseService 静态类型分派时将静默绕过业务逻辑。 Controller 内调用以具体 Service 类型（如 dictItemService）声明，让编译器解析到最具体的重载； BaseSortableService 的 createModel/updateModel/isDeleteModel 已改为真正覆写（原窄边界声明构成重载，经父类引用调用会绕过 seqNo 初始化与删除标记）——新增类似 Service 方法时勿重蹈。
documents.s: 业务 Service 重载分裂陷阱

documents.t: 旧风格控制器（无参方法 + 手动解析 + 方法内 try-catch）按以下步骤迁移： 逐方法去除 try-catch 包装，方法体保留原逻辑（端点声明不动）。 getFilterGroup 调用需在方法签名补 throws ParseException。 行为变化点（需与前端确认）：失败路径从 HTTP 200 变为语义化状态码；msg 末尾追加错误码与反馈凭据；成功路径响应完全不变。

参数捕获基类：cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.BaseController（继承 ParameterOperator） 分页解析与防护：cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.ParameterOperator 全局异常处理：cn.geelato.web.platform.run.PlatformExceptionHandler 试点示例：DictItemController、UserController（去 try-catch 形态）、MetaController（运行态+设计态合并）、AuditLogController（独立 REST 风格，参数命名与异常约定与本规范一致）

This page maps the modules in the geelato-community repository by layer. Framework-layer modules are consumed directly by host projects and backend developers; platform-layer modules form the low-code platform runtime and shells and ship with the platform application.
Shared contracts, API result models, and low-level annotations.
Shared utility capabilities and cross-module helpers, including the unified local cache LocalBoundedCache.
Security contracts and context model (User, Org, Role, Permission, Tenant, etc.).
Curated BOM for framework consumers, aligning framework module and third-party dependency versions.
Unified starter for the foundation modules, forming the minimal base. Capabilities with strong implementation preferences ship as optional dependencies.

The framework kernel: metadata model, MQL engine, SQL builder, and ORM runtime management, plus the global context (GlobalContext/SessionCtx), the datasource registry (DataSourceManager), and experiment gates.

Fluent DSL (MetaFactory chained CRUD), command execution, and ORM event hooks for backend developers, with the dynamic datasource capability under cn.geelato.datasource (routing datasource, DynamicDataSourceScope switching, entity resolution, p6spy SQL logging defaults).

General-purpose script engine SDK: GraalVM Polyglot sandbox, the @GraalService kit registry, the six built-in kits ($gl.sql/$gl.mql/$gl.http/$gl.encrypt/$gl.ctx/$gl.parameter), and engine revision snapshots. See Script Engine.
Platform-layer modules are not part of the framework minimal base; they ship with the platform application.

Module Responsibility geelato-meta Platform entities and metadata definitions (apps, pages, dictionaries, messages, attachments, etc.) geelato-web-common Web-level shared support: filters and interceptors, Shiro/OAuth2 integration, the token authentication SPI (TokenAuthenticator), traffic marking, online users, log routing geelato-web-oss Object storage abstraction and providers (built-in Alibaba Cloud implementation)

Module Responsibility geelato-web-runtime Runtime application shell (PlatformWebRuntime) geelato-web-designer Designer application shell (PlatformDesginer) geelato-web-platform Shared platform base (controllers + services + boot) geelato-web-platform-extras Optional heavy-dependency feature pack: OCR, Office-to-PDF, 7zip, Elasticsearch, JGit, seata, atomikos, JDBC drivers geelato-app-scaffold-starter Starter that assembles runtime base services for scaffold applications geelato-web-quickstart Platform boot host (full feature set); the platform starts from this module by default

Module Responsibility geelato-search-api / geelato-search-lucene Search abstraction (SearchEngine port) and the embedded Lucene engine (NRT + ngram contains, async event indexing, failure compensation, reconciliation, reindex) geelato-exception Business exception center: rule library, instances, handling steps, trails, notification records, scan records geelato-alert Business alert center: alert rules, notification templates, silence windows, alert records geelato-mail Personal mailbox client: IMAP receive, SMTP send, filters, labels, signatures, vacation replies, contacts geelato-maintenance Built-in maintenance: entity three-way sync validation and compensation, MQL test suites and online debugging toolchain

Module Responsibility geelato-archive-policy / geelato-archive-engine Archive policy management and archive engine (two-phase reconciled moving, scheduling, restore); self-contained, introduced per project, not part of the platform standard set geelato-mcp MCP services (common/fms/platform submodules); not part of the aggregate build, install separately Sibling repositories Workflow (geelato-workflow), dynamic integration (geelato-dyn, Karaf/OSGi), packaging (geelato-package) live in separate repositories; see the dedicated chapters

SecurityContext must be written only after successful authentication in the security chain DynamicDataSourceScope is the single entry point for datasource switching; primaryDao never routes, and dynamicDao remains higher priority than primaryDao for compatibility fallback Upload capabilities with strong implementation preferences stay outside the minimal starter base and ship as optional dependencies guarded by the platform feature pack

ORM Overview, ORM Annotations, Fluent DSL Guide Dynamic Datasource Sample skeleton: geelato-sample-quickstart (in geelato-hello-example) Runtime / Designer shells: PlatformWebRuntime, PlatformDesginer

平台业务错误码以 public static final int ERROR_CODE 常量定义在各异常类（CoreException 子类）中，异常构造时传入码值与文案；本页是错误码的登记清单与唯一对照表。异常响应（ApiResult.data）携带 docUrl 字段，指向本页对应锚点或独立详情页，便于快速定位排障文档。 本页描述的是平台错误码（Java 异常类体系）。基于规则引擎的「业务异常」（异常实例、告警工单）是另一套机制，见 业务异常。

按码值查表：接口返回的 code（或 msg 中的"错误码 xxxx"）→ 按下方分段规则定位类别段 → 在对应表格中查错误说明与解决方法 凭反馈凭据排障：需要技术详情时，取 msg 末尾的反馈凭据（logTag），调用 GET /api/exceptionLog/byTag/{logTag} 查看该次异常的完整技术消息与堆栈；完整排障流程见 排障指南 docUrl 直达：异常响应自带 docUrl 字段，直接跳转到本页对应错误码行或独立详情页 20xxx 段为常规业务事件（登录/权限），不落服务端日志、响应不带反馈凭据

段位 类别 说明 10xxx 数据与解析 MQL / SQL / GQL 的解析与执行 20xxx 认证 / 授权 / 会话 登录、令牌、权限、租户 30xxx 文件处理 文件上传、校验、读取 40xxx 插件 插件治理与调用 50xxx 系统通用 兜底系统异常（透出详细错误消息） 60xxx 应用打包与部署 低代码应用的打包、部署、回滚 70xxx 数据归档 归档策略校验、对账、并发冲突 同类错误跨模块归入同一段，模块重构不影响码段；前端可凭段位判断错误大类。
documents.s: 分段规则（按错误类别，不以模块为维度）
documents.h: #分段规则按错误类别不以模块为维度

documents.t: public class UnauthorizedException extends CoreException { public static final int ERROR_CODE = 20005; public UnauthorizedException() { this("未授权访问，请登录"); } public UnauthorizedException(String message) { super(ERROR_CODE, message); } @Override public int getHttpStatus() { return 401; } // 默认 500，仅鉴权类覆写 } CoreException 仅持有码值；HTTP 状态码（getHttpStatus()，默认 500）与文档 slug（getDocSlug()，默认 null）通过可覆写方法按需提供 无参构造传入的文案即用户可见文案（getUserMessage() 默认取 errorMsg） 用户文案末尾由 PlatformExceptionHandler 追加排障凭据，如：数据操作失败，请稍后重试（错误码 10002，反馈凭据 123456789012345678） 是否记录日志由异常类定义者决定（shouldLog()，默认 true）：覆写为 false 的异常属常规业务事件（如鉴权不通过），处理器跳过 log.error 与 platform_exception_log 落库，响应不带反馈凭据、msg 为纯文案——见 20xxx 认证/授权/会话类

异常响应（ApiResult）按职责分层，用户看到友好文案的同时技术详情可直接取到： msg（前端直接展示）：CoreException.getUserMessage() 友好文案 + 排障凭据 data.errorMsg：同友好文案（不含 SQL/参数/堆栈） data.stackTraceDetail：技术详情 = 异常技术消息（如 SQL 执行异常的"原因/执行SQL/参数/数据库错误码"）+ 完整堆栈，默认随响应下发；GlobalContext.setLogStack(false) 可关闭（仅隐藏本字段，不影响 msg/errorMsg） 反馈凭据即 logTag：技术详情同时写入服务端错误日志（${LOG_DIR}/error/，凭 logTag= 检索），并异步持久化到 platform_exception_log 表（catalog=platform-log，默认主库，可配置独立日志库）——运维凭 GET /api/exceptionLog/byTag/{logTag} 直接查询该次异常的完整详情（结构化前缀 + 技术消息 + 堆栈），无需登服务器；GET /api/exceptionLog/page 支持按错误码/应用/租户/时间分页排查

documents.t: 错误码定义在各异常类的 ERROR_CODE 常量中；本页码表为登记清单，新增错误码必须同步登记（新增码在对应类别段段尾顺延）。 码值全局唯一性靠本页登记表约束（无编译期/运行期强制检测）；新增前先查本页避免重复。 码值是前后端契约：前端存在按码值的分支逻辑（如 20001 弹租户选择、30016 下载错误文件、20002 静默处理），调整码值必须前后端同步发布，并同步更新本页。 未接入 CoreException 体系的异常（如 McpException、ScriptExecutionException）不占用码段，以文末体系外异常附表形式登记。

异常响应中的 docUrl 按以下规则生成（baseUrl 为 https://docs.geelato.cn）： 异常类未覆写 getDocSlug()：{baseUrl}/docs/reference/error-codes#{code} —— 指向本页对应锚点。 异常类覆写了 getDocSlug()（如 SqlExecuteException 返回 sql-execute）：{baseUrl}/docs/reference/error-codes/{slug} —— 指向独立详情页。 关闭文档跳转：将 GlobalContext.__DocUrlEnabled__ 设为 false，异常响应不再输出 docUrl 字段。
documents.s: 错误码与文档链接规则

documents.t: 码值 异常类 错误说明（默认文案） 常见原因与解决方法 10001 cn.geelato.core.mql.parser.JsonParseException 请求解析失败，请检查数据格式 请求体不是合法 JSON（格式错误、转义错误、编码问题）。检查请求体 JSON 格式与 Content-Type 10002 cn.geelato.core.orm.SqlExecuteException（根码） 数据操作失败，请稍后重试（docSlug=sql-execute，独立详情页：sql-execute） SQL 执行异常的根码，实际返回由 1002x 分类工厂按根因细分为具体子码；未分类故障的兜底为 10028，根类不再直接作为兜底返回值 10003 cn.geelato.core.sql.InvalidFilterFieldException 实体[实体名]的过滤字段[字段名]不存在（文案含 operator 与 scene 信息） 查询条件中的过滤字段不在实体元数据中（字段名拼写错误、字段未定义或未发布）。对照实体定义修正过滤字段名 10004 cn.geelato.web.platform.utils.GqlResolveException 请求解析失败，请检查表达式 GQL 表达式语法错误或无法解析。检查表达式写法与引用的字段/函数是否存在 10005 cn.geelato.core.mql.parser.InvalidPageParamException 分页参数非法（文案含参数名与实际值，HTTP 400） 分页参数为非整数等非法值。按提示改为合法整数；pageSize=-1 表示全量查询，数值越界会被自动钳制到有效区间不报错 10006 cn.geelato.lang.exception.UnSupportedVersionException 当前版本不支持该操作 预留码（当前无抛出点）。出现时升级平台或应用至支持该操作的版本 10007 cn.geelato.core.mql.ViewTemplateParamException 实体[实体名]收到@pf参数[参数列表]，但[原因]。@pf参数仅支持虚拟视图（virtual）类型视图实体 对非 virtual 类型的视图实体使用了 @pf 模板参数。将该视图实体改为虚拟视图（virtual），或移除 @pf 参数（见 MQL 文档的 @pf 模板参数说明）

码值 异常类 判定依据 错误说明（用户文案） 常见原因与解决方法 10021 SqlConnectionException 取连接失败、sqlState 08xxx（PG 08001/08003/08006）、Communications link failure/Connection refused 数据库连接中断，系统正在自动恢复，请稍后重试 数据库不可达或连接池耗尽。稍后重试（系统自动恢复）；频繁出现时检查数据库可用性、连接池配置与网络 10022 SqlLockConflictException MySQL 1213/1205、sqlState 40001、PG 40P01（死锁）/55P03（锁不可用） 当前数据正被其他操作占用，请稍后重试 行锁/表锁竞争或死锁。稍后重试；频繁出现时排查长事务、未提交事务与并发更新热点 10023 SqlDuplicateKeyException MySQL 1062、PG 23505 数据已存在，无法重复提交 唯一键/唯一索引冲突（重复提交、业务键重复）。改为更新已有数据，或调整业务键后重试 10024 SqlConstraintViolationException MySQL 1451/1452、sqlState 23xxx 段（PG 23503 外键/23502 非空/23514 CHECK） 数据存在关联引用或不符合约束，请检查后重试 外键引用存在（如删除被引用数据）、非空约束、CHECK 约束不满足。按业务含义补齐或清理关联数据后重试 10025 SqlDataTooLongException MySQL 1406、sqlState 22001（PG string_data_right_truncation） 字段[字段名]的内容超出长度限制，请缩短后重试 字段值超过列长度定义。按文案中的字段名缩短内容，或调整表字段长度 10026 SqlDataOutOfRangeException MySQL 1690、sqlState 22003（PG numeric_value_out_of_range） 字段[字段名]的数值超出允许范围，请调整后重试 数值超出列类型范围或 CHECK 约束。按字段名调整数值/精度 10027 SqlDataFormatException MySQL 1366（值/字符集非法）、1292（日期非法）、sqlState 22007/22008 字段[字段名]的数据格式不正确，请检查填写内容后重试 值与列类型不匹配（日期格式、字符集、非法字符）。按字段名修正填写格式 10028 SqlUnexpectedException 未纳入 10021~10027 分类的 SQL 故障兜底（如 MySQL 1052 用法错误、1064 语法错误、权限不足） 数据操作出现未预期错误，已记录日志，请联系管理员排查 数据库语法错误、权限不足等需开发/DBA 排查的根因。稍后重试；持续出现时凭反馈凭据（logTag）提取完整 SQL 与错误码定位 PostgreSQL 说明：PG 驱动的 getErrorCode() 恒为 0，上述 PG 判定全部依赖 sqlState。子类 docSlug 继承根类（同一详情页）。

documents.t: 本段异常均覆写 shouldLog() 为 false：属常规业务事件（过期会话、无权访问、登录流程），不是服务端错误——不写 error 日志、不落 platform_exception_log、响应不带反馈凭据（msg 为纯文案）。 码值 异常类 HTTP 状态 错误说明（默认文案） 常见原因与解决方法 20001 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.auth.LoginMultiTenantException 500 请选择租户 多租户账号登录需选择归属租户。前端凭此码自动弹出租户选择框，选择后继续登录（历史码值不变，现由登录接口直接返回） 20002 cn.geelato.web.common.oauth2.InvalidTokenException 500 令牌校验异常，请重新登录 令牌无效、过期或被顶替。重新登录获取新令牌；前端通常静默处理并跳转登录 20003 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.auth.AuthBadRequestException 400 请求参数错误（文案为具体原因，如"头像文件不能为空"） 鉴权链路参数缺失或非法。按文案补齐/修正参数后重试 20004 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.auth.AccountOperationForbiddenException 403 无权操作该用户 操作目标不是当前登录用户自身可管理的账号。切换到对应账号或由管理员操作 20005 cn.geelato.web.common.interceptor.UnauthorizedException 401 未授权访问，请登录 未登录或会话已失效。重新登录；前端自动跳转登录页 20006 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 登录凭证无效，请重新进入小程序 微信登录凭证（js_code）无效或已过期。重新进入小程序触发登录 20007 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 登录凭证已被使用，请重新获取 js_code 一次性凭证被重复消费。重新调用 wx.login 获取新凭证 20008 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 手机号授权失败，请重新授权 手机号授权凭证无效或过期。重新发起手机号授权 20009 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 绑定确认已过期，请重新发起绑定 绑定确认票据过期、签名不匹配或已消费。重新发起绑定流程 20010 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 无法获取微信身份标识，请联系管理员 小程序未绑定微信开放平台，拿不到 unionid。管理员在微信开放平台完成绑定配置 20011 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppUnauthorizedException 401 请先绑定账号 微信身份尚未绑定平台账号。先完成账号绑定 20012 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppAccountDisabledException 403 账号已停用，请联系业务员 目标账号已停用。联系管理员启用账号 20013 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppBindConflictException 409 该微信已绑定其他账号，请先解绑 同一微信只能绑定一个账号（一对一约束）。先解绑旧账号再绑定 20014 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppBindConflictException 409 该账号已绑定其他微信，请先解绑 同一账号只能绑定一个微信。先解绑旧微信再绑定 20015 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.weixin.miniapp.MiniAppRateLimitException 429 操作过于频繁，请稍后再试 登录/绑定链路触发防撞库限流。稍后重试

文件相关异常统一在 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.excel.exception 包，30000 为根码，30013-30018 为子类（30001~30012 段位未使用）。 码值 异常类 错误说明（默认文案） 常见原因与解决方法 30000 FileException（根码） 文件处理失败（可带详细信息） 文件处理通用失败。按文案中的详细信息排查 30013 FileTypeNotSupportedException 文件类型不支持 上传的扩展名/MIME 不在支持范围。更换为平台支持的文件类型 30014 FileSizeExceedLimitException 文件超出大小限制 上传文件超过大小上限。压缩或拆分文件后重新上传 30015 FileNotFoundException 文件不存在 文件已被删除/清理或路径失效。确认文件存在后重新上传 30016 FileContentValidFailedException 文件内容校验失败（前端凭此码下载错误提示文件） 导入数据校验不通过。按下载的错误提示文件逐行修正数据后重新导入 30017 FileContentIsEmptyException 文件内容为空 上传了空文件或空 sheet。填写内容后重新上传 30018 FileContentReadFailedException 文件内容读取失败 文件损坏或流读取失败。重新上传；持续失败联系管理员检查存储服务

码值 异常类 错误说明（默认文案） 常见原因与解决方法 40001 UnFoundPluginException 插件未找到 容器中不存在该插件 Bean（未安装/未注册）。确认插件已部署且正确注册 40002 PluginNotEnabledForTenantException 插件未对当前租户启用 租户级未启用该插件。在插件管理中为当前租户启用 40003 PluginNotEnabledForTenantException（平台级禁用形态） 插件已被平台级禁用 插件被平台级禁用。由平台管理员在平台级启用 40004 PluginInvocationTimeoutException 插件调用超时（文案为动态值，含插件 ID 与超时阈值毫秒数） 插件扩展方法执行超过阈值被中断（防卡死）。优化插件逻辑性能、调大超时阈值后重试 （40005 段位暂未使用。）

码值 异常类 错误说明（默认文案） 常见原因与解决方法 50001 ——（PlatformExceptionHandler.handleOtherException 兜底，常量定义于 handler） 系统繁忙，请稍后重试（msg 透出详细错误消息：ex.getMessage()；无消息时"系统异常：异常类名"） 未接入 CoreException 体系的未知异常兜底。凭响应中的反馈凭据（logTag）通过 GET /api/exceptionLog/byTag/{logTag} 查看完整堆栈定位根因

错误码常量集中定义在 cn.geelato.web.platform.srv.pack.exception.PackException（一个类 + 场景常量，v1/v2 打包部署链路共用）。 码值 常量 错误说明 常见原因与解决方法 60001 ERROR_CODE_APP_NOT_FOUND 打包-应用不存在 应用 ID/编码无效。确认应用存在后重新选择打包目标 60002 ERROR_CODE_COLUMN_INCONSISTENT 打包前校验-物理表与实体定义列不一致（pre-pack gate） 物理表结构与实体元数据出现列差异（硬失败门禁）。先对齐表结构与实体定义（刷新表结构/补列）后重新打包 60003 ERROR_CODE_PACKAGE_INVALID 部署-版本/包数据缺失或损坏 应用包内容不完整。重新打包或重新上传完整的应用包 60004 ERROR_CODE_PLATFORM_MISMATCH 部署前校验-平台版本/元数据不匹配 目标平台版本或元数据基线与包不匹配。升级目标平台或改用匹配的包版本 60005 ERROR_CODE_META_NOT_FOUND 部署中-元数据或字段在目标平台不存在 目标环境缺少包内依赖的元数据。确认目标环境已安装对应实体/字段后重试 60006 ERROR_CODE_DEPLOY_DATA_FAILED 部署中-包数据写入失败（事务回滚） 目标库写入异常。查看目标库错误日志，修复后重新部署 60007 ERROR_CODE_ILLEGAL_TABLE_NAME 表名非法（防注入校验） 实体表名含非法字符。修正实体表名（仅字母/数字/下划线）后重新打包 60008 ERROR_CODE_PACKAGE_IO 应用包文件读写失败（IO） 磁盘空间不足、文件权限或存储服务异常。检查存储环境后重试 60009 ERROR_CODE_REFRESH_CACHE_FAILED 部署成功但元数据缓存刷新失败 部署已成功，仅缓存刷新失败。手动刷新元数据缓存或重启服务保证一致性 60010 ERROR_CODE_NOT_ALLOWED 环境限制不允许操作 / 回滚无备份版本 当前环境策略禁止该操作（如生产环境），或回滚缺少备份版本。按环境策略操作或先确认备份 说明：外部依赖 geelato-package 的 PackageException 保留给 market 等外部链路，平台内打包部署链路统一使用 PackException。

错误码常量集中定义在 cn.geelato.archive.exception.ArchiveException（geelato-archive-policy 模块）。 归档引擎以"确保不误删数据"为第一目标：所有对账类失败均为硬失败中止（源库未动或整批回滚，重跑安全）， 错误信息包含表名/批次/游标/期望与实际行数等上下文，支持精确诊断（详见 platform_archive_run.error_json）。 码值 常量 错误说明 常见原因与解决方法 70001 VALIDATION_ERROR 策略校验失败（源表/列不存在、归档库连接不可达、WHERE 条件语法或安全校验不通过、保留期低于平台最小值、目标类型不支持、保护名单、同库目标同名等） 策略配置不合法。按错误信息逐项修正策略配置后重新校验 70002 SCHEMA_DRIFT 归档目标表列结构漂移（源表存在而目标缺少列，禁止静默跳列） 目标表缺少源表已有列。同步目标表结构（补齐缺失列）后重跑 70003 TARGET_WRITE_MISMATCH 归档目标写入对账不一致（载入行数或目标复核数与本批期望不符） 目标库写入丢失或多余。源库未动、零丢失，排查目标库故障（磁盘/约束/连接）后重跑安全 70004 SOURCE_DELETE_MISMATCH 源表删除对账不一致（整批已回滚，归档库数据完整） 源表删除行数与预期不符。整批已回滚，排查并发写入等干扰后重跑安全 70005 POLICY_RUNNING_CONFLICT 策略并发冲突（同策略已有运行中的 run，或运行中禁止停用/删除/修改） 同策略已有运行中的归档。等待当前 run 结束，或处理异常挂起的运行后重试

以下异常不继承 CoreException，不占用错误码分段、不输出 docUrl，在此登记备查： 异常类 模块 错误说明 常见原因与解决方法 MailAccessException（code=40903） geelato-mail 邮件 Service 无法解析当前登录用户（未登录/会话过期） 重新登录后再使用邮件功能；由 MailExceptionHandler 统一转为 ApiResult.fail(40903, msg) McpException（字符串型 errorCode） geelato-mcp-common MCP 工具调用失败 按 errorCode 与消息排查 MCP 服务端状态与工具配置 ScriptExecutionException（无码，携带 api 与 retryable 标志） geelato-web-platform（脚本） 脚本执行失败（脚本不存在、执行异常等） 按消息排查脚本定义与依赖；retryable=true 时可安全重试 DeliverException（无码） geelato-alert 告警投递失败（message 调用异常/渠道映射缺失/渲染失败） 检查告警通道配置与消息服务可用性；错误详情记录在告警记录的 error_message 列 IdeOptimisticLockException（无码） geelato-web-designer IDE 脚本乐观锁冲突：脚本版本冲突（服务端/客户端 version 不一致） 脚本已被他人修改。先 pull 最新版本，合并改动后再提交
documents.s: 体系外异常（未接入 CoreException 体系）

documents.t: 体系外异常不输出 docUrl：文末附表中的异常未接入 CoreException 体系，异常响应不携带 docUrl 字段。 兜底 handler 不带 docUrl：非 CoreException 体系抛出的异常走 handleOtherException 分支，返回 50001 并携带 logTag，但不携带 docUrl。

SqlExecuteException 在 ORM 层执行 SQL 失败时抛出。这是平台中最常见、排障信息最丰富的异常之一，因此提供独立详情页。 错误码：10002（根码，兜底未分类 SQL 错误，如语法错误、权限不足） 错误码常量：SqlExecuteException.ERROR_CODE 所在类：cn.geelato.core.orm.SqlExecuteException 文档 slug：sql-execute（docUrl 指向本页；子类继承同一 slug） 抛出位置：Dao / BaseDao 捕获 Spring DataAccessException 后经 SqlExecuteException.of(...) 分类工厂包装抛出
documents.s: 10002 SQL执行异常（根码，1002x 子类细分）

documents.t: 底层 JDBC 执行 SQL 时抛出异常（语法错误、约束冲突、连接失败、字段不存在、死锁等），由 geelato-core 的 ORM 模板统一捕获，of(...) 工厂按根因包装为对应子类（各持独立错误码），未归类返回根类。

默认（生产）不再向前端下发 SQL 语句与参数，msg 为按根因分类的友好文案，末尾追加错误码与反馈凭据（logTag）： 分类 错误码 异常类 判定依据 文案 连接中断 10021 SqlConnectionException CannotGetJdbcConnectionException、sqlState 08xxx（PG 08001/08003/08006）、Communications link failure/Connection refused 数据库连接中断，系统正在自动恢复，请稍后重试 死锁/锁等待 10022 SqlLockConflictException MySQL 1213/1205、sqlState 40001、PG 40P01（死锁）/55P03（锁不可用，NOWAIT/lock_timeout） 当前数据正被其他操作占用，请稍后重试 唯一键冲突 10023 SqlDuplicateKeyException MySQL 1062、PG 23505 数据已存在，无法重复提交 外键/约束 10024 SqlConstraintViolationException MySQL 1451/1452、sqlState 23xxx（PG 23503 外键/23502 非空/23514 CHECK） 数据存在关联引用或不符合约束，请检查后重试 数据超长 10025 SqlDataTooLongException MySQL 1406、sqlState 22001 字段[字段名]的内容超出长度限制，请缩短后重试 数值超范围 10026 SqlDataOutOfRangeException MySQL 1690、sqlState 22003 字段[字段名]的数值超出允许范围，请调整后重试 数据格式不正确 10027 SqlDataFormatException MySQL 1366/1292、sqlState 22007/22008 字段[字段名]的数据格式不正确，请检查填写内容后重试 其他（根码） 10002 SqlExecuteException 未命中上述分类（语法错误、字段不存在等） 数据操作失败，请稍后重试 10025-10027 的用户文案中的"字段名"提取自数据库根因消息（MySQL 格式 ... for column 'xxx' at row 1）；PG 消息通常不含字段名，退回通用文案（如"数据内容超出字段长度限制"）。 PostgreSQL 说明：PG 驱动的 getErrorCode() 恒为 0，PG 判定全部依赖 sqlState。 兼容性：子类均继承 SqlExecuteException（is-a 成立，与 FileException 家族同模式），既有 catch (SqlExecuteException) 代码不受影响。 示例：数据已存在，无法重复提交（错误码 10023，反馈凭据 123456789012345678）。开发模式（GlobalContext.getLogStack()=true）下，data.errorMsg 保留下方完整技术文案，便于本地排障。

documents.t: Dao 执行 SQL 前经 JdbcRetryExecutor 做有限范围的透明重试：仅当"从连接池获取连接失败"（CannotGetJdbcConnectionException，SQL 必然未发送到数据库，重新执行绝对安全）且无活动事务时，按固化策略重试 2 次（退避 300ms/800ms）。 以下情况不重试： 执行中途的连接断开（Communications link failure、sqlState 08xxx、Transient 瞬时故障等）——SQL 可能已发送甚至已提交，重试有重复执行风险，由错误码细分（10021）+ 友好文案承接，交由用户重试； 活动事务内（@Transactional、batchSave 事务模式等）——事务连接绑定与多数据源路由语义不允许 Dao 层擅自重新获取连接。
documents.s: 连接类故障的自动重试

documents.t: 唯一约束冲突（MySQL errorCode=1062，SQLState 23000）：插入了重复的主键/唯一键值。 外键约束失败（MySQL errorCode=1216/1452）：引用了不存在的父表记录。 字段不存在（MySQL errorCode=1054）：实体字段映射与数据库表结构不一致。 死锁/锁等待超时（MySQL errorCode=1205/1213）：并发事务互相等待。 连接失效：连接池连接被数据库侧关闭（透明重试后仍失败才会报到前端）。
从用户反馈文案中提取 反馈凭据（logTag），在服务端错误日志（${LOG_DIR}/error/）检索 logTag= 定位对应记录。 从日志中的技术详情提取 执行SQL 与 数据库错误码。 用提取到的 SQL 在目标数据库手动执行，复现问题。 根据数据库错误码定位具体原因（参见上节"常见原因"）。 若 SQL 涉及动态参数，对照 参数 列表核验类型与取值。

The framework now exposes metadata definition sources through the MetaStore SPI, so the platform-table implementation is no longer the only possible metadata source.
The current metadata SPI surface includes: MetaStore MetaStoreProvider MetaResourceProvider MetaBootstrap These contracts are located under cn.geelato.core.meta.spi in geelato-core.

The current module-internal default implementation is DefaultMetaStore. Its responsibility is to: load table definitions from the current platform table structure load columns, views, checks, and foreign keys return metadata definition bundles by entity name or view name This keeps compatibility with the current platform schema while opening the door for replacement.

MetaConfiguration now carried by geelato-web-runtime supports optional bean injection for: MetaStore MetaResourceProvider MetaBootstrap If the host application provides those beans, MetaManager uses them before continuing with package scanning, database metadata parsing, and optional bootstrap logic.

Custom MetaStore implementations are appropriate when: the project does not use the default platform metadata tables metadata comes from a configuration center metadata comes from JSON, YAML, or the file system metadata must be composed from multiple sources at startup
Keep responsibilities separate: MetaStore: metadata definition source MetaResourceProvider: resource source MetaBootstrap: startup-time metadata initialization
Core Modules Minimal Integration

This page explains how to extend Geelato through query filter SPI and save field fill SPI. These extension points are typically used for three kinds of tasks: inject platform-level filters such as tenant, permission, or organization constraints into query flows fill default values such as creator, updater, tenant code, or timestamps into save flows replace platform default rules in the host project instead of modifying the framework kernel directly The common goal is to move platform rules out of geelato-core / geelato-orm and make them explicit SPI integrations in upper-layer projects.
documents.s: Query Filter and Field Fill SPI Extension

documents.t: Start with this page if you want to: make MQL or Fluent DSL queries automatically include tenant, permission, or organization filters fill audit fields, tenant fields, or organization fields automatically during save plug custom platform rules into different host projects This page is not the best starting point if you only need to: append one temporary condition inside a specific business method switch datasource for a single query listen to save events for notifications, sync jobs, or mirror writes In those cases, read these first: ORM / Datasource Extension ORM Event Features

Before writing code, separate the scenario clearly: affect query behavior: use a query filter SPI affect save behavior: use a field fill SPI affect MQL: choose the MQL SPI affect Fluent DSL: choose the Fluent DSL SPI affect entity save flow: choose the entity-save SPI These entry points look similar, but they run at different positions in the execution chain. Picking the wrong one is the fastest way to end up with code that never runs.
documents.s: First Choose The Right Extension Type

documents.t: The current responsibility split is fixed: geelato-core / geelato-orm keep SPI contracts only keep context objects and runtime resolvers only do not hold platform default tenant, permission, or field-fill rules geelato-web-platform holds platform default implementations holds platform business rules If your project needs different behavior, implement or replace the SPI at the host or platform layer instead of putting those rules back into the lower-level modules.
If you only want to add one platform rule quickly, follow these four steps.

Use this mapping: MQL query: MqlQueryFilterInjector Fluent DSL query: FluentQueryFilterInjector MQL save: MqlSaveFieldValueFiller Fluent DSL save: FluentSaveFieldValueFiller entity save flow: EntitySaveFieldValueFiller A practical rule of thumb: if the rule should affect frontend or platform common APIs, start from MQL if the rule should affect backend Java services, start from Fluent DSL if the rule should affect object-save parsing directly, use entity save
Create a Spring Bean in the host project instead of editing lower-level modules first.
SPI types here are designed as "at most one enabled implementation", not "merge all matching beans together".
documents.s: Step 3: Keep Only One Enabled Implementation Per SPI Type

documents.t: Do not stop at successful Spring startup. Trigger a real query or save request and confirm the rule actually enters the execution chain.
documents.s: Step 4: Verify With A Real Query Or Save Flow

documents.t: Query filter SPI injects platform-level constraints into query flows, for example: tenant isolation data permission rules organization isolation default valid-record filtering

MQL query uses: cn.geelato.core.mql.spi.MqlQueryFilterInjector cn.geelato.core.mql.spi.support.MqlQueryFilterRuntimeResolver The corresponding flow is: JsonTextQueryParser parses QueryCommand calls MqlQueryFilterRuntimeResolver.injectIfAvailable(command) Interface: public interface MqlQueryFilterInjector { boolean isEnabled(); void inject(QueryCommand command); } Typical use cases: page list queries platform generic data APIs low-code configuration scenarios

Fluent DSL query uses: cn.geelato.orm.spi.FluentQueryFilterInjector cn.geelato.orm.spi.support.FluentQueryFilterRuntimeResolver The corresponding flow is: QueryCommandAdapter adapts MetaQuery into QueryCommand calls FluentQueryFilterRuntimeResolver.injectIfAvailable(command, query) Interface: public interface FluentQueryFilterInjector { boolean isEnabled(); void inject(QueryCommand command, MetaQuery query); /** * Whether injection is forced; defaults to false. * When true, injection still runs even if the query called MetaQuery.disableInjectFilter(). * Implementations usually do not need to care and inherit the default; * override to return true only when an injector must never be bypassed by a single query. */ default boolean isForceInject() { return false; } } Typical use cases: backend Java service queries query flows started by MetaFactory.query(...)

Current platform defaults are in geelato-web-platform: PlatformMqlQueryFilterInjector PlatformFluentQueryFilterInjector PlatformQueryFilterSupport PlatformQueryFilterSupport holds the default tenant and permission rules. Those defaults are no longer embedded in lower-level modules.

Save field fill SPI fills default values during save flows, for example: creator create time updater update time tenant code organization fields This capability is intentionally split into three SPI groups instead of one overly broad interface.

cn.geelato.core.mql.spi.MqlSaveFieldValueFiller cn.geelato.core.mql.spi.support.MqlSaveFieldValueFillRuntimeResolver Invocation entry: JsonTextSaveParser Interface: public interface MqlSaveFieldValueFiller { boolean isEnabled(); void fill(MqlSaveFieldValueFillContext context); } Typical use cases: saves initiated by frontend MQL requests platform generic save APIs

cn.geelato.orm.spi.FluentSaveFieldValueFiller cn.geelato.orm.spi.support.FluentSaveFieldValueFillRuntimeResolver Invocation entry: SaveCommandAdapter Interface: public interface FluentSaveFieldValueFiller { boolean isEnabled(); void fill(FluentSaveFieldValueFillContext context); } Typical use cases: backend Java service saves triggered by MetaFactory.insert/update(...)

cn.geelato.core.meta.spi.EntitySaveFieldValueFiller cn.geelato.core.meta.spi.support.EntitySaveFieldValueFillRuntimeResolver Invocation entry: EntitySaveParser Interface: public interface EntitySaveFieldValueFiller { boolean isEnabled(); void fill(EntitySaveFieldValueFillContext context); } Typical use cases: host projects that use direct entity-save parsing flows

Current platform defaults are in geelato-web-platform: PlatformMqlSaveFieldValueFiller PlatformFluentSaveFieldValueFiller PlatformEntitySaveFieldValueFiller PlatformFieldValueFillSupport PlatformFieldValueFillSupport keeps the default field rules, while still preserving differences between each entry point.
Here are implementation patterns close to real usage.

Typical cases: frontend list queries should always be tenant-isolated platform generic APIs should always append permission conditions Minimal example: @Component public class DemoMqlQueryFilterInjector implements MqlQueryFilterInjector { @Override public boolean isEnabled() { return true; } @Override public void inject(QueryCommand command) { // Inject platform-level query conditions into QueryCommand here } }
documents.s: Scenario 1: Add Tenant Filtering For MQL Query

documents.t: Typical cases: backend Java service queries should automatically include tenant, permission, or organization constraints Minimal example: @Component public class DemoFluentQueryFilterInjector implements FluentQueryFilterInjector { @Override public boolean isEnabled() { return true; } @Override public void inject(QueryCommand command, MetaQuery query) { // Inject platform-level conditions into the Fluent DSL query here } }
documents.s: Scenario 2: Add Platform Filters For Fluent DSL Query

documents.t: Typical cases: backend Java service saves should automatically fill creator, update time, or tenant code Minimal example: @Component public class DemoFluentSaveFieldValueFiller implements FluentSaveFieldValueFiller { @Override public boolean isEnabled() { return true; } @Override public void fill(FluentSaveFieldValueFillContext context) { // Fill default values for the save flow here } }
documents.s: Scenario 3: Fill Default Fields For Fluent DSL Save

documents.t: Typical cases: frontend or protocol-side saves should get unified default fields Minimal example: @Component public class DemoMqlSaveFieldValueFiller implements MqlSaveFieldValueFiller { @Override public boolean isEnabled() { return true; } @Override public void fill(MqlSaveFieldValueFillContext context) { // Fill default values for the MQL save flow here } }
documents.s: Scenario 4: Fill Default Fields For MQL Save

documents.t: Both query filter SPI and save field fill SPI follow the same runtime rules: when 0 implementations are found: skip when 1 implementation is found: execute only if isEnabled() returns true when multiple implementations are found: throw IllegalStateException This matters a lot for troubleshooting. The design intention is: no implicit fallback keep enablement visible avoid hidden stacking of multiple platform rules That means you should not enable more than one of the same SPI type, such as: two MqlQueryFilterInjector implementations two FluentQueryFilterInjector implementations two MqlSaveFieldValueFiller implementations two FluentSaveFieldValueFiller implementations If your project really has multiple candidates, merge the decision at the host layer and keep only one enabled implementation.

A Fluent DSL query can skip injected filters per query: calling disableInjectFilter() on a MetaQuery prevents any FluentQueryFilterInjector from running for that query, so platform defaults such as tenant isolation and data permission are not appended. MetaFactory.query("platform_user") .disableInjectFilter() .list(); Resolution rules (inside FluentQueryFilterRuntimeResolver.injectIfAvailable): disableInjectFilter() not called: inject normally disableInjectFilter() called and the injector isForceInject()=false: skip injection disableInjectFilter() called but the injector isForceInject()=true: inject anyway (forced override) isForceInject() is a default method on FluentQueryFilterInjector, defaulting to false; implementations do not need to care. Override it to return true only when an injector must never be bypassed by a single query (for example a hard boundary like tenant isolation). Note: skipping injection also bypasses tenant isolation and data permission, which risks cross-tenant or unauthorized reads. Use it only in trusted scenarios (system back office, scheduled tasks, admin tools) and only per query.
documents.s: Skipping Injection for a Single Query (Fluent DSL only)

documents.t: For a new project, this order usually works best: identify which execution flow the rule should affect choose the correct SPI interface implement one minimal Bean confirm there is only one enabled implementation of that SPI type verify through a real query or save flow When something fails, this sequence helps you quickly judge whether: the wrong SPI was chosen the Bean was not registered isEnabled() returned false multiple implementations were registered the real business flow never touched the entry point you expected

If an SPI "does not take effect", check in this order: confirm whether the current request uses MQL, Fluent DSL, or entity save flow confirm that your implementation matches that entry point confirm the container contains only one bean of the same SPI type confirm isEnabled() returns true trigger a real query or save flow once if you see Multiple ... beans found, inspect duplicate registrations first if a query is "missing" expected tenant/permission filters, check whether the caller invoked MetaQuery.disableInjectFilter() for that query, or whether the injector was disabled via isEnabled() For save field filling, also note: SaveDefaultValueFiller / DefaultSaveDefaultValueFiller now act as a compatibility layer the current primary extension entries are: MqlSaveFieldValueFiller FluentSaveFieldValueFiller EntitySaveFieldValueFiller BaseEntityMetaObjectHandler currently remains as-is and is not the main entry of this SPI chain

do not put platform rules back into geelato-core / geelato-orm query filters and field filling should stay framework-level reusable rules instead of scattered business patches if a rule belongs to one entry point only, implement that specific SPI instead of forcing a unified mega-interface if the logic is local to one API or one service, prefer the business layer instead of overusing SPI

SaveDefaultValueFiller / DefaultSaveDefaultValueFiller still exist in geelato-orm, but they are now compatibility-only and no longer the recommended primary extension point for SaveCommandAdapter. For current save-flow extensions, prefer: MqlSaveFieldValueFiller FluentSaveFieldValueFiller EntitySaveFieldValueFiller
