This page explains the platform's startup sequence when a Geelato Runtime application is based on: cn.geelato.web.platform.boot.BootApplication It focuses on: startup order metadata loading package scanning data source definition loading SQL and DB script loading Graal context initialization environment cache initialization

In a business application, the startup class usually extends BootApplication. There are two layers involved: Spring Boot starts and refreshes the ApplicationContext after the container is ready, BootApplication.run(...) is executed So BootApplication is not the outermost Spring Boot entry. It is the Geelato runtime bootstrap coordinator inside the Spring lifecycle.

The current startup sequence can be summarized as: Spring Boot creates and refreshes the ApplicationContext Spring scans platform beans and business beans MetaConfiguration initializes metadata from classes and database definitions Spring executes BootApplication.run(...) runtime managers initialize data source definitions SQL resources and DB scripts are loaded Graal services and variables are scanned environment configuration cache is initialized The overall sequence in its two layers:

Metadata initialization is performed in: MetaConfiguration not directly in BootApplication.run(...). It does two things: scan class-based metadata through geelato.meta.scan-package-names load database metadata through MetaManager.parseDBMeta(dao)
MetaManager.scanAndParse(...) scans packages for classes annotated with: @Entity and parses them into runtime metadata such as: EntityMeta FieldMeta ColumnMeta

After class scanning, MetaManager.parseDBMeta(dao) loads metadata from database metadata tables through: MetaStore The default implementation is: DefaultMetaStore It loads: table definitions column definitions view definitions checks foreign keys So runtime metadata comes from both: Java annotations database metadata definitions
If a custom MetaBootstrap bean exists, it runs after DB metadata is loaded. This makes MetaBootstrap a post-metadata extension point.

After the container is ready, BootApplication.run(...) executes in this order: log startup arguments and config info initialize data source definitions load SQL resources and DB scripts initialize Graal context initialize environment cache log runtime version

BootApplication first initializes: DataSourceManager If a custom DataSourceDefinitionLoader bean exists, it replaces the default loader. Then: parseDataSourceMeta(dao) does two things: registers the primary data source as primary loads dynamic data source definitions into a snapshot cache (DataSourceManager: registered instances in dataSourceMap, connection definitions in dataSourceConfigMap, reloaded on demand via loadOne on a snapshot miss) The important point is that dynamic data sources are usually not created eagerly at startup. Their definitions are cached first, and real pools are built lazily by the orm-side DynamicDataSourceRegistry when a specific connectId is routed (with DynamicRoutingDataSource triggering creation as a fallback). DataSourceManager itself is a pure registry — registered instances, connection-config snapshots and the default key; it builds no pools.
Next, BootApplication loads runtime SQL scripts.
documents.s: SQL Resource and DB Script Loading

documents.t: If the runtime is not running as a fat jar, it uses: SqlScriptManagerFactory.get("sql").loadFiles(...) to load SQL resources from the classpath file system. Then it sets dao into DbScriptManager and calls: loadDb() to load DB scripts from: platform_sql

If the runtime is packaged as a fat jar, SQL resources are loaded from: loadResource("/geelato/web/platform/sql/**/*.sql") instead of a file-system directory. DB script loading still happens afterward.
DbScriptManager now checks whether platform_sql exists first. If the table does not exist, it logs and skips DB script loading instead of crashing startup.
documents.s: Why Missing platform_sql Does Not Block Startup

documents.t: Then BootApplication initializes the Graal context through: geelato.graal.scan-package-names For each configured package it scans: @GraalService @GraalVariable GraalManager instantiates those classes and registers them into runtime Graal maps. For Graal service beans, it also tries to inject a Dao, preferring: dynamicDao when available.

Finally, BootApplication initializes: EnvManager It sets the current JdbcTemplate and runs: EnvInit() At the moment this mainly loads enabled records from: platform_sys_config into in-memory caches. So after startup, system configuration can be accessed from memory instead of querying the database every time.
Spring bean scanning and metadata entity scanning are not the same thing.
This is about: @Component @Service @Controller @Configuration and its goal is to register beans in the Spring container.
This is about: @Entity and its goal is to build runtime metadata in MetaManager.

The current startup process can be remembered as: Spring scans beans MetaConfiguration scans and loads metadata BootApplication initializes runtime managers runtime startup completes More specifically, BootApplication is responsible for: dynamic data source definition initialization SQL resource and DB script loading Graal service and variable scanning environment cache initialization while metadata loading happens earlier in: MetaConfiguration

PlatformWebRuntime is the runtime application shell of the Geelato web platform. It is the runnable entry that boots the shared geelato-web-platform base for business-execution scenarios.

PlatformWebRuntime is a Spring Boot main class: package: cn.geelato.web.runtime class: cn.geelato.web.runtime.PlatformWebRuntime main class: cn.geelato.web.runtime.PlatformWebRuntime declared in module: geelato-web-runtime The full source is: @SpringBootApplication(scanBasePackages = {"cn.geelato"}) @EnableConfigurationProperties @EnableCaching @EnableAsync(proxyTargetClass = true) public class PlatformWebRuntime extends BootApplication { public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(PlatformWebRuntime.class, args); } } It extends cn.geelato.web.platform.boot.BootApplication, which is the shared Geelato runtime bootstrap coordinator (see Startup Process for the full chain).

Item Value Maven artifactId geelato-web-runtime Module path geelato-community/geelato-web-runtime Packaging jar spring-boot-maven-plugin mainClass cn.geelato.web.runtime.PlatformWebRuntime spring-boot-maven-plugin classifier exec Direct dependencies geelato-web-platform, spring-boot-starter-test (test scope) The module deliberately has only one direct dependency (geelato-web-platform). All platform capabilities come transitively from the shared base.

geelato-web-runtime/src/main/resources/application.properties: spring.application.name=geelato-web-runtime logging.level.root=INFO logging.level.cn.geelato=INFO The shell currently overrides only the application name and log levels. All other settings (datasource, upload, security, plugin directory, etc.) come from the shared base or the host project that consumes this shell.

When the shell starts, it brings up everything the shared base declares, including: the geelato-web-platform controllers and services the default BootApplication startup chain (datasource, SQL/Graal scripts, environment cache) the framework starter wiring (geelato-framework-starter) the metadata loading layer (geelato-meta) the plugin runtime (pf4j + geelato-plugins/geelato-plugin-all) the OSS, package, security, and Redis integrations declared by the shared base It enables Spring caching and async execution with CGLIB proxying (@EnableAsync(proxyTargetClass = true)) and exposes @ConfigurationProperties beans.

PlatformWebRuntime does not duplicate any startup work. It only sets the cn.geelato scan base and enables caching, async, and configuration properties. The actual startup work happens in BootApplication.run(...): DataSourceManager.parseDataSourceMeta(dao) SQL / DB script loading (exploded mode or fat-jar mode) Graal service and variable scanning EnvManager.EnvInit() See Startup Process for details.
mvn -pl geelato-web-runtime spring-boot:run or build the runnable jar: mvn -pl geelato-web-runtime clean package java -jar geelato-web-runtime/target/geelato-web-runtime-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT-exec.jar

PlatformWebRuntime and PlatformDesginer are structurally identical shells. They: both extend BootApplication both depend only on geelato-web-platform both have the same Spring annotations differ only in spring.application.name and the main class FQN There is no code-level "switch" between runtime and designer mode. The two jars are two independent deployable entry points. A host project picks one of them as its main class. Splitting endpoint surface between the two is not yet part of the shared base; both shells currently expose the full endpoint set from geelato-web-platform.

Geelato provides a unified job scheduling center: scheduled jobs are registered as database configuration in the platform_schedule table. On application startup, enabled jobs are loaded automatically and triggered periodically by cron expressions; changes made while running take effect through hot refresh, with no restart required. This page is for business developers and operations staff who need to configure scheduled jobs on the platform. It covers which jobs can be scheduled, how to enable scheduling, and where platform built-in periodic tasks live. For job configuration and start/stop operations, see Job Configuration & Operations.

The scheduling center supports three job types, each pointing via a unique code (code) to an existing executable: Type (type) How the job is defined Typical use cases sql code refers to a SQL registered in platform SQL management (platform_sql) Periodic data cleanup, aggregation, status refresh via configured SQL java code + class_info = "fully.qualified.ClassName,methodName", invoking a Bean method inside the application container Logic that has already been developed within the application general code refers to a JS script published in platform API management (platform_api) Business orchestration jobs; scripts can use $gl services directly note The retry_times field in the job model is reserved, but automatic retry is not yet implemented: a failed job will not be re-run automatically and needs manual handling. Execution identity: jobs are triggered by the scheduler under a system identity — SQL and scripts are not filtered by the current user's data permissions, while tenant isolation still applies. Take this into account when assessing data visibility in job SQL or scripts.

Scheduling is enabled through application configuration: # Scheduling master switch (off by default) geelato.schedule=true # Scheduling thread pool size (default 10) geelato.schedule.thread-pool-size=10 :::warning Clustering behavior The scheduler has no cluster coordination (no distributed lock or leader election): every node with geelato.schedule=true independently loads and triggers all enabled jobs. When running multiple instances, the same job executes once per node — enable scheduling on a single instance only, or make sure the job itself is idempotent. :::

Some platform modules ship their own periodic engine actions (mail sync, alert scanning, etc.). These actions are not registered in the scheduling center; they run independently within each module and expose their own configuration switches: Module Periodic action Configuration switch Mail Incremental mailbox account sync geelato.mail.sync.enabled In-app notifications Notification delivery geelato.notification.outbox-enabled Business alerts Alert engine scan/delivery geelato.alert.engine.enabled Data archiving Scheduled archiving by archive templates geelato.archive.scheduler-enabled Business exceptions Exception rule scanning geelato.exception.engine.enabled Selection guideline: business jobs configured through the admin UI (sql/java/general) → the unified scheduling center; periodic engine actions inside modules → controlled by their own switches, no job registration needed.
documents.s: 3. Built-in periodic tasks of platform modules

documents.t: Job Configuration & Operations: how to configure a scheduled job, start/stop it, and view execution logs. Schedule & Log Entities: full field definitions of platform_schedule / platform_schedule_log.

This page is for business developers and operations staff who need to configure scheduled jobs on the platform. It covers how to configure a scheduled job, how to start/stop it, and how to view execution logs and troubleshoot problems. For the positioning of the scheduling capability and deployment notes, see Scheduler Overview.

Prepare the executable (one of the three types): sql: register the SQL in platform SQL management (platform_sql) first; java: make sure the target Bean exists in the application container, formatted as class_info = "fully.qualified.ClassName,methodName", with a no-arg method or framework-convention injection; general: publish a JS script in platform API management (platform_api); the script can use $gl services, and ctx.result carries data across runs. Create the job: in the admin/Designer "Schedule Management" page, or via POST /api/schedule/createOrUpdate, fill in code (unique), expression (cron), type, params (JSON parameters), app_id, etc. (see the field table below). Enable the job: set status to 1 (the "Enable" button on the list page, or GET /api/schedule/status/{id}/1). Make it effective: a newly created or modified job takes effect on the next application restart, or after calling the hot-refresh endpoint — see "When changes take effect" below.

Jobs are registered in the platform_schedule table. The main configuration fields are listed below (full field definitions in Schedule & Log Entities): Field Required Description code ✅ Unique job code; for sql/general it is also the referenced SQL/API identifier type ✅ Job type: sql / java / general expression ✅ Cron expression (6 fields: second minute hour day month weekday, ? supported in day/weekday), e.g. 0 0 3 * * ? = 3:00 AM daily app_id Recommended Owning application name Recommended Display name of the job params Optional JSON parameters readable during execution class_info By type Only for java jobs, formatted as "fully.qualified.ClassName,methodName" status — Job status: 0 stopped / 1 enabled; new jobs default to stopped retry_times — Retry count (reserved; automatic retry not yet implemented) context — Persisted cross-run context written by the job itself (e.g. ctx.result of general jobs) description Optional Job description last_start_time / last_finish_time are written back automatically by the scheduler on each execution, for showing the latest run.

sql (periodic data cleanup): platform_schedule: { code: "CLEAN_TEMP", type: "sql", expression: "0 0 3 * * ?" } platform_sql: { key_name: "CLEAN_TEMP", ... DELETE FROM xxx WHERE create_at < :cutoff } general (JS business job with cross-run context): // Script published in platform_api; the job's code points to this API const pending = $gl.sql.query("SELECT COUNT(*) c FROM task WHERE status='PENDING'") if (pending[0].c > 0) { // processing logic ctx.result = { lastCount: pending[0].c } // written back to the job context, readable next run } java: class_info = "cn.geelato.app.task.ReportTask,buildDailyReport".
documents.s: 3. Examples of the three job types

documents.t: The "Schedule Management" page in the admin/Designer provides full management for jobs: Create/edit jobs: a form for the configuration fields above, with cron validation; Enable/disable: the list page offers "Enable" for stopped jobs and "Disable" for enabled ones (both with confirmation); Execution logs: each job in the list can open its log page showing every execution record.

Endpoint Description POST /pageQuery, GET /query, GET /get/{id} Job pagination / list / detail POST /createOrUpdate, DELETE /isDelete/{id}, POST /validate Create or update / delete / validate GET /status/{id}/{status} Enable (1) / disable (0) /api/schedule/log/pageQuery, GET /api/schedule/log/query Execution log pagination / list

Endpoint Description GET /{code}/start Trigger an immediate one-off execution (periodic schedule unaffected) GET /{code}/stop Cancel the current pending trigger of the job GET /{code}/config Query the trigger configuration currently registered for the job GET /{code}/config/refresh Hot refresh: call after changing the DB configuration, effective without restart

Newly created jobs / enabling a stopped job: effective on the next application restart, or after calling GET /schedule/runtime/{code}/config/refresh; Changing the cron or params of a running job: call GET /schedule/runtime/{code}/config/refresh to take effect immediately, no restart needed; Disabling a job: subsequent triggers stop immediately; an execution already in progress is not interrupted.

Every execution writes one log entry (platform_schedule_log): status (execute running → success / fail), start_at / finish_at, and result (result summary). View them on the log page or via /api/schedule/log. Common troubleshooting: Job not triggering: confirm geelato.schedule=true is on, the job status=1, the node is a single instance or jobs are idempotent across instances (see the cluster warning), and the cron expression is correct; then check GET /schedule/runtime/{code}/config to confirm the job is registered. Execution failures: check result summaries and finish_at of status=fail log entries; note that automatic retry is not yet implemented (retry_times has no effect) — failed jobs do not re-run automatically. Residual context: context is written explicitly by the job; the ctx.result of general jobs persists across runs — if you don't need cross-run data, don't set ctx.result, or overwrite/clean it yourself. Duplicate execution on multiple instances: see "Clustering behavior" in the overview — enable scheduling on a single instance only, or make jobs idempotent.

脚本执行时，引擎按场景档案注入一批预置变量。每个变量是什么、来自哪里、能做什么，本页逐一说明。 变量 来源 一句话说明 console 引擎 日志输出，随 ScriptResult 返回，恒可见 $env 引擎 执行元数据（execId、版本、租户、用户等），只读，恒可见 $ctx 调用方 bindings 业务上下文（触发模式、业务单号等） $params 调用方 params 脚本参数输入（阈值、天数等） $input 调用方 bindings 管道场景中上一步的输出 $gl 引擎 内置与自定义 kit 的挂载对象，见内置 Kit

标准日志对象，提供 log/info/warn/error/debug 五个方法（debug 按 log 记录）。输出不打印到控制台，而是收集后随 ScriptResult.console 返回，并进入执行日志（失败时自动附带末尾 10 条）。 约束： 单条超过 2000 字符截断； 总量上限 100 条，超出后静默丢弃； 序列化对象时最多展开 30 个成员、数组最多 50 个元素。 console.log('rows', rows.length); console.warn('fallback branch', $ctx.bizId);

执行元数据，引擎组装、只读。用于在脚本内感知"本次执行是谁、在什么配置下跑"： 键 说明 execId 本次执行的唯一 id（与 ScriptResult.execId、执行日志同源） lang 脚本语言（js/python） engineVersion 实际执行的引擎版本 profileId 场景档案 id startedAt 执行开始时间（yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss） timeoutMs 本次执行超时毫秒 tenantCode / tenantName 租户编码/名称（无身份快照时为 null） appId / appName 应用 id/名称 user 用户对象：id、userId、userName、loginName、orgId、orgName、deptId attrs 宿主经 attributes 中 env. 前缀键透传的扩展项（无则不存在） console.log('running under', $env.engineVersion, 'as', $env.user.userName);

调用方注入的业务上下文：触发模式、业务单号、单据快照等场景数据，经 ScriptExecution.bindings 的 $ctx 键传入。 const bizId = $ctx.bizId; const trigger = $ctx.trigger; // 如 SCAN / RECHECK / TRIAL 与 $gl.ctx.get(key)/$gl.ctx.all() 同源（同一份数据的两种入口）。
脚本的参数输入：阈值、天数等由调用方配置的数值，经 ScriptExecution.params 便捷字段传入，引擎归一注入为 $params（若显式 bindings 已含 $params，以 bindings 为准不覆盖）。 const days = $params.days ?? 90; 与 $gl.parameter.get(key)/$gl.parameter.all() 同源。
多步管道（如异常判定管道）中的约定变量：从第二步起，上一步脚本的返回值经 bindings 注入为 $input。引擎不对其做特殊处理，形态由管道各步的约定决定。 // 第二步：消费第一步筛出的候选列表 return $input.filter(r => r.amount > $params.minAmount);

变量注入受**场景档案（ScriptProfile）**收口，与引擎版本正交（版本定"哪个版本的 kit"，档案定"哪些能力对本次执行可见"）： 变量白名单 variables：只有名单内的变量名会被真正注入（$ctx 不在名单则脚本内不可见）；含 "*" 表示全部放行；console 与 $env 恒可见，不受该名单约束； kit 白名单 namespaces：$gl.ctx/$gl.parameter 等 kit 形态入口受命名空间白名单约束，而非变量白名单——即使 $ctx 变量被过滤，$gl.ctx 仍可能可用（反之亦然），按场景档案的能力择一使用； 冻结 frozenBindings：档案开启后，Map/List 型注入变量会做冻结处理，脚本内不可覆盖成员； 缺省 default 档案全量放行（namespaces/variables 均为 *，不冻结，缺省超时 30s），收窄能力边界由宿主按场景定义档案（如告警渲染档案只放开模板 kit）。 宿主侧注入示例（谁给了脚本这些变量）： scriptEngine.execute(ScriptExecution.builder() .content(content) .params(Map.of("days", 90)) // → $params .bindings(Map.of("$ctx", Map.of("bizId", "10234"))) // → $ctx .build());
内置 kit（见内置 Kit）之外，集成方可以把自有能力开发为 kit 注入脚本：一个标注注解的 Java 类 + 一次注册。SDK 内置的 cn.geelato.script.kit.demo.DemoService 是参考模板。

kit 的全部元数据来自两个注解（定义于 cn.geelato.core.graal）： @GraalService(name = "demo", built = "true", descrption = "演示 kit（模板）：hello/add") public class DemoService { private final KitContext ctx; public DemoService(KitContext ctx) { this.ctx = ctx; } @GraalFunction(example = "$gl.demo.hello('world')", description = "回显问好并携带本次执行 execId") public Map<String, Object> hello(String name) { return Map.of( "message", "hello " + (name == null || name.isBlank() ? "world" : name), "execId", String.valueOf(ctx.getExecId())); } @GraalFunction(example = "$gl.demo.add(1, 2)", description = "两数相加") public long add(long a, long b) { return a + b; } } 注解属性 说明 @GraalService.name 脚本侧命名空间，也是注册与档案白名单匹配的 key，全局唯一（冲突启动即报错） @GraalService.built "true" 挂到 $gl.{name}；"false"（缺省）挂顶层变量 ${name} @GraalService.descrption 描述文本，进 $gl.help() 与 catalog 清单 @GraalFunction.example 调用示例，进 help 详情与 catalog，供编辑器补全展示 @GraalFunction.description 方法说明 只有标注 @GraalFunction 的 public 方法会暴露给脚本，其余方法不可见。

参数与返回类型必须在 interop 兼容白名单内，否则启动即 fail-fast（IllegalStateException，指明类#方法与违规类型）： 参数允许：String、数值（Number 家族与原始类型）、Boolean、Map、List、Date、Object、polyglot Value； 返回允许：同上外加 void； 泛型集合按原始类型（Map/List）判定；Set 等其他类型不支持。

形态 判定方式 生命周期 适用 单例 无参构造器，或以实例注册 全引擎复用一个实例 无状态 kit scoped 声明 (KitContext) 构造器（唯一 public 构造器参数恰为 KitContext），或经 registerScoped 工厂通道注册 每次执行实例化，互不串扰 需要执行级上下文的 kit scoped kit 经构造器获取的 KitContext 是单次执行的上下文：execId、身份快照（identity）、注入变量（bindings，$gl.ctx/$gl.parameter 的数据源）、执行级属性袋（attributes）、行数计数器（addRows）、kit 调用留痕（record）以及宿主装配的 SPI（数据源、ORM 供给等）。 带外部依赖（Spring Bean 等）不适合构造器直接创建时，走工厂通道： builder.registerScoped("demo", DemoService.class, ctx -> new DemoService(depService, ctx));

1. 配置扫描：把 kit 所在包加入扫描清单，无需写注册代码： geelato.script.engine.scan-packages=cn.geelato.example.rulekit 2. 编程注册：非 Spring 环境或单测中直接在 Builder 上注册（Spring Bean 优先传实例，避免重复实例化）： ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineBuilder() .registerKit(new DemoKit()) // 实例（恒单例） .registerKit(OtherKit.class) // 类（按构造器形状判定 scoped） .build(); 3. Spring 定制器：定义 ScriptEngineCustomizer Bean，自动装配时按序应用： @Bean public ScriptEngineCustomizer demoKitCustomizer() { return builder -> builder.registerKit(new DemoKit()); } 命名空间冲突（两个 kit 同 name）在注册时即抛错，不会静默覆盖。
build() 默认注册六个内置 kit，但仅当注册表中尚无同名 kit 时——消费方显式注册（registerKit/registerScoped/扫描）同名者优先，内置版本被跳过。可用它整体替换某个内置 kit 的实现（如换成走专属数据源的 $gl.sql）。

把自定义 kit 固化到某个引擎版本快照，供脚本按 engineVersion 路由（引擎版本语义见脚本使用手册）。以基线版本为底声明差异，构建期派生注册： ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineBuilder() .registerKit(new RuleKitV2()) // 先注册（进缺省版本） .deriveRevision("v2", "v1", deriver -> deriver .scoped("rule", RuleKitV2.class) // v2 用新实现覆盖 rule 命名空间 .remove("legacy") // 移除不再暴露的 kit .esVersion("2023")) // 语言级别差异（可选） .build(); RevisionDeriver 差异声明项：singleton(ns, kit) 覆盖/新增无状态 kit、scoped(ns, clazz[, factory]) 覆盖/新增 scoped kit、remove(ns) 移除、esVersion(...) 语言级别、status(...) 注册时初始状态（缺省 CURRENT）。派生出的 kit 同样经 interop 白名单 fail-fast 校验；ns 须与 @GraalService.name 一致。

注册完成后三种自检方式： 脚本内 $gl.help() / $gl.help('demo') 打印可见 kit 与方法； GET /api/script/catalog 拉取结构化清单（开启 geelato.script.rest.enabled）； KitDtsGenerator.generate(...) 生成 .d.ts 声明文件，在 IDE 中获得补全提示。 第三方 Java 库无需逐个写 kit 类即可整库引入，见第三方库引入。

实验性功能：在线调试处于实验阶段，界面与体验待完善，接口与行为可能调整，暂不建议在生产环境依赖。 geelato-script 基于 GraalJS 内置的 CDP inspector 提供断点调试：为一组脚本内容启动调试会话，用 Chrome DevTools 连接后即可断点、单步、查看变量。调试执行与正常执行共用同一条 kit/变量/环境注入链，保证调试副作用与线上一致（写通道 dry-run 恒生效）。
宿主开启 geelato.script.rest.enabled=true 后，访问 GET /script-playground.html 打开内置调试台： 调试台：编辑脚本、传参执行、语法预检、浏览 kit 目录（自动补全数据源）； 调试会话：以调试台中的脚本与参数创建/停止调试会话，查看会话状态与 inspector 地址。

调试端点随 geelato.script.rest.enabled 装配，仅限内网可信环境： 端点 说明 POST /api/script/debug/start 创建调试会话，入参与 /api/script/execute 对齐（lang/content/scriptName/engineVersion/profileId/params/bindings），另可指定 debugSessionId（空由引擎分配）、debugOwner（会话归属，供代理鉴权）、debugPort（空/0 自动分配空闲端口）。返回 DebugSession POST /api/script/debug/stop/{sessionId} 停止会话，强关 Context 并释放 inspector 端口（幂等） GET /api/script/debug/{sessionId}/status 查询会话状态 DebugSession 返回字段：sessionId、host（恒 127.0.0.1，inspector 只绑回环，绝不公网暴露）、port、path（= sessionId，多会话经路径区分）、owner、engineVersion。面向浏览器的同源网关（如设计器）应剥离 host/port，只向浏览器下发代理路径。 curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/script/debug/start \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"scriptName":"EXC-BL-005","engineVersion":"v1", "params":{"days":90}, "content":"const rows = $gl.sql.query(\"...\", {});\nreturn rows.length;"}' # → {"sessionId":"a1b2...","host":"127.0.0.1","port":41235,"path":"a1b2...","owner":null,"engineVersion":"v1"}

调试会话创建后脚本挂起等待（WaitAttached + Suspend：DevTools 连接并 resume 前不执行）： 打开 Chrome，访问 chrome://inspect； Configure 添加目标地址 127.0.0.1:{port}（端口来自 DebugSession）； 稍候出现 Remote Target，点击 inspect 打开 DevTools； 在 Sources 面板定位调试源码 gl-debug://<scriptName>，行号与编辑器 1:1 对应，直接下断点后 resume。 scriptName 作为调试 Source 名，同一脚本重复调试时断点可持久。

状态 含义 WAITING 已创建，等待 DevTools 连接 RUNNING DevTools 已连接，执行中 EXITED 脚本自然执行结束（Context 已关闭） STOPPED 被 stop 主动停止，或会话不存在 GET /api/script/debug/{sessionId}/status 额外返回 alive（会话线程是否存活）与 error/errorMessage（执行异常信息）。

仅支持 javascript：lang 非 js 时启动报错； 与线上一致：复用正常执行的 kit 注入、变量注入（$ctx/$params，受场景档案白名单过滤）与 $env 组装；写通道 dry-run 恒生效（写语句在事务内执行后回滚）； 资源上限仍生效：语句数上限（statement-limit）防死循环； 不受同步超时约束：调试是长会话，timeoutMs 仅注入 $env 供脚本读取，不会像正常执行那样超时强杀——记得调试完 stop 释放端口； 引擎版本语义同正常执行：RETIRED 版本拒绝创建会话。
脚本不能 import 任意 Java 类；要把第三方库能力提供给脚本，由宿主声明整库引入：SDK 按包扫描其中的工具类，把 interop 兼容的公共方法挂载为 $kit 顶层对象。库本身以普通 Maven 依赖进入宿主 classpath，脚本侧零声明。

沙箱限制了脚本内的宿主类查找：Java.type(...) 仅对一份固定白名单放行——三个 kit 注解类与 HashMap/ArrayList/LinkedHashMap/String/Integer/Long/Double/Boolean/BigDecimal/Date 等少数 JDK 类。其余类（如 java.lang.System）查找即被拒绝，Class/ClassLoader/System/Runtime/Thread 的访问被显式 deny。 因此引入第三方能力的唯一受控通道是宿主侧的整库注入（下述两种声明方式），没有脚本内依赖声明 DSL。
ScriptEngine engine = new ScriptEngineBuilder() .hostPackage("hutool", "cn.hutool.core.util") // 库别名 = 根包 .hostExcludes(List.of("RuntimeUtil")) // 按类简单名或全限定名剔除（可选） .build();

在任意 jar（含宿主自身）内放置 META-INF/gl/script-kits.properties，自动装配时解析： # 别名 = 根包 hutool=cn.hutool.core.util codec=org.example.commons.codec # 特殊键：逗号分隔的剔除清单（类简单名或全限定名） exclude=RuntimeUtil,ObjUtil 多份文件（多个 jar 各自带一份）自动合并；同一别名映射到不同包时启动报错，须为其中一个改用其他别名。

整库注入统一挂载为顶层 $kit 对象，三层结构：$kit.{库别名}.{类简单名小写}.{方法}。 // hostPackage("hutool", "cn.hutool.core.util") 之后 const uuid = $kit.hutool.idutil.fastSimpleUUID(); const masked = $kit.hutool.strutil.hide($ctx.phone, 3, 7); return { uuid, masked };

对根包（含子包）下扫到的每个具体类（接口、抽象类、枚举、注解均跳过）： 静态方法：签名 interop 兼容即直接暴露； 实例方法：类有 public 无参构造器时实例化后暴露（无参构造缺失则跳过该类实例方法）； interop 兼容口径与自定义 kit 相同：参数/返回类型限于 String、数值、Boolean、Map、List、Date、Object、Value 与原始类型；不兼容的方法静默跳过（启动日志 warn 提示跳过数量）。

危险类硬拒绝：扫到 System/Runtime/Class/ClassLoader/Thread 直接抛错，而非跳过——声明过宽（根包覆盖到 java.lang 等）会立即暴露问题； 别名下类名冲突 fail-fast：同别名内两个类简单名相同（decapitalize 后撞名）启动报错，提示拆分为多个别名子包； 空库 fail-fast：别名对应包没扫到任何可注入类（包名不在 classpath、全被 exclude、无兼容方法）启动报错； 暴露面即攻击面：$kit 方法不经 @GraalFunction 注解收口，库内所有兼容签名的方法都会暴露。声明根包时收敛到工具子包（如 cn.hutool.core.util 而非 cn.hutool.core），并善用 exclude 剔除不该进脚本的类；HTTP/IO 类库谨慎引入。
KitDtsGenerator.generate(...) 同样为 $kit 生成三层嵌套的 .d.ts 声明，规则作者放进工程即可获得 $kit.hutool.strutil.* 的补全。

kit 是脚本调用宿主能力的受控通道，built=true 的 kit 挂在 $gl 对象下。ScriptEngineBuilder.build() 默认注册六个内置 kit；消费方显式注册同名 kit 时优先消费方（见自定义 Kit）。脚本内 $gl.help() 可速查当前可见的 kit 与方法。 kit 用途 $gl.sql 命名参数 SQL 桥（含跨库路由） $gl.mql MQL 元数据查询（对齐平台 /meta/* 接口） $gl.http HTTP 出网（白名单管控） $gl.encrypt 摘要与 AES 加解密 $gl.ctx 执行上下文读取（与 $ctx 同源） $gl.parameter 参数输入读取（与 $params 同源）

数据源由宿主装配，脚本侧只管语句与参数。参数为命名参数（:name），查询受行数上限（sql.row-limit，缺省 10000）与查询超时（sql.query-timeout-ms，缺省 10s）收口。 方法 说明 $gl.sql.query(sql, params) 查询返回行数组（字段名→值）；行数计入本次执行的 rowCount $gl.sql.queryOne(sql, params) 查询单行，无结果返回 null $gl.sql.queryValue(sql, params) 查询单值，无结果返回 null $gl.sql.update(sql, params) 写语句（INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE），返回 {affected, dryRun} $gl.sql.execute(sql) 执行 DDL/无参语句，门控同 update const total = $gl.sql.queryValue('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM grant_apply', {}); const row = $gl.sql.queryOne('SELECT * FROM grant_apply WHERE id = :id', { id: '1' }); const rows = $gl.sql.query(` SELECT id AS biz_id, eco_no AS biz_no, not_written_off FROM grant_apply WHERE not_written_off > :minAmount `, { minAmount: $gl.parameter.get('minAmount') });

$gl.sql 会自动识别语句引用的物理表（依据 platform_dev_table.connect_id / @Entity(connectId) / catalog 映射的连接登记），按表所在库与执行库的关系三段路由： 场景 行为 全部在执行库本库（含未登记表） 原样直连执行，零开销 同实例跨库 自动加库名前缀（如 `bizdb`.`t`）后仍在执行库执行；事务与 dry-run 回滚语义不变 跨实例 / 异构库 Apache Calcite 联邦执行：单源过滤与投影下推各库，跨源 join/聚合在应用内存计算（非分布式引擎，大结果集受行数上限与超时收口） 边界：跨实例写语句直接拒绝（无跨库事务保证）；未登记表、已带库名限定的表、CTE 别名、无法解析的语句均原样透传；登记的连接在 platform_dev_db_connect 中无配置则硬失败。同实例前缀改写只替换表名文本区间，语句其余部分（含注释与 hint）保持原文不变。路由决策记入 trace（sql/route 条目）与 KIT-XDB 日志。

入参为 MQL JSON 文本（语法见 MQL 使用指引），方法面对齐平台 /meta/* 接口（MetaController），按实体元数据自动路由数据源与身份。 方法 对齐接口 说明 $gl.mql.list(mqlJson) /meta/list 单实体查询，返回 {data, total, page, size} $gl.mql.multiList(mqlJson) /meta/multiList 多实体查询，返回 {data: {实体名: {data, total, page, size}}} $gl.mql.save(mqlJson) /meta/save/{biz} 保存，返回 {pk, dryRun}；受写通道门控 $gl.mql.batchSave(mqlJson) /meta/batchSave 批量保存，返回 {pks, dryRun}；受写通道门控 $gl.mql.multiSave(mqlJson) /meta/multiSave 多实体保存，返回 {count, dryRun}；受写通道门控 $gl.mql.delete(entityName, id) /meta/delete/{biz}/{id} 按 id 删除（id 支持逗号分隔多值），返回 {affected, dryRun}；受写通道门控 $gl.mql.deleteByGql(mqlJson) /meta/delete2/{biz} 按条件删除，返回 {affected, dryRun}；受写通道门控 $gl.mql.explain(mqlJson, op) — 解释不执行（op=list/save/delete），返回 {sql, params, countSql} const page = $gl.mql.list('{ "platform_user": { "@fs": "id,userName", "del_status|eq": 0, "@p": "1,20" } }'); return page.data.map(u => ({ bizType: 'USER', bizId: u.ID, hitBrief: u.USERNAME }));

三重管控：总开关 http.enabled（缺省开，但白名单为空时仍拒绝所有请求——出网必须显式配置 allowlist）、主机白名单 http.allowlist（条目支持精确 host、*. 前缀域名、可选 scheme:// 限定）、单请求超时不超过 http.timeout-ms（缺省 5s）。不做证书绕过。 方法 说明 $gl.http.get(url, params, headers) GET，返回响应体字符串 $gl.http.post(url, body, headers) POST（body 为字符串原样、对象自动 JSON），返回响应体字符串 $gl.http.put(url, body, headers) / $gl.http.patch(...) PUT/PATCH，同 post $gl.http.delete(url, headers) DELETE，返回响应体字符串 $gl.http.request({method, url, params, body, headers, timeoutMs}) 完整请求，返回 {status, headers, body} const resp = $gl.http.request({ method: 'POST', url: baseUrl, body: { code: 'X1' } }); if (resp.status !== 200) { console.warn('bad status', resp.status); } return JSON.parse(resp.body);

AES 复用平台 AesUtils 口径（AES/GCM，Base64(IV+密文)），密文与平台其他模块互操作。密钥经 geelato.script.engine.encrypt.aes-key 配置，未配置时 aes/aesDecrypt 抛错。执行留痕只记输入长度，不落敏感明文。 方法 说明 $gl.encrypt.md5(text) MD5 摘要，32 位小写十六进制 $gl.encrypt.md5Short(text) MD5 摘要 16 位（32 位截取 [8,24)） $gl.encrypt.aes(text) AES 加密 $gl.encrypt.aesDecrypt(cipher) AES 解密

$ctx/$params 的 kit 形态入口，与注入变量同源（含义见内置上下文）。区别在于可见性：变量形态受场景档案的变量白名单过滤，kit 形态受命名空间白名单约束。 方法 说明 $gl.ctx.get(key) / $gl.ctx.all() 取上下文单键值（缺失返回 null）/ 完整 Map $gl.parameter.get(key) / $gl.parameter.all() 取参数单键值（缺失返回 null）/ 完整 Map
脚本内直接打印当前可见的 kit 清单与方法名： return $gl.help(); // 全部 kit 速查 // return $gl.help('sql'); // 单 kit 详情（方法 + 示例 + 说明）

能力清单：GET /api/script/catalog?profile=&version=（需 geelato.script.rest.enabled=true），按场景档案过滤，是速查面板与编辑器自动补全的数据源； TypeScript 声明：宿主可用 KitDtsGenerator.generate(...) 把 catalog 生成为 .d.ts 声明文件，规则作者把产物放进工程即可在 IDE 中获得 $gl/$kit 的智能提示。
documents.s: kit 目录与 IDE 提示

documents.t: geelato-script is the general-purpose script execution engine SDK of Geelato Framework. Built on the GraalVM Polyglot sandbox, it provides safe script computation.

Each execution is an isolated loop: The consumer assembles a ScriptExecution (content, language, timeout, injected variables, attributes) and submits it to ScriptEngine.execute; The engine resolves the engine version (EngineRevision snapshot) and the scenario profile (ScriptProfile), activating whitelisted kits; A fresh Polyglot Context is populated with console, built-in kits ($gl.*), injected variables ($ctx/$params, etc.) and the execution environment ($env); The script runs on a worker thread; the calling thread enforces the timeout with a hard kill (context.close(true)); A ScriptResult is returned: status (SUCCESS/ERROR/TIMEOUT), value, console logs, cost, SQL row count, a kit-call trace and a structured error (type + line/column + stack).

No file or network primitives: IO, process creation, native access and environment variables are denied (outbound HTTP only via the $gl.http allowlist channel); Class-access allowlist: only methods annotated with @GraalService/@GraalFunction are callable; Class/ClassLoader/System/Runtime/Thread are rejected; Resource limits: a per-execution statement limit (statement-limit) plus an execution timeout; Controlled kit signatures: parameter and return types are validated fail-fast at registration.

EngineRevision: a frozen snapshot of the kit set; breaking changes ship as a new version with parallel routing, and old versions can be marked DEPRECATED/RETIRED. Defaults to v1. ScriptProfile: declares the kit namespaces (namespaces) and injectable variables (variables) visible to a scenario, plus a default timeout.

ScriptEngineBuilder.build() registers six built-in kits by default (an explicit same-name registration from the consumer takes precedence): $gl.sql, $gl.mql, $gl.http, $gl.encrypt, $gl.ctx, $gl.parameter. See the script authoring guide for APIs and conventions.

Variable Source Notes $ctx / $gl.ctx caller bindings business context, dual-entry same source $params / $gl.parameter caller params script parameter input, dual-entry same source $input caller bindings previous step output in pipelines $env engine execution metadata (execId, engine version, tenant, user, read-only) console engine logging, returned with ScriptResult Injected variables are filtered by the ScriptProfile.variables whitelist; $gl.ctx/$gl.parameter are kit-form entries governed by the namespaces whitelist instead.

In Spring environments the engine is auto-configured via geelato.script.engine.*; consumers add profiles, revisions, data sources (dataSourceSupplier) and ORM supplies (daoSupplier/ormWrapper) through a ScriptEngineCustomizer bean. The SDK does not bind how data sources are located.
This page describes how to write platform scripts: structure, variables, the six built-in kits ($gl.*), the write channel and dry-run, error handling and best practices.

A script is a statement block ending in return; the returned value is the result. JavaScript is the default language (lang optionally python). const rows = $gl.sql.query(` SELECT id AS biz_id, eco_no AS biz_no, not_written_off FROM grant_apply WHERE not_written_off > :minAmount `, { minAmount: $gl.parameter.get('minAmount') }); return rows.filter(r => r.NOT_WRITTEN_OFF > 0) .map(r => ({ bizType: 'BOL_GRANT', bizId: r.BIZ_ID, bizNo: r.BIZ_NO })); In multi-step pipelines (e.g. exception judgment pipeline_json.steps), every step after the first can read the previous output via $input.

Variable Notes $ctx / $gl.ctx.get(key) / $gl.ctx.all() business context injected by the caller $params / $gl.parameter.get(key) / $gl.parameter.all() script parameters (thresholds, etc.) $input previous step output in pipelines $env read-only execution metadata (execId, engineVersion, profileId, tenantCode, user) console logging (log/info/warn/error/debug)

Named parameters (:name); queries are capped by sql.row-limit (default 10000) and sql.query-timeout-ms (default 10s). Method Description $gl.sql.query(sql, params) returns an array of rows; row count feeds the execution rowCount $gl.sql.queryOne(sql, params) single row or null $gl.sql.queryValue(sql, params) single value or null $gl.sql.update(sql, params) write statement, returns {affected, dryRun} $gl.sql.execute(sql) DDL / no-parameter statement, same gating as update

$gl.sql resolves the physical tables referenced by a statement (via connection registration: platform_dev_table.connect_id / @Entity(connectId) / catalog mapping) and routes in three tiers by how each table's database relates to the executing database: Case Behavior All tables local to the executing database (incl. unregistered ones) executed as-is on the direct connection, zero overhead Same server, different database database-name prefix added automatically (e.g. `bizdb`.`t`), still executed on the executing connection; transaction and dry-run rollback semantics unchanged Cross-server / heterogeneous sources federated execution via Apache Calcite: per-source filters and projections are pushed down; cross-source joins/aggregations run in application memory (not a distributed engine; large results are bounded by row limit and timeout) Boundaries: cross-server write statements are rejected outright (no cross-database transaction guarantee); unregistered tables, already qualified names, CTE aliases, and unparsable statements pass through unchanged; a registered connection with no platform_dev_db_connect row fails hard. The same-server prefix rewrite replaces only the table-name text span; the rest of the statement (comments and hints included) is preserved verbatim. Routing decisions are recorded in the trace (sql/route entries) and KIT-XDB logs.

Input is an MQL JSON text (see the MQL guide); the method set mirrors the platform /meta/* endpoints (MetaController), and entity metadata drives data-source routing and identity. Method Mirrors Description $gl.mql.list(mqlJson) /meta/list single-entity query, returns {data, total, page, size} $gl.mql.multiList(mqlJson) /meta/multiList multi-entity query, returns {data: {entity: {data, total, page, size}}} $gl.mql.save(mqlJson) /meta/save/{biz} save, returns {pk, dryRun}; write-gated $gl.mql.batchSave(mqlJson) /meta/batchSave batch save, returns {pks, dryRun}; write-gated $gl.mql.multiSave(mqlJson) /meta/multiSave multi-entity save, returns {count, dryRun}; write-gated $gl.mql.delete(entityName, id) /meta/delete/{biz}/{id} delete by id (comma-separated multi-value), returns {affected, dryRun} $gl.mql.deleteByGql(mqlJson) /meta/delete2/{biz} delete by condition, returns {affected, dryRun}; write-gated $gl.mql.explain(mqlJson, op) — explain without executing (op=list/save/delete)

Gated by http.enabled (default off), a host http.allowlist (exact host, *. prefix, optional scheme://) and a http.timeout-ms ceiling. No certificate bypass. Method Description $gl.http.get(url, params, headers) GET, returns the body string $gl.http.post/put/patch(url, body, headers) body string as-is or JSON-serialized object $gl.http.delete(url, headers) DELETE $gl.http.request({method, url, params, body, headers, timeoutMs}) full request, returns {status, headers, body}

AES follows the platform AesUtils convention (AES/GCM, Base64(IV+ciphertext)); the key comes from geelato.script.engine.encrypt.aes-key and both methods throw when unset. Method Description $gl.encrypt.md5(text) 32-char lowercase hex $gl.encrypt.md5Short(text) 16-char slice [8,24) $gl.encrypt.aes(text) / $gl.encrypt.aesDecrypt(cipher) AES encrypt/decrypt

Write methods ($gl.sql.update/execute, $gl.mql.save/batchSave/multiSave/delete/deleteByGql) are gated uniformly: Master switch: geelato.script.engine.dao.write-enabled, default false — write calls throw when off; Dry-run: geelato.script.engine.dao.dry-run, default true — statements execute inside a transaction that is always rolled back, with dryRun: true in the result; ScriptExecution.dryRun overrides per execution.

Kit failures surface as script RUNTIME errors carrying the precise cause and configuration key (e.g. "SQL 写通道未启用（geelato.script.engine.dao.write-enabled）"). Use try/catch to convert them to business semantics when appropriate.

Select only what you need: explicit column lists, paging (@p) or WHERE windows; Always parameterize: named parameters, never string concatenation; Explain first: validate complex MQL via $gl.mql.explain before going live; Leave traces: console.log/warn on key branches; Fail explicitly: do not swallow exceptions or mask errors with empty arrays.

The search engine follows a port-adapter split: geelato-search-api defines the contract, geelato-search-lucene is the reference implementation. Business systems can replace it with another engine (e.g. Elasticsearch) or extend routing without changing engines.

cn.geelato.search.api.SearchEngine is the single port: Method Description name() Engine name (logging and routing decisions) capabilities() Capability declaration (below) upsert(domainId, docs) Whole-document replace upsert (idempotent) delete(domainId, docIds) Delete documents search(domainId, query) Search; returns SearchResult (ids + truncated flag) health() UP / DEGRADED / DOWN The semantics-critical part of SearchEngineCapabilities is the consistency declaration: SYNC_FAIL_FAST for embedded engines (like Lucene; write failures fail fast with the compensation queue as safety net), ASYNC_EVENTUAL for remote engines (like ES; the framework adjusts reconciliation expectations accordingly).

Result equivalence: search means "multi-keyword OR × multi-field contains", strictly aligned with the SQL-level gfn_fuzzymatch multi-word OR; any mismatch causes routing to miss documents. tenant/delStatus/appId filter fields are written with each document and must be applied from SearchQuery. Report truncated honestly: when hits exceed maxIdsLimit, return truncated=true; routing will abandon the route. TCK: SearchEngineContractTest in geelato-search-api must pass fully — it guarantees implementations are interchangeable without semantic drift.

Implement SearchEngine against geelato-search-api. Register it as a Spring Bean (at most one engine bean is wired; use @Primary when several exist). Pass the TCK. Backfill: once the engine supports bulk loading, reuse POST /api/search/reindex/{domainId} — SearchReindexService writes via SearchEngine.upsert, so it works for any engine. Index sync (ORM save/delete listeners), the compensation queue, daily reconciliation and reindex orchestration are engine-agnostic and inherited automatically.
documents.s: Steps to Plug in a Custom Engine

documents.t: L2 routing plugs in through core's cn.geelato.core.mql.spi.MqlFuzzymatchRouter SPI: MqlQueryProcessor calls MqlFuzzymatchRouteResolver, which takes at most one Router bean from the context (more than one throws; none logs at debug and falls back to SQL). LuceneFuzzymatchRouter is the default implementation: ① per-condition replacement of top-level predicates; ② whole-group replacement of or-bracketed groups (all fuzzymatch conditions with identical keywords).

If any of the following holds, routing must be abandoned and SQL used (info log with reason) — this is the baseline of result equivalence: Constraint Reason Domain not backfilled (no marker watermark) Incomplete index; id IN (...) would miss documents Keyword contains regex metacharacters Cannot be aligned with L1 REGEXP semantics Token length < 2 NGram(2,2) has no 1-gram; contains semantics diverge Re-assembled tokens ≠ whole pattern Alignment check with stored-function quirks fails Column not mappable to a domain field (incl. view column-map) Routing target unknown Hits exceed maxIds (truncated) Truncated sets cannot be used for equivalent routing Empty hits re-inject the always-false value __search_no_match__, so "no search hits = no SQL rows".

The Elasticsearch implementation is design + TCK skeleton only (SearchEngineCapabilities.ASYNC_EVENTUAL is reserved); no implementation module exists yet. Implementing the contract and passing the TCK allows a seamless swap — MQL syntax and domain configuration stay unchanged.

The Geelato search engine accelerates fuzzymatch multi-number fuzzy search in MQL. A typical query — "one document's numbers are spread across multiple columns of the main table and multiple rows of child tables; hitting any number hits the document" — originally relied on the database stored function gfn_fuzzymatch, which degrades into a full table scan on large tables (measured 3s+ on 1.44M rows). The search engine equivalently offloads such predicates to an embedded search engine while keeping result sets strictly identical to the original SQL: Layer Condition Mechanism Status L1 REGEXP rewrite Default, zero config gfn_fuzzymatch(col,'kw')>0 rewritten at SQL level to (col<>'' AND col REGEXP ?) Implemented L2 Lucene routing Domain configured + reindexed fuzzymatch predicates routed to an embedded Lucene inverted index (NRT + NGram contains); matched ids re-injected as id IN (...) Implemented, behind experiment gate L3 Sync & compensation Automatic with L2 ORM save/delete events sync the index asynchronously; failures go to the search_sync_fail retry queue; daily update_at watermark reconciliation Implemented Boundary: the source of truth is always the database; the engine only answers "which ids match". Joins, paging, sorting and data-permission filtering stay in SQL — the index is only an accelerator and lagging indexes affect freshness, not correctness.

Concept Description Search domain Retrieval model of one document: id, mainEntity, pkField (default id), fields[], plus children[] aggregations (entity + FK fkField + fields[]). Child-entity changes rebuild the parent document automatically Document Document id = main-entity primary key; fieldValues is multi-valued — main-table fields single value, aggregated child fields multiple values Query Multi-keyword OR × multi-field contains (aligned with gfn_fuzzymatch); optional tenantCode/delStatus/appId filters; maxIds default 50000 Truncation A truncated hit set cannot be used for equivalent routing (re-injecting ids would miss documents); routing must fall back to SQL

Dependency: quickstart already includes geelato-search-api + geelato-search-lucene. Configure a domain (geelato.search.domains.*): geelato.search.domains[0].id=il_eco geelato.search.domains[0].main-entity=il_eco geelato.search.domains[0].pk-field=id geelato.search.domains[0].fields[0]=soNo geelato.search.domains[0].fields[1]=mblNo geelato.search.domains[0].fields[2]=containerNo # child-entity aggregation #geelato.search.domains[0].children[0].entity=il_so_container_fee_detail #geelato.search.domains[0].children[0].fk-field=orderId #geelato.search.domains[0].children[0].fields[0]=containerNo # view-entity routing map #geelato.search.domains[0].route-entities.vt_eco_view.pk-column=id #geelato.search.domains[0].route-entities.vt_eco_view.column-map.so_no=soNo Backfill: POST /api/search/reindex/{domainId}, poll GET /api/search/reindex/{domainId}/progress until finished=true. Domains without a completed reindex never participate in routing. Automatic routing: fuzzymatch conditions on that domain route automatically (zero business-code changes); index sync hooks ORM save/delete events.

Endpoint Description POST /api/search/reindex/{domainId} Trigger backfill (idempotent, domain-exclusive) GET /api/search/reindex/{domainId}/progress Backfill progress GET /api/search/domains / health / debug/{domainId} Domain list / engine health / debug info GET /api/search-ops/consistency / compensation / watermarks Read-only data for the ops page GET /search-ops.html Ops page (consistency / compensation queue / watermarks)

Key Default Description enabled true Master switch; false keeps L1 fallback and skips index writes index-root-dir data/search-index Index directory (one sub-directory per domain) max-ids 50000 Routing hit cap; over the cap routing is abandoned reindex-batch-size 500 Backfill batch size compensation-cron 0 * * * * ? Compensation retry schedule reconcile-cron 0 0 2 * * ? Daily watermark reconciliation retry-backoff-minutes [1,5,30,120] Compensation backoff (over max-retry-count=16 → DEAD, manual intervention) domains[].{...} — Domain definitions

L2 query routing (including the L1 rewrite) is gated by the experiment feature gate: a build-time whitelist constant ExperimentFeatures.SEARCH plus request header X-Gl-Experiments: search. Index sync/compensation/reconciliation are not gated (controlled by geelato.search.enabled), so you can warm indexes first and open query routing on your own release rhythm. See Extending the Search Engine.

SecurityContext is the thread-level security context: it holds the current thread's user, tenant, password, and application through ThreadLocal variables, and is the single entry for reading "who is current" at runtime. This page documents the four dimensions, the judgment methods, the write boundary, and cross-thread propagation.

Dimension Held type Meaning Written by threadUser User Current user principal The security chain after successful authentication threadTenant Tenant Current tenant The security chain after successful authentication threadPassword String Current request credential The security chain after successful authentication threadApp App Current application (subsystem) Subsystem identification scenarios

Method Semantics setCurrentUser(User) / getCurrentUser() Write/read the current user setCurrentTenant(Tenant) / getCurrentTenant() Write/read the current tenant setCurrentPassword(String) / getCurrentPassword() Write/read the current credential setCurrentApp(App) / getCurrentApp() Write/read the current application clear() Clears all four dimensions

Method Semantics isDelegated() Whether the current operation is a delegation: the current user's delegateUserId is non-empty getDelegateUserId() The delegate's ID, null when there is no current user isAdmin() Iterates the current user's direct roles (userRoles); true if any code contains "admin" isSystemPrincipal() Whether the current thread runs as a system background principal: decided by the currentUser.systemPrincipal flag, set explicitly by background jobs when establishing the context (e.g. ScheduleHelper.wrapWithContext) :::warning isAdmin historical semantics isAdmin() reads direct roles only, not org-attached roles — which differs from the union semantics of User.getEffectiveRoles(). Source comments declare this difference a preserved contract (historical consumer behavior unchanged); new code checking effective roles should use getEffectiveRoles(). :::

SecurityContext follows two hard constraints: It is a thread-level context whose lifetime matches the request. The security principal can only be set inside the security chain after successful authentication. Today, authentication and principal writing belong to the platform-side DefaultSecurityInterceptor: in preHandle() it routes by the Authorization prefix to the matching TokenAuthenticator, and after the scheme gate, cache restore, and credential check succeed, it uniformly writes the current user, tenant, and password into SecurityContext (flow details in Authentication & Authorization). The generic SecurityContextFilter never sets the principal; it only runs SecurityContext.clear() in a finally block when the request ends. Why: Filters sit at the generic request entrance and must not trust principal information the frontend could declare directly; The principal can only come from the internal chain after successful authentication; Clearing once at request end prevents thread-reuse principal leaks and dirty contexts left by failed requests. Usage constraints: Controllers and services only read SecurityContext; never fabricate a pseudo-principal in business code; Never parse headers in a generic filter and write them straight into the context; To add a new authentication method, implement the TokenAuthenticator SPI — see Authenticator Extension (SPI).

The four dimensions are plain ThreadLocals and do not travel across thread switches (the framework uses neither InheritableThreadLocal nor TransmittableThreadLocal). An async task that needs the current principal must explicitly wrap itself with SecurityContextRunnable — a capture-replay pattern: Factory method Semantics wrap(Runnable) Captures the current thread's User/Tenant automatically (captured at submission time) wrap(Runnable, User, Tenant) Explicit values, for scheduled jobs and other contexts without HTTP wrap(Runnable, User) Explicit User; Tenant captured from the current thread run() sequence: setCurrentUser/setCurrentTenant on entry → run delegate.run() → SecurityContext.clear() in finally (cleared after the task, so pool threads stay clean). // Capture the current thread's context automatically CompletableFuture.runAsync(SecurityContextRunnable.wrap(() -> { // SecurityContext.getCurrentUser() works here })); // Explicit user (for scheduled jobs without HTTP context) CompletableFuture.runAsync(SecurityContextRunnable.wrap(() -> { ... }, overrideUser, overrideTenant)); Two notes: Only User/Tenant propagate; password/app do not. The wrapper is a Runnable, so any executor accepting Runnable works (CompletableFuture, custom pools, etc.).

Facility Location Pattern EngineContextExecutor geelato-exception Save original context → replace → restore in finally; offers withContext/withSystemContext (cross-tenant)/withEngineContext/withParticipantPrincipal (participant identity delegation) AlertContextExecutor geelato-alert withContext (injects a system principal when no session exists)/withParticipantPrincipal ScheduleHelper.wrapWithContext Host-side scheduler Establishes the context for background jobs with a system principal (systemPrincipal=true)
documents.s: Context Facilities with the Same Pattern

documents.t: SecurityContext is a thread-level context of four ThreadLocal dimensions: user / tenant / password / app; clear() empties them all at once. The write boundary is hard: principals are written only by the security chain after successful authentication, and filters are responsible only for cleanup at request end. Cross-thread propagation is never automatic — async tasks must explicitly use SecurityContextRunnable.wrap(...) (capture-replay with finally cleanup); among the judgment methods, isAdmin reading direct roles only is historical semantics — use getEffectiveRoles() for effective roles.
Authentication & Authorization — who writes the principal Security Model — the User/Tenant objects inside the context Global Context — the request-scoped general context

This page documents the three snapshot loader SPIs and the two loading helper contracts of geelato-security. Loaders are the assembly boundary from "external security data" to "immutable snapshots": the framework and platform never read the database directly — data is assembled into snapshots through these three interfaces and cached by providers (see Provider Contracts).

Interface Method Semantics OrgSnapshotLoader OrgSnapshot load() Load the org snapshot UserSnapshotLoader UserSnapshot load(UserOrgInfoEnricher userOrgInfoEnricher) Load the user snapshot RoleSnapshotLoader RoleSnapshot load() Load the role snapshot Each interface has a single load() method. Contract points: Single responsibility: assemble external data into a complete snapshot in one pass; every call returns a freshly built snapshot, no incremental loading. Replaceable by upper layers: the interface javadoc states "allows the upper layer to replace the default platform-table reading implementation" — the default implementation reads the platform primary DB (JDBC), and a host project can swap it entirely for an external service, config center, Redis, aggregation API, or any other source. Why UserSnapshotLoader carries an enricher parameter: the user's org-derived fields (department / company / extension ID) depend on org relation resolution; the loader delegates that enrichment to the injected UserOrgInfoEnricher instead of depending on OrgProvider itself. The loader calls enrich(UserOrg) and enrich(User) one by one during assembly.
Two enrichers act as fillers during loading, populating derived and extension fields of the model.

Method Semantics enrich(User user) Fill the user's org-derived fields: orgName/companyId/companyName/extendId/buId/buName/deptId/defaultOrgName enrich(UserOrg userOrg) Fill one attachment's derived fields: name/deptId/companyId/extendId/fullName The data comes from org relation resolution (it depends on org data), so the default implementation takes an OrgProvider in its constructor.

Method Semantics enrich(User user) Fill User.extendInfo while the user snapshot is being loaded The data source (binding tables / configuration / auth center) is decided by the upper layer; key conventions are defined by consumers (e.g. the git operations module) and the User layer never knows key meanings. The default implementation is a no-op (no extension info bound); see Platform Defaults.

load() returns a newly built immutable snapshot every time; the loading thread publishes only after the build completes — readers never observe the loading process. A provider's refresh() calls load() and then swaps the snapshot reference atomically; the refresh chain is described in Snapshots & Loading. When replacing a loader implementation, keep the refresh() semantics stable: reload the latest snapshot, and never implement refresh() as a side-effectful heavy transaction.

The loader SPI is three load() methods: org, user, and role; their job is assembling external sources into immutable snapshots, and the default JDBC implementation can be replaced wholesale. Two enrichers fill derived data: UserOrgInfoEnricher fills org-derived fields (resolved via OrgProvider), UserExtInfoEnricher fills extendInfo (source decided by the upper layer). The enricher parameter on UserSnapshotLoader.load is a deliberate dependency-direction design: loaders never depend on providers.

This page documents the security model defined by geelato-security, attribute by attribute: six core entities, four attachment relation classes, and the relation rules between them. All classes live in the cn.geelato.security package as pure data contracts (POJOs) with no source or storage details; the platform DB column mapping is covered in Platform Defaults.

The org model has two layers: OrgCore carries the tree structure and tenant ownership; Org adds company ownership and node type.

0 female, 1 male (UserSexEnum) avatar String Avatar mobilePrefix String Mobile country dialing prefix mobilePhone String Mobile number telephone String Landline number email String Email post String Position nationCode String Country/region code provinceCode String Province code cityCode String City code address String Detailed address Org ownership and derivations (filled during loading by UserOrgInfoEnricher, see Loading Abstractions): Attribute Type Meaning orgId String The department or section the user is directly attached to; UserProvider.getUserByExtendKey looks users up by key type. Delegation (acting on behalf): Attribute Type Meaning delegateUserId String The delegate (actual executor) ID; empty means the user acted personally delegateUserName String The delegate's name Semantics: when an operation is executed by a delegate, creator/updater still record the effective identity (the delegating user); delegateUserId/delegateUserName exist only for audit — "who acted for whom". The same semantics apply when an engine (system principal) writes on a user's behalf: effective identity = owning user, delegate fields = engine system identity. They are different concepts. ::: Principal flag: Attribute Type Meaning systemPrincipal boolean Whether this is a system background principal (scheduled jobs and other contexts without HTTP). Full-snapshot permission loading belongs to the auth-center implementation (AuthCenterSecurityProvider). :::

Method Semantics getEffectiveRoles() Effective roles = direct roles (userRoles) ∪ org-attached roles (userOrgRoles), deduplicated by role code. The unified entry for effective-role semantics; historical consumers (e.g. SecurityContext.isAdmin) keep reading direct roles only, unchanged getDataPermissionByEntity(String entity) Per-entity data permission: filters dataPermissions by matching entity and takes the rule with the largest weight (first one on ties); returns null when the collection is missing or nothing matches setupOrgInfo(OrgProvider orgProvider) Legacy compatibility entry: fills orgName/companyId/companyName/extendId/buId/buName/deptId (when empty)/defaultOrgName via OrgProvider. New code should prefer UserOrgInfoEnricher

Attribute Type Meaning Id String Role ID. Note the field name starts with a capital letter; the getters/setters are getId/setId code String Role code; business code and data-permission rules always reference roles by code (stable across environments), never by ID name String Role name type String Role type, see table below tenantCode String Owning tenant code Platform values of type (RoleTypeEnum): Value Meaning platform Platform-level role app Application-level role

Attribute Type Meaning code String Permission code, the reference identifier (hasPermission matches on code) entity String Entity the permission belongs to; data permissions take effect per entity name String Permission name rule String Permission rule expression. For data permissions it is a filter condition that may contain #currentUser.xxx# variables; for element permissions it is the element identifier weight Integer Data-permission weight; among multiple rules on one entity the largest weight wins roleWeight Integer Weight of the source role (carried when the permission is inherited through a role)

PermissionRuleUtils.replaceRuleVariable(Permission, User) replaces user variables in rule with the current user's field values before querying. Syntax: #currentUser.field#, with #currentUser.defaultOrg.field# supported to reach fields of the default org object. Allowed field whitelist (strict camelCase; anything outside it throws IllegalArgumentException): Category Allowed fields Basic user fields userId, orgId, defaultOrgId, cooperatingOrgId, companyId, extendId, deptId, buId, weixinUnionId, weixinWorkUserId, tenantCode defaultOrg object fields defaultOrg.orgId, defaultOrg.deptId, defaultOrg.companyId, defaultOrg.extendId Replacement behavior: A non-empty field value is replaced with a quoted string literal (e.g. #currentUser.userId# → '123456'); empty values are replaced with null. When merging multiple rules (replaceRuleVariable(List<Permission>, User)), rules are deduplicated, whitespace-normalized, wrapped in parentheses, and joined with OR. After replacement, any remaining #...# placeholder throws an exception (carrying entity name, original rule, and the placeholder list) — unresolved variables never reach a query.

The membership relation between a user and an organization; one user may attach to multiple orgs. Attribute Type Meaning (inherited) — orgId (attached org ID)/code/pid/name/tenantCode fullName String Full org name (full path; filled from name by the enricher when empty) deptId String Parent department ID of this org (derived) companyId String Owning company ID (derived) extendId String Company extension ID of the owning company (derived) defaultOrg Boolean Whether this is the default org; true means this attachment is the user's default department type String Org type, same values as Org.type category String Org category, see table below description String Description Platform values of category (OrgCategoryEnum): Value Meaning inside Internal outside External virtual Virtual
A role attached directly to the user; no extra fields. The role is granted to the user without going through an org.

The user-org role contract model: a userId × orgId × roleId triple (userId is implicit when embedded in a User snapshot). Attribute Type Meaning (inherited) — Role fields, see Role orgId String Source org of the role (the org the role is attached to) Semantics: the only way a department role takes effect for a user — the user is attached through this relation. The user does not have to be a member of the source org (membership is UserOrg, an independent relation that grants no role inheritance).

The org-attached role contract model (a role attached to an org). Attribute Type Meaning (inherited) — Role fields, see Role orgId String The org (department) the role is attached to Semantics: the role is attached to an org (department) and provided by that department. Only direct departments take effect — no upward recursion along the tree. The attachment itself never grants the role to members automatically; for a user it takes effect only via a direct UserOrgRole.

Attribute Type Meaning userRoles List<UserRole> Direct roles userOrgRoles List<UserOrgRole> Org-attached roles (department roles, orgId = source org) getEffectiveRoles() shares the semantics of User.getEffectiveRoles(): direct ∪ org-attached, deduplicated by code.
documents.s: UserRoles (aggregate of the two attachment results)

documents.t: Org tree: Org nodes link through pid, empty at the root; type marks the node type. Relation resolution (department/company ownership) walks up the parent chain with a visited set guarding against cycles. User-org: many-to-many attachments (UserOrg), defaultOrg=true marks the default; when User.orgId is empty it is resolved from attachments (default org first, then the first attachment). Two role grant shapes: direct (UserRole) and department role (UserOrgRole, userId × orgId × roleId — the user need not be a member of that org). Both are user-side relations. Role-org attachment (OrgRole): a role attached to a department; only direct departments take effect, no recursion. The attachment never auto-grants members — user-side effect requires a direct UserOrgRole. Effective roles: direct ∪ org-attached, deduplicated by code, always taken from getEffectiveRoles(). Company ownership: take the first ancestor with type=company along the parent chain, falling back to the top-level ancestor when none exists; companyId/companyName/extendId/buId/buName derive from it. Data permission effect: grouped by entity, the rule with the largest weight wins (getDataPermissionByEntity); multiple rules are merged with OR after variable replacement. System principal: systemPrincipal=true skips data-permission filtering but keeps tenant isolation — for scheduled jobs and other background scenarios. Delegation: the effective identity is the delegating user (written to creator/updater); delegateUserId/delegateUserName record the actual executor for audit only.

The model layer is a pure data contract: entities (tenant / app / org / user / role / permission) + relation classes (org attachment and the three role attachment shapes), with no source details. The user is the center: org- and company-ownership fields are all derived values filled by enrichers at loading; permission collections are not loaded by default (auth-center domain). Effective-role semantics converge on getEffectiveRoles(): direct ∪ org-attached deduplicated by code; the only way a department role takes effect for a user is a direct UserOrgRole. Data permissions take effect per entity by the largest weight; rule variables support a strict whitelist and unresolved placeholders hard-fail.

geelato-security is the security contract module of the framework: it only defines the security model, read interfaces, loading mechanisms, and context contracts — it never binds to a concrete data source. Runtime consumers (authentication, org enrichment, participant resolution, data permission) program against these contracts only; where the data comes from is decided by the implementation layer and is invisible to consumers.

geelato-security is a pure contract module: its pom carries no framework dependencies (only Lombok), and all contracts live in a single package cn.geelato.security. Implementations are distributed across two upper modules; all three deliberately share the same package name (split package) to keep consumer imports consistent: Layer Module Content Contracts geelato-security Security model (Tenant/App/Org/User/Role/Permission), attachment relation classes, four Provider interfaces, three snapshot & loader SPIs, SecurityContext, SecurityContextRunnable Framework defaults geelato-core DefaultOrgProvider/DefaultUserProvider/DefaultRoleProvider, OrgRelationResolver, BridgeSecurityProvider, the two default Enrichers, SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator Platform defaults geelato-web-platform DBOrgSnapshotLoader/DBUserSnapshotLoader/DBRoleSnapshotLoader (primary DB readers), SecurityProviderConfiguration assembly

Key points: Loading always flows Loader → Snapshot → Provider: loaders assemble external data into immutable snapshots, providers cache the snapshot and expose read-only queries, and consumers depend on providers only. Snapshots are loaded as a whole and swapped atomically (AtomicReference); the read side is lock-free and a refresh never exposes a half-new, half-old state. SecurityProvider coexists with the three snapshot providers: the former serves on-demand single-point queries (people resolution, hierarchy traversal, decision checks), the latter serve full-snapshot reads — each has its own job.

The security contract answers "what does security data look like, where is it read from, and how does it enter the context"; authentication answers "how does one HTTP request get authenticated and write the principal into the context". The latter belongs to the platform side (DefaultSecurityInterceptor lives in geelato-web-common); see Authentication & Authorization.
