This page documents every default implementation of the security contracts by layer, together with the Spring assembly and the replacement paths for host projects. Contracts live in geelato-security; framework-layer defaults (snapshot providers, bridging, refresh coordination) live in geelato-core; platform-layer JDBC loaders and the unified assembly live in geelato-web-platform. All three share the package name cn.geelato.security (a split package, kept deliberately for import consistency).

Layer Module Defaults Framework geelato-core DefaultOrgProvider, OrgRelationResolver (package-private), DefaultUserProvider, DefaultRoleProvider, DefaultUserOrgInfoEnricher, DefaultUserExtInfoEnricher, BridgeSecurityProvider, SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator Platform geelato-web-platform DBOrgSnapshotLoader, DBUserSnapshotLoader, DBRoleSnapshotLoader, SecurityProviderConfiguration (assembly) The default architecture in one sentence: loaders assemble the platform primary DB into snapshots (platform layer), providers cache the snapshots and expose read-only queries (framework layer), and every bean is assembled @ConditionalOnMissingBean so it can be replaced wholesale.

Constructor takes an OrgSnapshotLoader; internally it holds an AtomicReference<OrgSnapshot> and an AtomicReference<OrgRelationResolver>. Method Implementation getOrg Current snapshot's getOrg getAllOrgs All orgs of the current snapshot (value-copied into an ArrayList) getDeptId Delegates to OrgRelationResolver.resolveDeptId getCompanyId Delegates to OrgRelationResolver.resolveCompanyId getCompanyName resolveCompanyOrg → the company entity's name, "" when absent getCompanyExtendId resolveCompanyOrg → the company entity's extendId, null when absent refresh loader.load(), then atomically swaps both references (snapshot and resolver)

A relation resolver over the full org index (orgId → Org); every resolution walks up the parent chain with a visited set guarding against cycles. Method Resolution rule resolveDeptId(orgId) If the org itself is a department, return it; otherwise walk the parent chain for the first department ancestor; when none exists, return the top-level ancestor (last node of the chain) resolveCompanyId(orgId) Delegates to resolveCompanyOrg for the ID, "" when absent resolveCompanyExtendId(orgId) Delegates to resolveCompanyOrg for the extendId, null when absent resolveCompanyOrg(orgId) If the org itself is a company, return it; otherwise take the first ancestor with type=company along the parent chain, falling back to the top-level ancestor when none exists; null when the org does not exist This implements the "company ownership" rule from Security Model: company first, top-level fallback.

Constructor takes a UserSnapshotLoader + UserOrgInfoEnricher (+ optional UserExtInfoEnricher); it holds an AtomicReference<UserSnapshot>. Method Implementation getUser Current snapshot's getUser getAllUsers All users of the current snapshot (value-copied), consumed by BridgeSecurityProvider for reverse resolution getUserByExtendKey Normalizes via normalizeType, then queries the snapshot's extended-identity two-level index refresh loader.load(userOrgInfoEnricher) → per-user enrich via the ext enricher when present → atomically swap the snapshot reference
Same pattern as DefaultOrgProvider: constructor takes a RoleSnapshotLoader; getRole/getRoleByCode/getOrgRoles query the snapshot directly, and refresh loads then swaps atomically.

Constructor takes an OrgProvider, relying on the org snapshot for derived resolution. enrich(User): orgId takes firstNonBlank(user.orgId, resolveOrgId(user)); resolveOrgId picks the first attachment with defaultOrg=true from userOrgs, falling back to the first non-empty attachment. Once resolved, it fills: orgName, companyId, companyName, extendId, buId (= companyId), buName (= companyName); when deptId is empty it fills getDeptId. defaultOrgId is resolved the same way (defaultOrg=true first) and defaultOrgName is filled. enrich(UserOrg): when orgId is non-empty, fills name (when empty), deptId, companyId, extendId; fullName falls back to name when empty.
The default no-op: when the upper layer provides no filler, extendInfo stays empty (no extension info bound).

The local-DB bridging implementation of the SecurityProvider contract: it combines the data planes of the existing OrgProvider/UserProvider/RoleProvider and derives contract queries (including people resolution and the org tree) locally, without any remote calls — for subsystems sharing the platform DB or network, where the auth center is unnecessary. Data-plane requirements: Capability Depends on Forward single/batch queries The single-query capability of the three providers People resolution (people under a department/role/department role) UserProvider.getAllUsers() (snapshot implementations support it natively; direct-lookup implementations returning empty make people resolution return empty too) Org tree (sub-orgs / ancestor chain) OrgProvider.getAllOrgs(); the ancestor chain only needs single queries (walking up by pid), no full list required Role-related queries RoleProvider; degrades to empty/null when absent (null) Implementation matrix: Contract method group Implementation Single-entity queries Fully implemented; getUserByLoginName goes through the loginName extended key; getOrgByCode scans all orgs matching by code Batch queries Per-ID single queries aggregated; missing IDs are skipped People resolution In-memory filtering over getAllUsers: departments by membership (userOrgs.orgId hits the target org set), roles by direct role code, department roles by userOrgRoles orgId+code (the user need not be a member); results deduplicated by user Paging Results sorted by userId then sliced, keeping pagination stable under the same data snapshot querySubOrgs Builds a pid → direct-children index from all orgs, expands level by level with BFS, visited set guarding cycles queryAncestorOrgs Walks up the pid chain, excluding itself queryOrgRoles Aggregates RoleProvider.getOrgRoles over each target org (optionally including descendants) Permission queries Not implemented, keeping the default empty return — permission-domain data belongs to the auth center; use its AuthCenterSecurityProvider Every call derives from the providers' current snapshots immediately, keeping no cache of its own — naturally consistent with provider refresh semantics.

The unified refresh coordinator for the three snapshots; the method semantics and refresh chain are in Snapshots & Loading. Assembly note here: UserProvider/RoleProvider are @Autowired(required = false), so direct-lookup implementations managing their own data plane can omit them.
All three DB loaders take the @Qualifier("primaryJdbcTemplate") JdbcTemplate in their constructors and read only rows with del_status = 0.

Item Content Source platform_org Query select id, pid, name, tenant_code, type, code, extend_id from platform_org where del_status = 0 Assembly Skips rows with empty id, builds orgById in load order (LinkedHashMap), and publishes via OrgSnapshot.from

Four query stages, assembled into userById stage by stage: Stage Source Assembly 1. User basics platform_user where del_status = 0: id/login_name/name/tenant_code/weixin_unionId/weixin_work_userId User objects; also builds the three extended-identity indexes loginName/weixinUnionId/weixinWorkUserId 2. Direct roles platform_role join platform_role_r_user (both del_status = 0) UserRole (id/code/name/type/tenantCode) 3. Org-attached roles platform_user_r_org_role join platform_role (both del_status = 0) UserOrgRole (role fields + org_id) 4. Org attachments platform_org_r_user where del_status = 0: user_id/org_id/org_name/default_org UserOrg; default_org judged as "1" or true; each row passes through userOrgInfoEnricher.enrich(uo); when defaultOrg=true, fills back user.orgId/user.defaultOrgId Finale: per-user enrich(user) fills derived fields; userRoles/userOrgs/userOrgRoles become empty lists when null, otherwise List.copyOf immutabilized; finally UserSnapshot.from(userById, extendIndex) publishes.

Item Content Role entities SELECT id, code, name, type, tenant_code FROM platform_role WHERE del_status = 0 → roleById; fields normalized with trimToNull Org-attached roles SELECT org_id, role_id FROM platform_org_r_role WHERE del_status = 0 → copies the role into an OrgRole (copyRole) with orgId; joins whose role is missing are skipped Publish RoleSnapshot.from(roleById, orgRolesByOrgId)

cn.geelato.web.platform.boot.SecurityProviderConfiguration in geelato-web-platform provides 10 default beans, all @ConditionalOnMissingBean — as soon as the host defines a bean of the same type, the default assembly steps aside: Bean Default class Dependencies OrgSnapshotLoader DBOrgSnapshotLoader primaryJdbcTemplate OrgProvider DefaultOrgProvider orgSnapshotLoader UserOrgInfoEnricher DefaultUserOrgInfoEnricher orgProvider UserExtInfoEnricher DefaultUserExtInfoEnricher — UserSnapshotLoader DBUserSnapshotLoader primaryJdbcTemplate UserProvider DefaultUserProvider userSnapshotLoader + userOrgInfoEnricher + userExtInfoEnricher RoleSnapshotLoader DBRoleSnapshotLoader primaryJdbcTemplate RoleProvider DefaultRoleProvider roleSnapshotLoader SecurityProvider BridgeSecurityProvider orgProvider + userProvider + roleProvider SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator orgProvider + userProvider + roleProvider Notes: Platform applications do not depend on geelato-auth-client, so there is no remote-implementation competition; subsystems integrated with the auth center get AuthCenterSecurityProvider (an open-API implementation, not in this repository) auto-assembled by auth-client, which does not interfere with this bean. At startup, SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator's @PostConstruct completes the first load of the three snapshots; at runtime OrgController.refreshOrg()/UserController.refreshUser() trigger refreshes after directory changes.
Three replacement options, from smallest to largest change:

The user snapshot is incomplete, or org ownership needs extra derivation: provide a custom UserOrgInfoEnricher (org derivations) or UserExtInfoEnricher (extendInfo filling) bean — no need to touch the whole provider set. Fits feeding extendInfo with business binding data (git binding and other agreed keys).

You accept the default "snapshot + read-only query" model but the data source is not the platform DB: provide custom OrgSnapshotLoader/UserSnapshotLoader/RoleSnapshotLoader beans. You keep reusing Default*Provider, BridgeSecurityProvider, and SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator, while snapshot data can come from external services, a config center, Redis, or aggregation APIs. This is usually the more robust path.

You already have a complete org/user/role access model (external IAM, org-center API, no snapshot model): provide custom OrgProvider/UserProvider/RoleProvider (or SecurityProvider) beans directly. When replacing UserProvider, the extended identity mapping (getUserByExtendKey) must remain available, or WeChat/WeCom extended-key authentication breaks.
documents.s: Option 3: Replace Providers Wholly (data plane does not fit snapshots)

documents.t: A custom UserProvider minimally implements: getUser(String), getUserByExtendKey(String, String), refresh(). If the returned User already carries userRoles/userOrgs/userOrgRoles, the three relation queries' default implementations can be reused as-is. A custom OrgProvider minimally implements: getOrg(String), getDeptId(String), getCompanyId(String), refresh(). The runtime needs not only org names but also department and company/BU derivations — an incomplete relation resolution directly degrades the user's org-dimension context after authentication.

refresh() reloads the latest snapshot; never implement it as a side-effectful heavy transaction. Org resolution (getDeptId/getCompanyId/getCompanyName) keeps stable semantics; consumers include post-auth org-dimension backfill and snapshot loading. The three extended identity mappings (loginName/weixinUnionId/weixinWorkUserId) of getUserByExtendKey remain available.

Defaults come in two layers: the framework layer (geelato-core) provides snapshot providers, relation resolution, bridged queries, and refresh coordination; the platform layer (geelato-web-platform) provides the three JDBC loaders and the unified assembly. Company-ownership resolution converges in OrgRelationResolver: the first ancestor with type=company up the parent chain, top-level fallback when none exists. All assembly is @ConditionalOnMissingBean: enricher → loader → whole provider, an increasing scope of change; replacing loaders is the recommended integration path.

Loading Abstractions — the interfaces you implement when replacing loaders Snapshots & Loading — refresh chain and immutable semantics Permission Integration — unified permission management on the AuthServer side

This page documents the four Provider interfaces of geelato-security and the paging contract, method by method. Providers are the read boundary for security data: consumers depend on these interfaces only, never on concrete implementations; every method defines read capability only, with no storage or network details.

Interface Paradigm Responsibility OrgProvider Snapshot-style full read + refresh Org read queries and org relation resolution (department / company / BU) UserProvider Snapshot-style full read + refresh User read queries, relation reads, extended identity lookup RoleProvider Snapshot-style full read + refresh Role read queries, org-attached role queries SecurityProvider On-demand single-point queries Single / batch / people-resolution / hierarchy / permission / decision queries over four entities and four attachment relation types The first three serve snapshot-style full loading (paired with Loaders and Snapshots); SecurityProvider serves on-demand queries consumed by workflow assignee resolution, rule/exception alert participant resolution, and data-permission checks. The two paradigms coexist, each with its own job.

Method Signature Contract semantics getOrg Org getOrg(String orgId) Look up an org by ID, null when absent (abstract) getAllOrgs List<Org> getAllOrgs() All orgs; default returns an empty list, snapshot implementations should override containsOrg boolean containsOrg(String orgId) Whether the org exists; default derives from getOrg != null getOrgName String getOrgName(String orgId) Org name; default via getOrg, "" when absent getDeptId String getDeptId(String orgId) Org → owning department ID relation-resolution entry (abstract; the resolution rule is defined by the implementation) getCompanyId String getCompanyId(String orgId) Org → owning company ID relation-resolution entry (abstract) getCompanyName String getCompanyName(String orgId) Owning company name; default via getCompanyId. When no company exists on the chain it matches getCompanyId, taking the top-level ancestor getCompanyExtendId String getCompanyExtendId(String orgId) The company's extendId, same source as getCompanyId; falls back to the top-level ancestor's when no company exists getBuId String getBuId(String orgId) Business unit ID; default is getCompanyId refresh void refresh() Reload the snapshot (abstract) getDeptId/getCompanyId are not mere dictionary lookups but org-relation resolution entries: they derive department and company from tree relations. The default resolution algorithm (first department/company up the chain, top-level fallback) is documented in Platform Defaults.

Method Signature Contract semantics getUser User getUser(String userId) Look up a user by ID (abstract) getUserName String getUserName(String userId) User name; default via getUser, "" when absent getAllUsers List<User> getAllUsers() All users, including the userRoles/userOrgs/userOrgRoles attachments, so that SecurityProvider bridging can resolve people under departments/roles. Snapshot implementations should override; direct-lookup implementations may not support it (empty list, and the bridged people-resolution methods then return empty) containsUser boolean containsUser(String userId) Whether the user exists; default derives from getUser != null getUserById User getUserById(String userId) Same as getUser; default delegates getUserByExtendKey User getUserByExtendKey(String extendKey, String type) Look up a user by extended identity key (abstract); type is normalized by normalizeType getUserRoles List<UserRole> getUserRoles(String userId) Direct roles; default aggregates from User.userRoles, empty when absent getUserOrgs List<UserOrg> getUserOrgs(String userId) Org attachments; default aggregates from User.userOrgs getUserOrgRoles List<UserOrgRole> getUserOrgRoles(String userId) Org-attached roles; default aggregates from User.userOrgRoles normalizeType String normalizeType(String type) Extended key type normalization, see table below refresh void refresh() Reload the snapshot (abstract) normalizeType rules (case-insensitive): Input Normalized to loginName / login_name loginName weixinUnionId / weixin_unionId / unionId weixinUnionId weixinWorkUserId / weixin_work_userId / workUserId weixinWorkUserId anything else returned as-is This is why the runtime auth chain can use WeixinUnionId, WeixinWorkUserId, and similar extended identity entrances directly (see Authentication & Authorization).

Method Signature Contract semantics getRole Role getRole(String roleId) Look up by role ID, null when absent (abstract) getRoleByCode Role getRoleByCode(String roleCode) Look up by role code; business code always references roles by code (abstract) getOrgRoles List<OrgRole> getOrgRoles(String orgId) Roles attached to the org (department roles, direct department only, no upward recursion). Small cardinality, not paged; default returns an empty list refresh void refresh() Reload the snapshot (abstract)

The security data provider: on-demand single-point queries over four entities (org / user / role / permission) and four attachment relation types. Methods come in six groups, all default-empty so an integrating system can implement just the methods it needs. The constant MAX_AGGREGATE_SIZE = 10_000 caps list aggregation: exceeding it throws IllegalStateException — fail rather than silently truncate; use the paging overloads for large result sets.

Method Contract semantics getUserById(String userId) User by ID; null when absent or not visible getUserByLoginName(String loginName) User by login name (the find-person-by-login-name entry for notification/alerting) getOrgById(String orgId) Org by ID getOrgByCode(String orgCode) Org by code getRoleById(String roleId) Role by ID (backfill scenario: you already hold role IDs, e.g. results of getUserRoles/queryOrgRoles) getRoleByCode(String roleCode) Role by code (business code and data-permission rules always use code) getUserRoles(String userId) The user's roles as a UserRoles aggregate, separating direct roles from org-attached roles (with source org); effective roles via UserRoles.getEffectiveRoles() getUserOrgs(String userId) Org attachments (membership; multiple orgs returned together; unrelated to role attachment)

Method Contract semantics queryUsersByIds(List<String> userIds) Batch query by user IDs; empty ids return an empty list queryOrgsByIds(List<String> orgIds) Batch query by org IDs queryRolesByIds(List<String> roleIds) Batch query by role IDs

People resolution along three dimensions (org / role / org-role) is the high-frequency entry for workflows and alerting. Naming pattern: the fully-parameterized pageQuery* is the core abstraction (implement it); flag-less overloads are default derivations (recursive by default); the query* full lists are default auto-pagination aggregations. Method Contract semantics pageQueryUsersOfOrg(String orgId, boolean includeSubOrgs, PageParam pageParam) Paged people under a department (membership only, no role inheritance). includeSubOrgs=true includes the department and all its descendants (recursive, users deduplicated); false only the department itself. Core method — implement it pageQueryUsersOfOrg(String orgId, PageParam pageParam) Same, recursive by default queryUsersOfOrg(String orgId, boolean includeSubOrgs) Full list; default auto-pagination aggregation queryUsersOfOrg(String orgId) Same, recursive by default (department and all descendants, users deduplicated) pageQueryUsersOfRole(String roleCode, PageParam pageParam) Paged users directly attached to the role; queried by role code — business sides (workflow assignee configuration, alert rules) always store codes. Core method queryUsersOfRole(String roleCode) Full list; default auto-pagination aggregation pageQueryUsersOfOrgRole(String orgId, String roleCode, boolean includeSubOrgs, PageParam pageParam) Paged users of a department role (attached via "user-org role"; the user need not be a member of the department). Core method pageQueryUsersOfOrgRole(String orgId, String roleCode, PageParam pageParam) Same, recursive by default queryUsersOfOrgRole(String orgId, String roleCode, boolean includeSubOrgs) Full list; default auto-pagination aggregation queryUsersOfOrgRole(String orgId, String roleCode) Same, recursive by default Full aggregation is implemented by the static collectAll: pages of 200 until no next page; exceeding MAX_AGGREGATE_SIZE throws IllegalStateException.

Method Contract semantics queryOrgRoles(String orgId, boolean includeSubOrgs) Roles attached to the org (roles on orgs). true includes the department and all descendants; false only direct attachments. Core method, small cardinality, not paged queryOrgRoles(String orgId) Same, recursive by default querySubOrgs(String orgId, boolean recursive) Sub-departments. false only direct children; true all descendants (level by level). Core method querySubOrgs(String orgId) All descendants, excluding itself queryAncestorOrgs(String orgId) The ancestor chain from the direct parent to the root, excluding itself
documents.s: 4. Department roles and the org tree (hierarchy traversal)

documents.t: Method Contract semantics queryPermissionsOfRole(String roleId) Permissions assigned to the role. Org roles are roles attached to orgs — permissions take effect through roles, so one query serves both; queried by role ID (backfill scenario) queryPermissionsOfUser(String userId) The user's effective permissions: direct roles ∪ org-attached roles → role permissions, then ∪ directly granted user permissions. Data permissions take effect per entity by the largest weight (consumer-side logic)

Method Contract semantics hasRole(String userId, String roleCode) Whether the user has a role, judged by effective roles (direct ∪ org-attached); default derives from getUserRoles — override when you have a faster check (cache / dedicated endpoint) hasPermission(String userId, String permissionCode) Whether the user has a permission (permissions are identified by code); default derives from queryPermissionsOfUser — override for faster checks

Naming: Prefix Meaning get* Single-entity query (a single object, or a single user's aggregate view) query* Full list query pageQuery* Paged query Parameters: appCode/tenantCode are bound by the implementation (configuration or client identity); contract methods never carry tenant/subsystem parameters. Roles are always referenced by code (stable across environments); only batch role queries (queryRolesByIds) and role permission queries (queryPermissionsOfRole) take IDs — they serve backfill scenarios where you already hold ID lists or role objects, and are not business reference entrances. Orgs are always referenced by orgId; department-related people/role resolution carries an includeSubOrgs flag (true = the department and all descendants, recursively). Overloads without the flag default to recursive, all descendants; in querySubOrgs(orgId, recursive), recursive toggles direct children / all descendants. All methods are default-empty; implement only what you need.

Member Meaning DEFAULT_PAGE_NUM = 1 / DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 20 Default page number and size MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 500 Page-size cap pageNum Page number, starting at 1 pageSize Page size, clamped to [1, 500] by of() of(int pageNum, int pageSize) Constructor with clamping getOffset() Query offset, (pageNum - 1) * pageSize

Member Meaning items Current page data (null replaced by an empty list) total Total count pageNum / pageSize Page number and size hasMore Whether a next page exists (the termination signal for aggregation and paging) of(items, total, pageNum, pageSize, hasMore) Constructor empty(PageParam) An empty page; falls back to defaults when pageParam is null

The first three providers are snapshot-style read boundaries (full loading + refresh); SecurityProvider is the on-demand query boundary (six method groups). The two paradigms coexist, each with its own job. Naming get*/query*/pageQuery* maps to single/full/paged; roles are referenced by code, orgs by orgId; tenant and app are bound by the implementation. Full aggregation has a hard cap (MAX_AGGREGATE_SIZE) that throws instead of silently truncating; use paging overloads for large sets. The default implementation's resolution algorithms and assembly are documented in Platform Defaults.
Security Model — what the returned objects look like Loading Abstractions — where snapshots come from Platform Defaults — out-of-the-box implementations and replacement options

This page documents the three snapshot classes (OrgSnapshot/UserSnapshot/RoleSnapshot) — their index structures and immutability guarantees — plus the unified loading and refresh chain. Snapshots are produced by the loader SPI and cached behind providers; they are the foundation of the lock-free read side.

Snapshot Index structure Produced by OrgSnapshot orgById OrgSnapshotLoader.load() UserSnapshot userById + a two-level userByExtendType index UserSnapshotLoader.load(enricher) RoleSnapshot roleById + roleByCode + orgRolesByOrgId RoleSnapshotLoader.load() All three snapshots are final classes with private constructors; the only entry is the static from(...) factory. Query methods are package-private — snapshots are never exposed directly; they are always surfaced through providers.

Member Meaning orgById Org ID → Org index from(Map<String, Org>) Static factory: copies into a LinkedHashMap (preserving load order) and wraps it with Collections.unmodifiableMap EMPTY Empty-snapshot singleton, the provider's initial state getOrg(String orgId) Package-private lookup, null when absent

Member Meaning userById User ID → User index userByExtendType Two-level extended-identity index: type → extendKey → User; type is one of the three extended keys loginName/weixinUnionId/weixinWorkUserId from(Map, Map) Static factory: both the outer map and every inner map are wrapped immutably (deep immutability) EMPTY Empty-snapshot singleton getUser(String userId) Package-private lookup getUserByExtendKey(String type, String extendKey) Package-private lookup: fetch the pool for type, then the user by key; null when the pool is absent The two-level index directly supports extended-key authentication (WeChat login, WeCom login): UserProvider.getUserByExtendKey normalizes type and lands on this index.

Member Meaning roleById Role ID → Role index roleByCode Role code → Role index, built by from() from roleById; duplicate codes resolve putIfAbsent-style — first wins, never overwritten orgRolesByOrgId Org ID → List<OrgRole> index (roles attached to the department); every list is made immutable via List.copyOf EMPTY Empty-snapshot singleton getRole(String roleId) / getRoleByCode(String roleCode) Package-private lookups getOrgRoles(String orgId) Package-private lookup, an empty list when absent

final + private constructor + immutable wrapping: once published, a snapshot's contents never change; from() performs the copy and wrapping before publication. Load as a whole, swap atomically: providers hold the snapshot in an AtomicReference; refresh() builds the new snapshot and replaces the reference in one step. The read side is lock-free, and every read sees a complete snapshot — never a half-new, half-old mix. Each query takes the current reference: every provider method first reads snapshotRef.get() and then queries, which aligns naturally with refresh semantics; BridgeSecurityProvider keeps no cache of its own for the same reason.

The unified loading and cascading-refresh coordinator for the three snapshots, living in the framework defaults (geelato-core). Method Semantics init() (@PostConstruct) Runs refreshAll() at startup, completing the first load refreshAll() orgProvider.refresh() → userProvider.refresh() → role snapshot refresh refreshOrg() Refreshes the org snapshot and cascades a user snapshot refresh (org changes affect the user's derived fields: company / department / BU) refreshUser() Refreshes only the user snapshot refreshRole() Refreshes only the role snapshot Key points: All refresh methods are synchronized, preventing interleaved concurrent refreshes. UserProvider/RoleProvider may be absent (@Autowired(required = false), when a direct-lookup implementation manages its own data plane); absent providers are skipped. Runtime trigger points: after directory changes, platform controllers call OrgController.refreshOrg() and UserController.refreshUser() (see the assembly table in Platform Defaults).

The three snapshots are immutable index containers: org has a single index, user has two (including the extended-identity two-level index), role has three (ID / code / org attachments). Immutability + atomic replacement make the read side lock-free: the loading thread publishes only after the build completes, and every read sees a fully consistent snapshot. SecurityDataRefreshCoordinator unifies refresh: full load at startup, org changes cascade to users, and user/role can refresh independently.

This page explains the main configuration entry of geelato-web-quickstart, the per-module property files, and the key settings of each module. The main file is: geelato-web-quickstart/src/main/resources/application.properties The module directory is: geelato-web-quickstart/src/main/resources/properties/

The current model is: one main file for global bootstrap and shared runtime settings one property file per module capability a unified import chain through spring.config.import The current import order is: workflow.properties seata.properties oss.properties package.properties sc.properties auth.properties market.properties message.properties weixin_work.properties elasticsearch.properties monitor.properties

The main file currently covers: server bootstrap such as server.port top-level feature switches such as geelato.web and geelato.schedule plugin directory and repository settings primary datasource configuration p6spy SQL logging settings multipart upload limits logging and metadata scan settings OCR, PDF, and AI service integration settings Redis and upload directory settings module property imports

The configuration heavily uses: ${ENV_NAME:defaultValue} This means: environment variables override first fallback defaults are kept for local startup That fits local development, container deployment, and multi-environment switching. The modules below are described in import order.
File: properties/seata.properties
This file carries reserved distributed transaction settings.
geelato.svcp seata.enabled seata.application-id seata.tx-service-group
Seata is not enabled by default use it only when distributed transaction behavior is explicitly required for deeper datasource customization, continue with ORM / Datasource Extension
File: properties/oss.properties
This file holds Aliyun OSS access settings.
geelato.oss.accessKeyId geelato.oss.accessKeySecret geelato.oss.endPoint geelato.oss.bucketName geelato.oss.region
inject secrets through environment variables keep bucket and region aligned with the actual OSS resources make sure upload capability has a fallback path if OSS is not configured
File: properties/package.properties
This file contains package and upload-path related settings.
geelato.package.env geelato.package.path geelato.package.uploadFolder
override paths according to the real deployment machine keep temporary upload folders separate from final package output folders
File: properties/sc.properties
This file carries the SC feature switch and site path settings.
geelato.sc geelato.sc.folder geelato.sc.path
keep the folder aligned with the real deployment filesystem prefer environment-variable override instead of hard-coded machine paths
File: properties/auth.properties
This file contains: OAuth2 client settings WeChat-related application settings sa-token basics
geelato.oauth2.* geelato.wx.* sa-token.*

keep OAuth2 client secrets and WeChat secrets in environment variables align the OAuth2 URL with the deployed unified authentication center combine this page with Authentication and Authorization to understand how runtime backend auth consumes these credentials
File: properties/market.properties
This file contains the Market module datasource and debug logging settings.
spring.datasource.market.* spring.datasource.market.hikari.* logging.level.cn.geelato.market logging.level.cn.geelato.orm logging.level.org.springframework.jdbc
set GEELATO_MARKET_JDBCURL explicitly when Market uses a dedicated database avoid keeping DEBUG logging enabled in production for long periods
File: properties/message.properties
This file contains: message scheduling settings message datasource settings RabbitMQ connection settings
geelato.message.schedule.* spring.datasource.message.* spring.datasource.message.hikari.* spring.rabbitmq.*

set GEELATO_MESSAGE_JDBCURL explicitly when the message module uses its own database replace the default RabbitMQ guest credentials in production tune processing interval and batch size according to throughput needs
File: properties/weixin_work.properties
This file contains server-side signature validation settings for Weixin Work.
wework.validate.token wework.validate.aeskey wework.validate.corpid
keep these values aligned with the Weixin Work admin console inject them through environment variables in production do not confuse them with the generic WeChat settings in auth.properties
File: properties/elasticsearch.properties
This file contains Elasticsearch connection settings.
geelato.es.url geelato.es.username geelato.es.password
keep credentials out of source defaults in production review debug-related properties in the main config before enabling verbose logs avoid accidental extra spaces in URLs
File: properties/monitor.properties
This file contains auxiliary suite monitoring settings.

geelato.monitor.auxiliary-suites.enabled geelato.monitor.auxiliary-suites.poll-interval-seconds geelato.monitor.auxiliary-suites.connect-timeout-seconds geelato.monitor.auxiliary-suites.read-timeout-seconds geelato.monitor.auxiliary-suites.suites-json
tune polling frequency according to the number of monitored targets keep suites-json readable and maintainable use stable health endpoints for external targets

Each file under properties/ represents one focused capability area. The practical reading rule is: use application.properties to understand the global runtime entry use one module file to understand one dedicated subsystem Examples: auth.properties for authentication-related settings message.properties for message scheduling and RabbitMQ workflow.properties for workflow datasource and engine settings oss.properties for object storage
documents.s: How To Read Module Property Files

documents.t: keep application.properties focused on global bootstrap and shared runtime settings keep module-specific settings inside properties/*.properties prefer environment variables for environment differences keep secrets out of source defaults whenever possible

This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, the APIs for saving, querying, versioning, publishing and locking process definitions. The data model (nodes / flows / properties) is described in Workflow Orchestration; version and publish status semantics in Workflow Orchestration · Versions and Status.

All APIs use the unified /api prefix and respond with: { "code": 200, "status": "success", "msg": "success", "data": "..." } Field Description code Business code: 200 success; 400 parameter/data problem; 403 no permission; 4090 edit-lock conflict; 4091 definition content conflict (optimistic lock) status success / fail msg Message data Business data, see each API Paginated responses carry data as: { "page": 1, "pageSize": 10, "total": 42, "data": [ "..." ] } Authentication (local login / OAuth2 / auth-client contract): see Geelato AuthServer.

Saves a process definition version. On create the definition key and the first version are generated; updates are only allowed on versions in design or debug status. Input (JSON body): Field Type Required Description id string Required on update Definition version id; empty on create defineKey string Required on update Unique definition identifier; empty on create name string Yes Process name remark string No Remark appId string Yes Owning application id defineGroup string No Process group pageId string No Bound form page id source object No Designer layout raw data (stored as-is) workflowNodes array Yes Node list, see Process Nodes; must contain start and end nodes sequenceFlows array Yes Flow list, see Sequence Flows; at least one lockVersion int No Optimistic-lock baseline: pass back the value from the detail API; a mismatch fails the save (4091); omit to skip baseline validation Output (data): Field Description id Definition version id defineKey Unique definition identifier version Version number status Status after save (design or debug) lockVersion Latest optimistic-lock version; pass back on the next save createAt / updateAt Creation / update time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss) Request example: { "defineKey": "leave_apply", "name": "Leave Application", "appId": "1001", "pageId": "leave_form_page", "lockVersion": 3, "workflowNodes": [ { "id": "start_1", "name": "Start", "nodeType": "start", "properties": [] }, { "id": "audit_1", "name": "Manager Approval", "nodeType": "audit", "properties": [ { "name": "assignee", "value": [{ "assignType": "role", "assignObject": "dept_manager" }] } ] }, { "id": "end_1", "name": "End", "nodeType": "end", "properties": [] } ], "sequenceFlows": [ { "id": "flow_1", "sourceRef": "start_1", "targetRef": "audit_1", "isAgree": 1 }, { "id": "flow_2", "sourceRef": "audit_1", "targetRef": "end_1", "isAgree": 1 } ] } Rules: Published (activated) or history (history) versions cannot be modified directly; create a new draft via Create Draft Version first. Updates take a row-level lock on the definition key to serialize against publish/draft creation. The current user needs the edit action on the definition (action bitmask, see Page-Query Definitions). Errors: 400 data not found / published version cannot be modified directly; 4091 definition modified by someone else, reload and retry.

Page-queries process definitions; each row summarizes the definition's latest version. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description keyword string No Unified keyword, fuzzy-matches name and defineKey name string No Name fuzzy match (legacy parameter) appId string No Filter by owning application status string No Publish status: published / unpublished defineGroup string No Single group (legacy parameter) defineGroups string No Multiple groups comma-separated; takes precedence over defineGroup statusList string No Version statuses comma-separated: design / debug / activated / history updateTimeFrom / updateTimeTo string No Update time range (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, inclusive) lockState string No Edit-lock state: locked / mine / others / unlocked sortBy string No Sort field (server-side whitelist) sortOrder string No asc / desc page / pageSize int No Paging, default 1 / 10 Output (data.data[], one row per definition): Field Description id Current (latest) version id defineKey Unique definition identifier name Process name version Current version number status Current version status: design / debug / activated / history publishStatus Publish status: published (a published version exists) / unpublished latestPublishedVersion Latest published version number, empty when unpublished defineGroup Process group updateTime Update time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss) actions Current user's action bitmask on this definition: view=1 / edit=2 / publish=4 / grant=8, OR-ed (e.g. 7 = view+edit+publish) lockOwnerName Current editor name, empty when unlocked lockRemainMinutes Longest remaining edit-lock minutes, empty when unlocked Response example: { "code": 200, "status": "success", "msg": "success", "data": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 10, "total": 2, "data": [ { "id": "1932048000000000001", "defineKey": "leave_apply", "name": "Leave Application", "version": "3", "status": "design", "publishStatus": "published", "latestPublishedVersion": "2", "defineGroup": "HR", "updateTime": "2026-11-10 15:30:00", "actions": 7, "lockOwnerName": "Alice", "lockRemainMinutes": 28 } ] } }

Lists all versions under one definition key. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Unique definition identifier Output (data[]): rows in the same shape as Page-Query Definitions.

Returns the full content of a definition version (nodes, flows and layout). Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Definition version id Output (data): same shape as the Save Definition Version input, plus system fields: version, status, deploymentId, deployAt, deployer, deployerName, lockVersion. Designers fetch this first and pass back id, defineKey, lockVersion when saving.

Lists the definition groups visible to the current user (for list-page group filtering). Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description appId string No Filter by application; empty for all Output (data[]): group name strings, e.g. ["HR", "Finance"].

Lightweight definition options for list filtering, one row per defineKey (current version info); same authorization scope as the list — non-admins only see definitions they can view. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description appId string No Filter by application keyword string No Fuzzy match on name/defineKey Output (data[]): Field Description defineKey Unique definition identifier name Process name defineGroup Process group

Creates or reuses an editable draft version (called when clicking "Edit" on the definition list). Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Source version id (the version currently shown in the list) Output (data): Field Description id Draft version id defineKey Unique definition identifier version Version number (+1 when the source is published; unchanged when it is already a draft/debug) status design Version strategy: Source version is already design or debug: returns that version directly, no new version. Source version is published: copies it into a new draft (version +1). Leftover draft/debug versions are retired to history, so a definition has at most one editable version.

Publishes a draft version as the activated version; once deployed to the engine it can be run by the formal start APIs. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Definition version id (must be in design or debug status) Output (data): deployment id string. Rules: The previously activated version automatically becomes history; one definition keeps exactly one activated version. Other draft/debug versions are retired to history. Publishing is rejected while someone else is editing (4090); a successful publish releases the current user's own edit lock. The current user needs the publish action. Errors: 400 data not found / non-design-or-debug status cannot publish; 403 no publish permission; 4090 definition is being edited by someone else.

Publishes a draft version as a debug version (debug), runnable only by the debug start APIs for pre-release validation. Input/Output: same as Publish Definition. Rules: only design versions can be debug-published; debug publish requires the edit action (same level as save); debug versions do not affect the running activated version.

Batch-deploys all pending definitions, for environment migration. No input. Output (data): deployment result description string. Rules: the migration scenario skips status and edit-lock checks and deploys definitions one by one.

Deletes an entire definition (all versions under the defineKey). Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Unique definition identifier Output (data): number of rows deleted.
Deletes a single definition version. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Definition version id Output (data): number of rows deleted.

Converts definition JSON into BPMN 2.0 XML (not persisted; for preview or export). Input (JSON body): the definition structure; conversion uses its workflowNodes, sequenceFlows, defineKey, name, remark fields. Output (data): BPMN XML string.
Converts BPMN XML back into definition JSON (not persisted). The request body is the raw BPMN XML string. Output (data): definition JSON, containing only workflowNodes and sequenceFlows.
Returns the deployed BPMN XML of a definition version. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description id string Yes Definition version id Output (data): BPMN XML string.

Returns the button metadata supported by the system; designers render configurable buttons from it. No input. Output (data[]): Field Description name Button identifier (e.g. wf_btn_agree) text Default text defaultSave Default form save policy: 0 no / 1 save / 2 confirm nodeDefaultEnabled Default visibility per node type: {"audit": 1, "handle": 0, ...} level Button level: primary / special / secondary The full button set and defaults: Workflow Orchestration · Button Reference.

While a definition is being edited, an edit lock prevents concurrent modification. The lock cooperates with save and publish concurrency control: when someone else holds the lock, save/publish is rejected (4090) and the response returns the holder info.

Acquires the edit lock. Input (query or form): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Unique definition identifier Output (data): Field Description lockToken Lock token; pass back on renew/release defineKey Unique definition identifier ownerName Holder name (used for prompting when locked by someone else) expiresAt Expiry time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss) remainingMinutes Remaining validity (minutes) Error: 4090 definition is being edited by someone else (response includes holder and remaining time).

Renews the edit lock; the front end should heartbeat every 5 minutes. Input (query or form): defineKey (string, required), lockToken (string, required). Output (data): renewed expiry info, same shape as acquire.
Releases the edit lock (on leaving the editor or after a successful publish). Input (query or form): defineKey (string, required), lockToken (string, required). Output: no business data.

This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, the APIs scoped to the current logged-in user: my pending tasks, done tasks, to-read, read, processes started by me, opinion phrases and circulation. The data scope is automatically the current user — no user parameter is needed (or accepted).

APIs use the unified /api prefix; response and pagination shapes are documented in Define Integration · Common Conventions. All page queries support a unified keyword (keyword), server-side sorting (sortBy whitelist / sortOrder only asc / desc) and paging (page default 1, pageSize default 10). Time parameters use yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss; ranges are inclusive.

Pending / done task entry: Field Description id Task id (use as taskId in the handling APIs) procInstId Process instance id procInstName Instance name (【Definition Name】Business Name) procDefName Process definition name taskDefId Task definition id (node id) taskName Task name formRecordId Business record id (businessKey) description Task description assigneeId / assigneeName Handler id / name (the current user) ownerId / ownerName Initiator id / name createTime Instance start time arriveTime Time the task arrived at the current node finishTime Task completion time (done list only)

To-read / read entry: Field Description id To-read record id (use as id in the complete APIs) procInstId / procInstName Process instance id / name procDefName Process definition name taskId Related process task id formRecordId Business record id recipientId / recipientName Recipient id / name (the current user) senderId / senderName Sender id / name comment Circulation comment receiveTime Receive time (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss) readAt Read time (read list only)

Lists all pending tasks of the current user (no paging). Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description appId string No Filter by definition's application; empty for all Output (data[]): MyTask list.

Page-queries the current user's pending tasks. This page documents, endpoint by endpoint, all runtime APIs: process start, next-step and participant resolution, task submission and handling, instance/task queries, instance management and reminding. The behavioral semantics (when to call what, how resolution works) are described in Workflow Runtime.

All APIs use the unified /api prefix and the {code, status, msg, data} response (see Define Integration · Common Conventions). Paginated responses carry data as {page, pageSize, total, data[]}. Key business codes: 400 task not found / instance not exist / parameter error; 403 no permission; 409 the task has been processed, refresh and retry (concurrent submission); 4031 no permission to view the process instance (insufficient data permission; front ends show a unified block).

Instance status (status): Value Description running In progress completed Completed (reached the end node normally) terminated Terminated (force-ended) Trace action types (actionType): Value Description INITIATE Start SUBMIT Submit WITHDRAW Withdraw TRANSFER Transfer TERMINATE / FORCE_END Terminate / force end DELETE Delete CIRCULATE Circulate REMIND Remind CANCEL Cancelled sibling tasks after a countersign denial

The core structure of next-step / submit routing; it appears in the queryNextStep* responses and the runWorkflow input: Field Description stepName Step name (e.g. "Submit") stepTargetName Target node name targetRef Target node id, passed back as-is at submit stepUserList Candidate handlers (StepUser); passed back at submit, may be trimmed to assigneeLimit isAgree Whether the step's flow is an agree line: 1 agree, 0 deny assigneeLimit Handler count limit of the target node (0 unlimited) subStepList Parallel sub-steps (one entry per branch on parallel fork; same structure) routeTargetRefs Route target id chain (includes traversed gateway/automatic nodes); passed back as-is at submit pathText Path text (flow names, or current->next1->next2... when names are missing) needAssignee Whether handlers must be picked: true for user tasks; false for end nodes / parallel joins (submit directly)
Handler entry: Field Description userId User id userName User name enName English name orgId / orgName Department id / name

POST /api/engine/startWorkflow​ Starts an instance from the activated version; the instance stays on the initiate node and a draft pending task is created for the initiator. Input (JSON body): Field Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Process definition key bizId string Yes Business id (stored as the instance businessKey for lookup) bizName string Yes Business name (instance name is 【Definition Name】Business Name) formData object No Business form data, written into process variables for condition evaluation and form echo attachIds string[] No Attachment ids uploaded at start, bound to the start action record Output (data): WorkflowInstance; currentWorkflowTasks holds the initiate-node task. Request example: { "defineKey": "leave_apply", "bizId": "LV202611150001", "bizName": "Alice's leave request", "formData": { "days": 3, "reason": "annual leave" } } Response example: { "code": 200, "status": "success", "msg": "success", "data": { "procId": "5001", "procName": "【Leave Application】Alice's leave request", "defineKey": "leave_apply", "bizId": "LV202611150001", "bizName": "Alice's leave request", "status": "running", "startUserId": "u_1001", "startUserName": "Alice", "createTime": "2026-11-15 10:00:00", "finishTime": null, "currentWorkflowTasks": [ { "procId": "5001", "taskId": "6001", "taskName": "Apply", "userId": "u_1001", "userName": "Alice", "fromTask": null } ] } } Errors: 400 definition not found or not published (no activated version).

Input (JSON body): the Start Process input plus: Field Type Required Description selectStepList array Yes Next-step selection (NextStep array), from queryNextStepPrediction / queryNextStep comment string No Initiate-node comment, written into the operation record Output (data): WorkflowInstance; currentWorkflowTasks holds the tasks after the flow.
POST /api/engine/startDebugWorkflow​ Starts an instance from the debug (debug) version; behavior, input and output match Start Process. Returns 400 when the definition has no debug version.
POST /api/engine/startDebugWorkflowAtomicity​ Starts and submits from the debug version; matches Start and Submit.

GET|POST /api/engine/queryNextStep​ Resolves the reachable next nodes and candidate handlers for a running instance's task. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description procId string Yes Process instance id taskId string Yes Process task id isAgree int No Filter outgoing flows by conclusion: 1 agree lines only, 0 deny lines only; omit for all Output (data[]): NextStep list. On a parallel fork each branch is returned as targetRef + subStepList. Errors: 400 process instance not found / task not found.

GET|POST /api/engine/queryNextStepPrediction​ Before the process is started, predicts the first stop after the initiate submission, by definition. Input (query + body): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Process definition key debug boolean No Predict by the debug version, default false formData object No Draft form data (JSON body) for condition-line evaluation; may be empty Output (data[]): NextStep list.

GET|POST /api/engine/queryStepUser​ Resolves candidate handlers of a target node on a running instance. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description procId string Yes Process instance id targetRef string Yes Target node id Output (data[]): StepUser list.

GET|POST /api/engine/queryStepUserPrediction​ Before the process is started, predicts candidate handlers of a node, by definition. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Process definition key targetRef string Yes Target node id debug boolean No Resolve by the debug version, default false Output (data[]): StepUser list.

GET|POST /api/engine/getDefineFormPageUrl​ Returns the form page url bound to the definition, for loading the business form in an iframe before starting. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description defineKey string Yes Process definition key debug boolean No Resolve by the debug version, default false Output (data): form page url string (computed from the definition pageId and the default form url config, template like http://host/{pageId}?bizId={bizId}).

POST /api/engine/runWorkflow​ Submits the current task and drives the flow — the unified entry for approval / handling / initiate submission. Input (JSON body): Field Type Required Description procId string Yes Process instance id taskId string Yes Current task id (must be the current user's pending task) selectStepList array Yes Next-step selection (NextStep array); pass back targetRef, stepUserList, routeTargetRefs, subStepList from the resolution APIs; stepUserList may be empty when the target needs no picking comment string No Approval comment, written into the operation record attachIds string[] No Attachment ids bound to this submission Output (data): "The Workflow Operate Success!". Request example: { "procId": "5001", "taskId": "6001", "comment": "Agreed, please follow the policy", "selectStepList": [ { "stepName": "Submit", "stepTargetName": "Manager Approval", "targetRef": "audit_1", "isAgree": 1, "assigneeLimit": 1, "needAssignee": true, "stepUserList": [ { "userId": "u_2001", "userName": "Bob", "orgId": "o_10", "orgName": "Engineering" } ] } ] } Rules: The task must belong to the current user and not be suspended, otherwise 400/403. Countersign: when one person votes deny (selectStepList contains isAgree=0), sibling pending tasks of the same node are cancelled and the deny line is followed. Concurrent submissions of the same task are retried inside the transaction; after exhausting retries the engine returns 409 The task has been processed, please refresh and retry. When the target node has no explicitly picked users, the engine resolves participants from the node assignee config; on an empty result the node's emptyAssigneeStrategy applies (see Workflow Orchestration · Empty Participant Strategy).

POST /api/engine/withdraw​ The initiator withdraws a sent-out process; the process returns to the initiator's pending list. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description procId string Yes Process instance id taskId string Yes Task id to withdraw (take withdrawTaskId from the instance detail) comment string Yes Withdrawal reason, written into the operation record Output (data): result description string. Rules: only completed tasks with no later node processing record can be withdrawn; the instance detail's withdrawable is the visibility flag.

POST /api/engine/rejectToLastStep​ Returns the process to the previous processing node. Input (query): procId (string, required), taskId (string, required, current task id), comment (string, required). Output (data): result description string.

POST /api/engine/rejectToStart​ Returns the process to the initiate node; the initiator edits and resubmits. Input (query): same as Reject to Previous Step (procId, taskId, comment). Output (data): result description string.

POST /api/engine/rejectToNode​ Returns the process to any specified node. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description procId string Yes Process instance id taskId string Yes Current task id targetNodeId string Yes Target node id to return to comment string Yes Reject comment Output (data): result description string.

POST /api/engine/transferTask​ Hands the own pending task to another user. Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description taskId string Yes Task id userId string Yes Target user id comment string No Transfer comment Output (data): result description string.
GET /api/engine/getCurrentTask​ Lists all active tasks of an instance. Input (query): procId (string, required). Output (data[]): TaskInfoVo list.

Output (data): WorkflowInstance. Error: 4031 no permission to view the process instance (insufficient data permission).
GET /api/engine/getProcTask​ Lists all tasks of an instance (with handler info). Input (query): procId (string, required). Output (data[]): WorkflowTask list.

Input (query): Parameter Type Required Description keyword string No Unified keyword (instance name / definition name fuzzy match) name string No Name fuzzy match (legacy parameter) status string No Instance status: running / completed / terminated statusList string No Statuses comma-separated (e.g. completed,terminated); takes precedence over status appId string No Filter by definition's application procDefKeys string No Process types (definition keys), comma-separated startUserId string No Filter by initiator startTimeFrom / startTimeTo string No Start time range (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss, inclusive) finishTimeFrom / finishTimeTo string No Finish time range currentAssigneeId string No Current handler id (running instances) currentTaskDefKey string No Current node id (running instances) sortBy / sortOrder string No Sort field (server-side whitelist) / direction asc / desc page / pageSize int No Paging, default 1 / 10 Output (data): PageResult; data[] holds ProcInstListVo rows.

GET /api/engine/getProcessTrace​ Returns node-level operation records of an instance (data source of the process timeline). Input (query): procId (string, required). Output (data[]): ActivityTraceVO list. Error: 400 history not exist (instance has no history).

GET /api/engine/getProcBpmn​ Returns the BPMN XML of the instance's definition, for read-only process diagram rendering; finished instances are served from history. Input (query): procId (string, required). Output (data): BPMN XML string.

GET /api/engine/getProcFormData​ Looks up process variables (form data) by business id. :::warning For testing only Form data should normally be provided by the business system per bizId; this API is kept for integration demos. ::: Input (query): bizId (string, required). Output (data): process variable key-value object.

POST /api/engine/forceEndProcInstance​ Force-terminates a running instance; all unfinished tasks are terminated and the instance becomes terminated. Input (query): procId (string, required), comment (string, optional). Output (data): result description string.

Workflow Runtime: behaviors and the end-to-end sequence behind these APIs My Process Integration: pending/done/to-read/read queries Define Integration: definition save and publish APIs

This page describes the core model of geelato-workflow process design: process nodes, sequence flows, participants, process properties and node properties. The designer produces a JSON process definition; on save the workflow service converts it into standard BPMN 2.0 and deploys it to the engine. Integrators only need the business model and fields described here — no BPMN knowledge required. For definition save/publish/version APIs see Define Integration; for runtime behavior see Workflow Runtime.

A process definition consists of three parts: Part Description Process nodes (workflowNodes) Node list; must contain a start node and an end node Sequence flows (sequenceFlows) Connections between nodes, at least one; they decide the routing Process properties Definition-level info: identifiers, name, group, form page, version status { "defineKey": "leave_apply", "name": "Leave Application", "appId": "1001", "defineGroup": "HR", "pageId": "leave_form_page", "workflowNodes": [ { "id": "start_1", "name": "Start", "nodeType": "start", "properties": [] }, { "id": "initiate_1", "name": "Apply", "nodeType": "initiate", "properties": [] }, { "id": "audit_1", "name": "Manager Approval", "nodeType": "audit", "properties": [ { "name": "assignee", "value": [{ "assignType": "role", "assignObject": "dept_manager" }] }, { "name": "auditType", "value": "any" } ] }, { "id": "end_1", "name": "End", "nodeType": "end", "properties": [] } ], "sequenceFlows": [ { "id": "flow_1", "sourceRef": "start_1", "targetRef": "initiate_1", "isAgree": 1 }, { "id": "flow_2", "name": "Agree", "sourceRef": "initiate_1", "targetRef": "audit_1", "isAgree": 1 }, { "id": "flow_3", "name": "Pass", "sourceRef": "audit_1", "targetRef": "end_1", "isAgree": 1 } ] }

A node is a processing step in the process. Each node has these fields: Field Type Description id string Node identifier, unique within the definition; sequence flows reference nodes by it name string Node name (2-50 characters) nodeType string Node type, see table below properties array Node property list ({name, value} pairs), see Process Node Properties x / y / width / height number Canvas layout (persisted by the designer, may be empty)

Type Name Behavior start Start Virtual node; the process entry. Exactly one per definition end End Virtual node; the process exit. Reaching it completes the process normally initiate Initiate First node reached after the process starts; the initiator is bound as handler and a draft pending task is created audit Audit Approver gives an agree/deny conclusion; executed as parallel multi-instance, multiple approvers judged by the completion rule handle Handle Handling user task; with a configured participant the handler is resolved at runtime, otherwise any user with permission may handle it notice Notice Automatic: sends notifications per node config and flows on; produces no pending task service Service Automatic: runs a script or HTTP call and flows on; produces no pending task exclusiveGateway Exclusive gateway Picks one outgoing flow by condition evaluation parallelGateway Parallel gateway Forks multiple branches; at join, waits for all branches hq Countersign Multi-person parallel voting approval node; node conclusion judged by completion rule and reject strategy countersignStart / countersignEnd Countersign start/end (legacy) Legacy countersign model, kept for backward compatibility only; use hq for new definitions :::note Fallback for automatic nodes When a notice or service node fails, the engine automatically creates a manual fallback task (handler = initiator). The handler can choose re-run (loop back and re-run the failed node) or skip (skip the failed node and flow to its original downstream). :::

A sequence flow connects two nodes and decides the routing: Field Type Description id string Flow identifier name string Flow name (e.g. "Agree" / "Deny"; shown in next-step selection and path text) sourceRef string Source node id targetRef string Target node id conditionExpression string Condition expression evaluated against form data / process variables; exclusive gateway outgoing flows must have one isAgree int Whether this is an agree-type flow: 1 agree line, 0 deny line Routing rules: Agree / deny lines: when submitting from an audit or countersign node, outgoing flows are filtered by the conclusion (isAgree) — agree follows isAgree=1 lines, deny follows isAgree=0 lines. Condition lines: conditionExpression is evaluated against process variables (including form data); typical use is an exclusive gateway with multiple outgoing flows selected by business data. Default routing: flows without a condition, or with a true condition, participate in routing. If no exclusive gateway condition matches, the process errors — conditions should be complete at design time. Parallel routing: after a parallel gateway fork, all outgoing flows take effect; at join, all branches must arrive.
User task nodes (audit / handle / hq) configure participants via the assignee property; multiple entries can be combined.

Field Description assignType Participant type: user specified users, role roles, dept departments, dept_role dept-role (orgId:roleId), initiator the initiator assignObject Participant identifiers, multiple values comma-separated (user ids or role ids) withChild Include sub-departments; only effective for assignType=dept Runtime semantics per type: assignType assignObject meaning Resolution user User id list The specified users role Role id list All users under the roles dept Department id list All users in the departments; withChild=true includes sub-departments dept_role deptId:roleId list Users in the department holding the role initiator Not needed The process initiator (used as fallback handler for automatic nodes and notice recipients)

Pick at submit: before submitting, resolve candidate handlers (StepUser) via the next-step and participant resolution APIs and let the submitter confirm; whether the target node requires picking is marked by needAssignee. Fallback resolution: at submit time, for audit/countersign target nodes without explicitly picked users, the engine resolves participants from the node assignee config; when the result is empty the node's emptyAssigneeStrategy applies (see Empty Participant Strategy).
assigneeLimit caps the number of participants: 0 unlimited, positive integer N at most N people. When resolved candidates exceed the limit, the submitter must trim before submitting.

emptyAssigneeStrategy decides the behavior when no participant can be resolved for the target node: Value Behavior initiator Default. The process initiator acts as handler, avoiding a stuck process skip The node is reached with an empty participant set, completes immediately and flows on error Submission fails with an error saying the node has no configured approver

Process properties are definition-level info saved with the definition JSON: Field Required Description defineKey Required on update Unique definition identifier (generated on first create); versions evolve under the same key name Yes Process name remark No Remark appId Yes Owning application id, used to filter definitions and tasks by application defineGroup No Process group (for list filtering) pageId No Bound form page id; start/handle pages load the business form (iframe) from it source No Designer layout raw data (maintained by the front end) lockVersion No Optimistic-lock baseline; validated on save to detect concurrent edits

Definitions evolve by version under the same defineKey. Version status: Status Description design Draft: editable, not deployed to the engine debug Debug: produced by debug deploy; runnable only by debug-start APIs, for pre-release validation activated Activated: published; formal start APIs run this version history History: superseded by a newer publication; running instances keep executing the original version Deploy actions (publish, debug deploy, batch deploy) and edit locks are documented in Define Integration.
Node properties are {name, value} pairs in the node properties array, distinguished by name. The full set:

name Applies to value values / structure Default auditType audit / hq any any one approval passes the node; all all must approve. deptStep (department cascade) and roleStep (role cascade) are reserved values, rejected at deploy time in the current version all assignee audit / handle / hq / notice Assignee config array, see Participants Unset: handle node is handled by any user with permission assigneeLimit audit / handle / hq 0 unlimited; positive integer N caps at N people 0 page All user task nodes Node-level form page id, overrides definition-level pageId Falls back to definition pageId batchSubmit audit / handle Batch submit configuration —

name Applies to value values / structure Default button All user task nodes {buttonId: {enabled, text, save}}. enabled 0 hide/1 show; text button text; save form save policy 0 no/1 save/2 confirm See Button Reference opinion audit / handle / hq {enabled, required, signature}: opinion box visibility, required, handwritten signature, all 0/1 enabled=1, others 0 attachment All user task nodes {upload, type, download, delete}: upload permission 0/1, allowed types (comma-separated), download permission 0/1, delete permission 0 forbidden/1 own items/2 all — ccEnabled audit / handle / hq CC switch 0/1 0 ccAssignee when ccEnabled=1 CC recipient config array, same structure as assignee config —

Countersign nodes run as parallel multi-instance: multiple people hold pending tasks simultaneously, and the node conclusion is judged by completion rule and reject strategy: name value values Default completionRule all all must agree; any any one agree; ratio by percentage (with completionValue as the numerator, positive integer); count by votes (with completionValue as vote threshold, positive integer) all completionValue Numerator for ratio (e.g. 60 means 60%) or vote threshold for count — rejectStrategy veto_any any single denial rolls back; vote_all collect all votes then judge veto_any emptyAssigneeStrategy initiator / skip / error, see Empty Participant Strategy initiator :::note auditType vs completionRule auditType=any/all is the simplified form of the approval mode, internally mapped to completion rules any/all; an explicit completionRule takes precedence over auditType. Use completionRule + completionValue for ratio- or vote-based control. :::

Grouped countersign splits participants into groups; each group participates in the countersign as one opinion body: name value values Default groupSource dept group by department (incl. sub-departments); role group by role; custom explicit groups (with groups); empty = no grouping, plain countersign empty groupInnerRule all group agrees only when all members agree; any one agreeing member makes the group agree all countingUnit member count by person; group count by group (completion rule counts group conclusions) member groupKeyName Group name display template (e.g. {dept} Countersign) — groups Explicit groups when groupSource=custom: [{key, name, members: [userId]}] — Empty groups are skipped automatically (marked skipped) and excluded from group-level counting; when all groups are empty, emptyAssigneeStrategy applies. Countersign progress (incl. group progress) is queried via the instance detail / countersign progress APIs, see Runtime Integration · Common Response Structures.

name Description noticeConfig Node notification config: template, recipients, etc.; the engine sends notifications on node arrival/completion async Whether the automatic node runs asynchronously: true async (requires the async executor); synchronous by default

geelato-workflow is an independently deployed workflow service built on the Activiti engine (7.1.0.M6), providing process definition, approval flow, circulation (to-read), attachments, notifications and process permissions. Business systems integrate via REST APIs; the service owns a dedicated workflow datasource plus a platform-database bridge. :::info Repository geelato-workflow is a standalone repository (geelato-workflow), not part of the geelato-community aggregate build. :::
