This page describes the full lifecycle of a process instance: start → resolution → operation → end, plus the actions available along the way: withdraw, reject, transfer, circulate and remind. The REST APIs for each action are documented in Runtime Integration and My Process Integration.
Three instance states apply throughout: running, completed (reached the end node normally) and terminated (force-ended).

Starting = attaching a business record to a published process definition. Three inputs are needed: the process definition (defineKey), the business id (bizId) and the business name (bizName). Standard start chain: Pick the process: GET /api/define/listDefineOptions lists the definitions that can be started in the current application. Load the draft form: GET /api/engine/getDefineFormPageUrl returns the form page bound to the definition; load it as an iframe and fill in the business form. Pre-start prediction (optional): POST /api/engine/queryNextStepPrediction predicts the first stop; GET /api/engine/queryStepUserPrediction predicts its candidate handlers. Start: POST /api/engine/startWorkflow with the definition key, business id/name and form data. Two outcomes after starting: API Behavior POST /api/engine/startWorkflow The instance stays on the initiate node and a draft pending task is created for the initiator; the initiator submits later via the run API POST /api/engine/startWorkflowAtomicity Start and submit: completes the initiate node's submission in the same call and flows to the next node (requires selectStepList) Both share the same inputs (the atomic variant adds selectStepList and an optional comment); both return the instance detail (WorkflowInstance, including instance id and current tasks). For validation use startDebugWorkflow / startDebugWorkflowAtomicity — identical except they run the debug version; the test data is persisted and can be deleted afterwards. :::note Instance name and business linkage The engine names the instance 【Definition Name】Business Name and stores bizId as the business key. Business systems can look up the instance by bizId; the workflow side can jump back to the business record via the instance's formRecordId. :::

"Resolution" is how the engine determines, at each submission, which nodes are reached next and who handles them. It happens on every submit (start-submit, approval submit) and is also available as prediction APIs before submitting. Resolution has two layers: Route resolution: pick the target from the current node's outgoing flows. Audit-type nodes filter by the conclusion (isAgree), exclusive gateways evaluate flow conditions, parallel gateways fork multiple branches. When the outgoing flow leads to a gateway or automatic node, the engine keeps traversing until it hits a user task that produces a pending task or the end node, and returns the full path via routeTargetRefs and pathText. Participant resolution: resolve handlers for the target node. Explicitly picked users (stepUserList) take precedence; otherwise participants are resolved from the node assignee config (user/role/dept/dept-role/initiator); when the result is empty, the node's emptyAssigneeStrategy applies. Countersign nodes are split into groups (by department/role/custom) that vote in parallel after resolution. The resolution result is a list of NextStep: each entry carries the target node (targetRef/stepTargetName), candidate handlers (stepUserList), whether picking is required (needAssignee), parallel sub-steps (subStepList) and more; the full structure is documented in Runtime Integration · NextStep. Related APIs: API When Description POST /api/engine/queryNextStepPrediction Before start Predicts the first stop by definition (form data can drive condition lines) GET /api/engine/queryNextStep Before submit Predicts the next steps of a running instance's task (filterable by conclusion) GET /api/engine/queryStepUserPrediction Before start Predicts candidate handlers of a node by definition GET /api/engine/queryStepUser Before submit Predicts candidate handlers of a target node on a running instance
While an instance is running, work revolves around pending tasks:

The handler gives a conclusion and sends the task on: GET /api/my/pageQueryMyPendingTask lists pending tasks; GET /api/engine/getTaskInfo loads the task detail (node info, form page url, whether next-step picking is required via needNextStep, countersign progress). GET /api/engine/queryNextStep + GET /api/engine/queryStepUser resolve and confirm the next step and handlers. POST /api/engine/runWorkflow submits: instance id, task id, next-step selection (selectStepList), comment and attachment ids. At submit time the engine: validates task ownership (must be the current user's pending task) → writes target participants → pre-sets grouped-countersign variables → fallback-resolves participants for unpicked nodes → records comment and attachment bindings → drives the flow → writes the operation record. If one person votes deny in a multi-instance node, sibling pending tasks of the same node are cancelled and the deny line is followed.

In a countersign node multiple people hold pending tasks in parallel: non-final submitters only record their opinion, without a next-step picker (needNextStep=false); when the completion rule (all/any/ratio/votes, incl. group rules) is satisfied, the last completed submission drives the node as a whole. Countersign progress is available via the instance detail countersignProgress or the task detail.

Action API Description Approval/handling submit POST /api/engine/runWorkflow The core submit action, see above Withdraw POST /api/engine/withdraw The initiator withdraws a sent-out process (available when no later node has processed it); the process returns to the initiator's pending list Reject to previous POST /api/engine/rejectToLastStep Returns to the previous processing node Reject to initiator POST /api/engine/rejectToStart Returns to the initiate node; the initiator edits and resubmits Reject to node POST /api/engine/rejectToNode Returns to any specified node in the process Transfer POST /api/engine/transferTask Hands the own pending task to another user Circulate POST /api/toRead/sendToRead Sends the instance to selected people for reading; creates their to-read items Remind GET /api/engine/remindTargets + POST /api/engine/remind The initiator sends a reminder to handlers of active tasks Attachment POST /api/attach/upload Uploads an attachment; its id is passed back at submit to bind it to the operation record Query instance detail / task detail / trace / instance BPMN See Runtime Integration

Ending Trigger Instance status Normal end Flow reaches the end node (end) completed, finish time recorded Force end POST /api/engine/forceEndProcInstance (admin/initiator) terminated, unfinished tasks are terminated Delete POST /api/engine/deleteProcInstance The instance and its tasks are deleted; business data is unaffected After completion the following remain queryable: instance detail (rendered from history), process trace (getProcessTrace), instance BPMN (getProcBpmn) and the completed-task list.
